ending: two consecutive rounds with no confirmed blocking or misleading finding, both gates green, frozen surface, self-inflicted under 25%

seatsSat: UX and information design — Orla, venue manager at The Orchard
rounds.headline: Six blocking and seven misleading, all closed. The spine — the one object that makes three products one application — had no working keyboard model: two products were still answering its keys and a hidden tile was in its rover. The seam promised in bold that only the picked words cross and sent the whole private note. The same couple carried two wedding days eleven weeks apart. None of it was visible in a frame.

confirmed.element: The seam · notes.seam → Send to Tasks → the created Tasks card (src/app.js, cross())
confirmed.problem: Notes states its handoff boundary twice on the sending screen — "Your note stays here. Tasks only ever receives the exact words you pick and check below." and "Tasks receives these words and nothing else from this note. The rest of what you wrote stays private here." — and the crossing sends the entire note body. Driven: peeling "Switch on before guests arrive, not when" from the heating note produces a Tasks card whose visible face reads "Heating: orchard room takes ~40 min to warm in October…" and whose accessible name reads the full 23-word note including "Note for the winter brochure couples." `cross()` sets `note: entry.body || ""`. The tag is set from the Notes subject too, so the card lands on the board tagged THE HOUSE beside cards tagged VENUE and BAR — a second vocabulary in one slot.
confirmed.consequence: The one promise the whole suite is built on is false in the only path that exercises it, and it is false in the direction that costs a person something: words Orla deliberately did not pick are published onto the shared board, on the card face, where a supplier or a colleague reads them. A person who trusted the sentence has already lost the thing it promised by the time they could notice.
confirmed.fix: In `cross()`, send only what the person checked: drop `note: entry.body` entirely (pass no note, or the empty string). If the card needs provenance, use a marker that carries no content — the existing `fromNote: true` already draws one. Map the Notes subject onto the board's own tag vocabulary through one translation, the way `laneIdFor` already translates a lane name, rather than importing "The house" onto a board that says "Venue".
confirmed.assertion: After driving the seam on notes.seam, the created Tasks card's textContent and its accessible name contain the picked wording and contain no word of the source note that was not inside the picked selection; and the card's tag is one of the board's own tag strings.
confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED, and it reproduces exactly as written. Driven at 1440 on `?v=paper&state=notes.seam`: clicking `.readBody .sent[data-i="1"]`, then `[data-act="send"]`, then the Tasks tile produces `.card[data-id="seam_n14_1"]` whose innerText is "Switch on before guests arrive, not when / Heating: orchard room takes ~40 min to warm in October… / THE HOUSE", with `

` and `#cd-seam_n14_1` reading that full body plus "The house." The sending screen prints both promises verbatim (fixture.js:609 `handoffBoundary`, fixture.js:625 `payload`) and the desk itself prints "LENGTH 23 words" beside them. `src/app.js:296` is `note: entry.body || ""`, and `entry` at notes.js:1107 is `{...note}`, so the whole body crosses. Two words on the finding: the full body is the accessible *description* (`aria-describedby`), not the accessible name (`aria-label` is the picked words) — imprecise, but a screen reader announces both, so the substance stands. The decisive evidence the finding did not use is that the artefact's own fixture already disagrees with `cross()`. Every `fromNote: true` card on this board carries a rewritten, condensed note, never the note body: n01's body is "Saturday wedding, Mara & Finn. Ceremony 2pm in the orchard, drinks on the terrace if it stays dry. Confirm marquee sides with the hire company by Thursday." while demo-t-01's note is "Mara & Finn, Saturday. Terrace plan if dry, marquee if not, they need the call by Thursday."; n09's body is the tonic/olives sentence pair while demo-t-06's note is "Two extra cases of tonic; last olive delivery was short." Tags likewise: n09 is `about: "the-house"` and demo-t-06 is tagged **Bar**, not "The house". So the three crossed cards the frames show and the one the seam makes live are different objects on the same board — a one-world break, in the same file that throws "ONE WORLD:" if the note→task join is inconsistent. `fixture.js` enforces the link and not the shape. Neither half restates a gate. `verify.mjs` seam block matches the landed card on `wording.slice(0,24)` (the title) and asserts only lane and presence; `interaction-check.mjs` contains no occurrence of "seam", "cardNote", "fromNote" or "tag". Nothing in the palette/weight/architecture lock is touched, and no lesson-library class covers it. Severity is right at misleading, not blocking: the seam does what it says mechanically — a card lands, `open-task` reveals it, undo removes it from both — but the surface asserts twice, in print, a boundary the code does not hold. Not a refinement either; a privacy sentence that is false is not taste. The fix is directionally correct and I am not refuting on it — dropping `note: entry.body` satisfies the promise and breaks nothing (the only consumers of `task.note` are tasks.js:328, :344, :348; `trayNote` at :636/:966 reads the *column's* note, not the task's), and `laneIdFor` is the right precedent for the tag. It is under-specified in two places, sharpened below.
confirmed.sharpenedFix:
Two corrections, both of which use a rule this artefact has already ratified.

1. Send the picked words, not nothing. "Tasks receives these words" is a promise to send *something* — and every fixture card that came from a note carries a note, so a seam card with none is a fourth shape on a board of three. Notes already owns the exact rule: `notes.js:1760` shows "The words you picked" as a separate fact only when `taskWording.trim() !== pickedWords.replace(/[.]$/, "")`. Mirror it. In `sendPeel` capture the pick beside the wording (`const wording = taskWording.trim();` at notes.js:1055 — add `const picked = pickedWords;` there, before the resets at :1067/:1045 clear it) and put it on both entry objects as `picked`. Then in `cross()`: `note: (entry.picked && entry.picked.replace(/[.]$/, "") !== String(entry.task).replace(/[.]$/, "")) ? entry.picked : ""`. Result: an unedited send carries no note (the title already is the words, and a duplicate line is not a fact), an edited wording carries the checked words underneath it, and no unchecked word ever crosses.

2. The tag map needs a declared fallback, because two of the five subjects have no word on the board. Notes' `SUBJECTS` (fixture.js:324–328) are mara-finn, the-house, the-studio, the-course, the-enquiries; the board's tag vocabulary is Mara & Finn / Nora & Cian / Aisling & Tom (the `CLIENTS` set at tasks.js:89) plus Venue, Bar, Enquiry. Only three translate: mara-finn → "Mara & Finn" (which correctly becomes the `.who` filter button rather than a static `.tag`), the-house → "Venue", the-enquiries → "Enquiry". the-studio and the-course have no board word and must fall back to `""` — `add()` already defaults `tag: ""` and the render is guarded by `if (task.tag)`, so an untagged card is a shape the board already draws (demo-t-03). Put the map next to `laneIdFor` in `TASKS_API` as `tagFor(label)`, so the board stays the authority on its own vocabulary exactly as it is for lanes, and pass `entry.about.key`/`aboutKey` rather than the label so the translation keys on an id and not on display copy.

3. Guard the empty description this creates. `tasks.js:344` builds `[said[0], task.note, task.tag, priority, comments].filter(Boolean).join(". ") + "."` and appends the full stop unconditionally. A `the-studio` note crossing into "To do" now has no time (`time.kind === "none"` → `said = ["",""]`), no note and no tag, so `#cd-<id>` renders as a lone `"."` — a card whose accessible description is one full stop. Emit the `<span class="sr">` and the `aria-describedby` only when the join is non-empty.
confirmed.breaks:
What it plausibly breaks:

- **The card's "open its note" affordance.** `tasks.js:328` emits `aria-expanded` only `if (task.note)`. An unedited send now produces a card with no note, so it loses `aria-expanded` and the press-the-body-to-open gesture — correctly, but it means a seam card and its three fixture siblings behave differently to the same press. Decide deliberately and say so in a comment, the way the rest of this file does.
- **Card height, hence tray layout.** Removing `.cardNote` takes ~38px off the seam card (measured: card box 234×135.75, `.cardNote` 181×37.69 at 13px/18.85 leading). This is runtime-only — the seam card exists only after driving — so the frozen four-width fidelity check is untouched. It *would* move if anyone "fixed" this by editing the `demo-t-*` notes in `fixture.js` instead. Do not; those cards are in the frames.
- **The condensed fixture notes become a claim the code cannot make.** Once the runtime seam sends only checked words, demo-t-01/02/06's hand-written condensations are a shape no live crossing can produce. Either accept them as "a person edited the wording later" or replace them with strings the new rule could have produced. Leaving them is defensible; leaving them *unexamined* is how this defect got here.

What to re-measure after it lands:

- `node verify.mjs` — the seam block matches on the title, not the note, so it should stay green; confirm "the card is on the board" and "…in the lane the seam chose" still pass, and confirm undo still restores `cardsBefore`.
- `node gate.mjs` and the audit at `--lab=…master-suite-2026-08` — palette/weights/targets/leading unaffected in principle, but the card's box changed, so re-run rather than assume.
- Fidelity at 390/768/1280/1440/1920 on `tasks.board` and `tasks.dense`: should be byte-identical, since no fixture card changed. If it is not, the fix touched the wrong thing.
- **Add the assertion while it is fresh**, in `interaction-check.mjs`, which today contains no seam assertion at all: after a driven send, assert that the landed card's rendered text and its `aria-describedby` target contain no word that was not in the picked selection, and that its `.tag`, if present, is a member of the board's own tag set. That is the assertion that would have caught this, and it is the one that keeps `cross()` and the fixture from drifting apart again.
- Drive one `the-studio` note (n04 or n13) end to end, not just n14 — that is the path that exercises the empty-tag fallback and the lone-full-stop description, and it is the case the finding as filed does not reach.

confirmed.element: Mara & Finn's wedding date, across all three sheets
confirmed.problem: Notes' head and its index both read "Mara & Finn · Saturday 18 July, in 2 days", and its notes say "Saturday wedding, Mara & Finn. Ceremony 2pm in the orchard". Tasks carries "Build the Saturday run-sheet — Ceremony 2pm orchard, drinks terrace, dinner 5.30pm" and "Confirm marquee sides… Mara & Finn, Saturday." Timeline's head reads "MARA & FINN · 79 days · Saturday 3 October 2026 · Wedding day". One couple, one clock, two wedding days, seventy-seven days apart. The ONE WORLD join in fixture.js asserts the project's *name* across the three fixtures and never asserts its *date*, which is the one fact all three sheets are organised around. It also makes Timeline's own moments nonsense against the other two: "Send the invitations, Sat 8 Aug" and "Final dress fitting, Sat 22 Aug" fall three and five weeks after the wedding Notes and Tasks are working towards.
confirmed.consequence: The suite's entire claim is that there is one world under the three sheets. A person clicks the spine from Notes to Timeline and the date the season turns on changes. That is not a nuance a venue manager forgives — it is the moment she stops believing any number on any of the three screens, and it is visible within ten seconds of the first spine press.
confirmed.fix: Extend the ONE WORLD join to assert the day, not just the name: `agree("Mara & Finn's day", T.project.primaryDate.date, <the ISO date Notes' next.when names>)`, and reconcile the fixtures so they agree — either Timeline's plan is Mara & Finn's and its dates sit around 18 July, or the plan on Timeline's head belongs to a differently named couple and the head, the countdown and the announcement say that name. No new data is needed either way; one of the two existing statements has to give.
confirmed.assertion: fixture.js throws at load if the wedding date Timeline's primaryDate names differs from the date Notes' `next` names for the same project, and the behaviour gate asserts that the day named on Timeline's head and the day named on Notes' head are the same calendar day.
confirmed.verdict: Verified in source and by driving. `src/fixture.js:324` and `:581` hardcode Notes' subject and head as `{ label: "Mara & Finn", when: "Saturday 18 July", days: 2 }`; note n01's body reads "Saturday wedding, Mara & Finn. Ceremony 2pm in the orchard"; Tasks carries `demo-t-05` "Build the Saturday run-sheet … Due today" (dueAt 2026-07-16) and `demo-t-01` "Mara & Finn, Saturday". `src/fixture.js:768` sets `PROJECT.primaryDate = { label: "Wedding day", date: "2026-10-03" }` on a project whose `name` is "Mara & Finn". Driven at 1440 the Timeline head renders "MARA & FINN / 79 days / Saturday 3 October 2026 / Wedding day" and the Notes head renders "Mara & Finn · Saturday 18 July, in 2 days". Both are Saturdays; both are 2026; they are 77 days apart. One couple, one clock, two wedding days — the suite's own premise contradicted on the one fact all three sheets are organised around, and the spine puts the two heads two seconds apart. The gate-blindness claim is also correct: the join asserts `T.project.name` (line 921) and `N.project` (line 922) but never a date; the only date join is the milestone-title twin check (lines 931–946), which the wedding day never enters because Tasks names only "Menu tasting at The Orchard". Misleading is the right class, not blocking: everything still works, but the product asserts something untrue. Two corrections to the finding's scope. First, the contradiction is already internal to Notes and Tasks, not just Timeline vs the other two: Notes' own n02 body says "Mara & Finn's menu tasting at The Orchard is booked for 1 August" and Tasks' `demo-t-02` carries "Milestone due 1 Aug" — a tasting two weeks after the wedding those same two sheets say is in two days. Second, "no new data is needed either way; one of the two existing statements has to give" understates the blast radius badly, and one of the two branches the fix offers is not available. Renaming Timeline's plan to another couple breaks `agree("Timeline's project", …)`, and there is no couple to give an October date to — the two siblings the fixture names are Nora & Cian (2027-04-17) and Aisling & Tom (undated), so that branch does require invented data. Moving Timeline to 18 July would strand nine dated milestones (1 Aug through 19 Sep all fall after the day), break the Tasks↔Timeline milestone join, contradict Tasks' season "6 Jul – 10 Oct · day 11 of 97", and rewrite the countdown 79 → 2, which is the whole Approach composition. The date the fixture can least afford to move is 3 October; the cheap-looking side, "Saturday 18 July", is the invented one — the SUBJECTS block labels itself "the one honest extension" and says its dated subjects "come from the review fixture's own project and its wedding date", which is exactly the derivation that came out wrong. Confirmed on the problem and on the direction of the fix; the mechanics are sharpened below.
confirmed.sharpenedFix: Anchor on 3 October and move the July claims, not the reverse. (1) Put the date in the header that already declares it in prose — `WORLD.projectDate = "2026-10-03"` — and assert all three against it: `agree("Timeline's day", T.project.primaryDate.date, WORLD.projectDate)`, plus `agree("Notes' day", N.next.when, T.fmt.long(WORLD.projectDate))` and `agree("Notes' countdown", N.next.days, T.days(WORLD.today, WORLD.projectDate))`. Note the finding's one-liner cannot be written as given: Notes holds no ISO anywhere, only the display string, which is why the assertion has to run through Timeline's `fmt.long`/`days` — and why `SUBJECTS["mara-finn"].when/days` and `next.when/days` should be derived from `WORLD.projectDate` at build rather than left as the two hardcoded literals that drifted in the first place. (2) Then the copy that names a July Saturday as the wedding has to move: Notes `next`/`SUBJECTS` ("Saturday 18 July", days 2), n01's "Saturday wedding … Ceremony 2pm in the orchard" (it can stay a Mara & Finn note about the ceremony without asserting it is this weekend), Tasks `demo-t-05` "Build the Saturday run-sheet" with `due: "Due today"` / `dueAt: 2026-07-16` / `dueTone: "today"`, `demo-t-01`'s "Mara & Finn, Saturday … by Thursday", and `demo_task_registrar` "Send registrar paperwork two weeks before the date" completed 2026-07-02, which is two weeks before the wrong date. Do not move Timeline's milestones, the Tasks milestone chip, or Notes' "booked for 1 August" — those nine dates are the load-bearing set and they already agree with each other. (3) Keep the stake sort as it is: Mara & Finn is stake 1 and the college reading stake 2, so the head still opens on the wedding at 79 days out — which is the case the stake rule was written for, and worth saying out loud in the comment.
confirmed.breaks: Notes' head and index string grows from "Saturday 18 July, in 2 days" to "Saturday 3 October, in 79 days" — re-measure the head row and the index row at 390 and 768, where that line is tightest, and confirm the two-digit countdown does not push the subject label to a second line. Tasks loses its only "Due today" card, so the board head's "1 today" counter, the `dueTone: "today"` treatment and `progress.overdue/day/of/left` all need re-deriving, and `demo-t-05`'s tone token stops being exercised anywhere unless another card takes it — check the dense state still covers today/soon/overdue. Every Notes and Tasks frame moves, so the pixel-fidelity gate against the frozen lab masters at four widths will fail until those two products' baselines are re-cut (Timeline's stay identical, which is the point of anchoring here). Re-run `node gate.mjs`, `node verify.mjs`, `interaction-check.mjs` and the elevate audit; the new `agree` calls are load-time throws, so a wrong ISO fails at load rather than in a frame, which is the behaviour to verify first. Also re-read the seam after the copy edits: n01 → `demo-t-01` and n02 → `demo-t-02` are two of the six LINK pairs, and the join checks the link by id but a reader checks it by wording. Size: this is a different decision plus a fixture rewrite, not polish — roughly half a day of fixture and copy work and a re-baseline of two products' frames, and the founder has to say out loud which date is Mara & Finn's before any of it is worth starting.

confirmed.element: Notes · notes.seam · "Already in Tasks · 3 so far, and every note stayed here"
confirmed.problem: The count comes from `CROSSED.length` — a three-row fixture array — while the same product badges three further notes "In Tasks" in its own index (the marquee note, the menu tasting note, the bar restock note), the suite's join declares six links, and Tasks carries six cards marked as having come from a note. So the heading says three under a promise about all of them, and the product itself shows six.
confirmed.consequence: This number sits directly under the sentence the whole suite is arguing — "and every note stayed here". A count that is half the truth in the place the promise is being made spends the credibility of the promise, and it is checkable by a person in about four seconds of scrolling.
confirmed.fix: Derive the heading's number and its rows from the same accessor that badges a note "In Tasks" — the join's LINK map — so the ledger counts and lists every note that has crossed. If the intent is a recent window, the heading has to say so in words rather than print an all-time grammar ("so far") over a partial list.
confirmed.assertion: On notes.seam, the number in the "Already in Tasks" heading equals the number of Tasks cards carrying fromNote, and equals the number of ledger rows rendered; driving the seam once raises all three by one.
confirmed.verdict: Verified in source and by driving chromium against _gate-suite.html. The seam ledger renders `${CROSSED.length} so far, and every note stayed here` (line 13224) over `indexOf(CROSSED, …)`, and CROSSED is `N.crossed.slice()` (10851) — the three-row fixture s1/s2/s3, which are NOT in the notebook at all. Driven at 1920: notes.seam head reads "ALREADY IN TASKS / 3 so far, and every note stayed here" with exactly 3 rows; notes.notebook badges three further notes "In Tasks" (n01 marquee, n02 menu tasting, n09 bar restock — all `sent: true`, tags counted live: 3 of 14); tasks.board paints 6 cards carrying the "Came from a note" glyph. The suite's own ONE WORLD join declares six links (LINK, 7480) and throws unless six tasks say they came from a note — it asserts six in the same file, twenty lines above the code that prints three. So the surface whose entire job is to hold the trace of the product's central act states a number the rest of the same application contradicts three ways. This is the named paid-for class "Self-contradicting counts" (lessons.md, Information and honesty: "Every fact on the surface derives from the rendered data through ONE accessor") creeping back across the product boundary, which is precisely the seam this first suite panel exists to test. The join was edited this round to make the ledger's LANE derive from the board (7514) and left the count alone. No scoped reading rescues it: the ledger is not filtered by subject (all three rows are mara-finn while the peeled note n14 is the-house), and "so far" is all-time grammar under a promise about "every note". Nothing the gates assert covers it — verify.mjs only checks that a just-sent row reaches the ledger. Severity is right at misleading, not blocking: the seam works end to end, the count is simply untrue. It is also permanent, not transient — a live send calls `window.__SUITE.cross`, which appends a `fromNote: true` task, so the board goes 6→7 while the ledger goes 3→4 (driven and confirmed). The gap of three never closes in either direction.
confirmed.sharpenedFix: The proposed fix has the right shape and the wrong accessor, so take the shape and correct the name. LINK is not "the accessor that badges a note In Tasks" — the badge comes from `note.sent` (idxRow, 12737), while LINK backs `N.taskOf()`, i.e. what "In Tasks as …" opens. Building the ledger from LINK literally would freeze it to a six-key static map and drop the just-sent row, regressing the bought fix recorded at 10847–10851 ("It read from the fixture constant, so the one surface whose whole job is to hold the trace of the product's central act was the one surface the act never reached"). Derive instead from `sent`, which is live: make the ledger's rows and its number one accessor returning the deduped union of `work().filter(n => n.sent)` and CROSSED, newest crossing first. Two supporting edits are required or the three new rows render broken: (a) extend the join at 7514 from `N.crossed.forEach` to every LINK key across both collections, so n01/n02/n09 get a board-derived lane — without it `esc(note.lane)` prints an empty or "null" chip, since those three carry no lane; (b) leave `crossedWhen` alone — idxRow already falls back `note.crossedWhen || note.when`, so the three notebook notes date from capture rather than crossing, and if that imprecision is unacceptable the honest alternative is dropping the when column for rows that have no crossing time, not inventing three timestamps. The finding's second clause — say "recent" in words if a window is intended — is not available here: there is no window, the two groups are disjoint containers, and naming a window would only relabel the contradiction.
confirmed.breaks: Six rows instead of three lengthens the seam's index below the desk; check that the ledger still fits without scrolling the sheet at 1280 and 1440 (the round already moved Notes' content column 1060→1440, and lessons.md warns the measure has a floor as well as a ceiling — check 1280, not only 1440). The three added rows print `note.task` as their lede, and n01/n02/n09's task strings run long ("Confirm marquee sides with hire company before Thursday", "Order 2 cases tonic + olives before weekend") — re-check single-line truncation and the idempotent-trim rule in crossed mode, where `rest` is empty and the tag plus when column compete for the same row. Re-run fidelity: notes.seam is a frozen-master comparison at four widths and this changes it deliberately, so the baseline needs re-freezing with the change named. Re-run the palette/contrast/target/leading audit and interaction-check on notes.seam (the ledger gains three rows with new lane chips whose text comes from the board's column names — "Done" for all six, which is what the board says). Re-drive the send path to confirm the count goes 6→7 and undo returns it to 6, and confirm the de-dup holds so a sent note cannot appear twice once `crossed_<id>` and the note itself both carry `sent`. No new colour, weight or architecture is involved.

confirmed.element: <kbd> across Notes, Tasks and Timeline
confirmed.problem: One modifier, four printings, in one document. Notes prints "Ctrl K" in the dock and "Ctrl ↓" on the index head, and "Ctrl+Z" on the undo bar and "Ctrl+Enter" on its commit buttons — space and plus on the same sheet, visible in the same frame. Timeline prints "Ctrl Z". On a Mac it gets worse: driven with a Mac platform, Notes prints "⌘K" and "⌘+Z" — and ⌘+Z is a form macOS does not use and no premium product prints. The detection differs too: Notes and Tasks read navigator.platform, Timeline reads navigator.userAgentData.platform first, so under a Mac platform in this browser Notes printed ⌘ while Timeline printed Ctrl in the same document.
confirmed.consequence: The keycap is the smallest and most repeated piece of type in the product, and it contradicts itself twice on one sheet. On a Mac one of the forms is simply wrong, which is the cheapest possible way to look like a Windows product with a Mac skin — and the two detections mean the app can tell one person she has two different keyboards.
confirmed.fix: One keycap helper at suite scope: one platform detection, one join — ⌘K / ⌘Z / ⌘↵ on Mac, Ctrl K / Ctrl Z / Ctrl ↵ elsewhere — and route every <kbd> in the three products through it. Delete the per-product MOD and MAC_KEYS constants.
confirmed.assertion: Across all eight states on both a Windows and a Mac platform string, every <kbd> in the document matches one notation; no <kbd> contains "+" under a Mac platform; and no two products in one document render different modifier glyphs.
confirmed.verdict:
Confirmed against source and against the running artifact; the frames alone would not have shown it, and driving made it worse than the seat claimed.

Co-visibility is real and needs no interaction. Loading `?v=paper&state=notes.notebook` at 1440 and dumping every `<kbd>` with a client rect returns exactly three, all on screen at once: `Ctrl+Enter`, `Ctrl ↓`, `Ctrl K`. Plus and space, same modifier, same frame, no scrolling. `notes.voice` shows five, including two `Ctrl+Enter` alongside `Ctrl ↓` and `Ctrl K`. Ticking a Tasks card raises `Ctrl Z`; `.b-grab` on Timeline raises `Ctrl Z`. Notes' undo strip renders `${MOD}+Z` (src/notes.js:1634) — driven through the seam it prints `Ctrl+Z`. Four printings stands.

The Mac half is worse than described, and the seat's causal account is incomplete. Under a spoofed `navigator.platform = "MacIntel"`, Notes prints `⌘+Enter` / `⌘↓` / `⌘K` / `⌘+Z`, Tasks prints `⌘Z`, Timeline prints `Ctrl Z` — six forms of one modifier. The seat blamed detection *order*. The actual mechanism is a case bug: timeline.js:1176-77 reads `(navigator.userAgentData && navigator.userAgentData.platform) || navigator.platform` and tests it with case-sensitive `/Mac|iPhone|iPad/`. Chrome's UA-CH value is the string `"macOS"` — lowercase m — which that regex does not match, and `||` short-circuits so `"MacIntel"` is never consulted. I confirmed this in page: with `userAgentData.platform === "macOS"` and `navigator.platform === "MacIntel"`, Timeline's expression evaluates **false** while Notes' evaluates **true**. This is not a harness artefact. **Timeline prints `Ctrl Z` on every Mac in every Chromium browser, today**, while Notes and Tasks two clicks away print ⌘. Three products in one application disagreeing about which keyboard the person is holding is the exact thing this round was convened to look for, and no gate can see it because no gate drives a Mac platform.

A fifth form the seat missed: on Mac, Tasks joins with no space (`⌘Z`, tasks.js:75 `MOD = "⌘"`) and Timeline joins with one (`⌘ Z`, timeline.js:1188). Tasks' constant is the only one of the three that is right — `"⌘"` bare on Mac, `"Ctrl "` with a trailing space elsewhere — because ⌘ is a glyph that abuts and Ctrl is a word that does not.

Severity corrected down to defect, deliberately. Every handler accepts both modifiers — timeline.js:1999, tasks.js:1809/1816, notes.js:3390/3415/3433/3438 all test `metaKey || ctrlKey` — so no keycap names a chord that fails, including `Ctrl Z` shown to a Mac user. Nothing the product says about what it will do is untrue, so this is not misleading and not blocking. But it sits at the very top of defect: it is not taste, it is one object typeset four ways inside one viewport, and at the Linear/Stripe/Vercel bar a shipped sheet does not print `Ctrl K` and `Ctrl+Enter` 400px apart.

The fix is directionally right and wrong in two places, both corrected below rather than used to refute — the diagnosis is sound and the remedy is one helper.
confirmed.sharpenedFix:
Same shape — one helper at suite scope, delete the three per-product constants — with three corrections.

1. **Do not introduce ↵.** The proposed normal form `⌘↵ / Ctrl ↵` is a copy change the defect does not require and a regression for this audience: Orla reads "Enter" off her keyboard, not U+21B5. It is also a font risk. Measuring the current keycap face in page, ⌘ renders 18px wide against 10.7px for "A" at the same size in the same declared stack (`Geist, system-ui, …`) — ⌘ is almost certainly already resolving out of Geist into a system fallback, and ↵ would be a second unmeasured glyph doing the same. Keep the word.

2. **Promote Tasks' join, not a new one.** tasks.js:75 already has the correct rule: `"⌘"` on Mac (no separator — ⌘ abuts, per Apple's own convention), `"Ctrl "` elsewhere (trailing space — Ctrl is a word). Normal form becomes `⌘Z ⌘K ⌘Enter ⌘↓` / `Ctrl Z Ctrl K Ctrl Enter Ctrl ↓`. That kills Notes' `+` in all four places and Timeline's stray space before Z, and requires no new typographic decision.

3. **Fix the detection while unifying it, and name the bug.** The single detection must be `/mac|iphone|ipad/i` tested against `navigator.platform` **or** must stop short-circuiting past it — adopting timeline.js's expression verbatim would propagate the `"macOS"` miss to all three products and silently lose Mac detection suite-wide. This is the load-bearing half of the fix; the notation cleanup is cosmetic beside it.

Scope the helper to modifier caps only. Leave `Esc`, `Space`, `T`, `K`, `L` and `.carry kbd[data-keys="arrows"]` untouched — the last carries bespoke `letter-spacing: 0.28em` and asymmetric padding at tasks.css:1014 that a shared helper must not swallow. Notes' index-head cap at notes.js:2049 already special-cases the arrow's spacing; preserve that rule when MOD is deleted or it regresses to `⌘ ↓`.

Call sites: notes.js 1617, 1634, 1715, 1850, 2049, 2319, 2390; tasks.js 755, 775; timeline.js 1188. Ten. The code is an afternoon; the cost is in the re-baseline below.
confirmed.breaks:
**Breaks the frozen-master fidelity assertion, and that is the real cost.** `Ctrl+Enter` → `Ctrl Enter` changes the cap's rendered width, which changes the intrinsic width of every Notes commit button carrying it — `.act.commitPart` (keep), save-edit, voice-stop, keep-both — and the undo strip's row. The round notes assert "every product's sheet is still pixel-identical to its own frozen lab master at four widths." This will move Notes' sheet at all four. That re-baseline must be taken deliberately and reviewed, not absorbed as noise, or the fidelity check stops being worth running.

**Re-measure, in this order:**

1. **The open contrast residue, after this lands and not before.** Round notes name it as "a handful of keycaps in the dictation state" — a 1px inset ring on an ink ground. The voice-stop cap (notes.js:2319) is one of the four caps this fix rewrites, it lives in exactly that state, and it gets wider. Re-measuring the residue against the current text would waste the measurement. `notes.voice` at 768 and 1440 are also the two frames already declared non-byte-reproducible, so the diff there has to be read by eye, not by hash.
2. `audit.mjs --lab=…/master-suite-2026-08` — palette/weights/families/AA/targets/radii/motion/ramp/leading. Families is the one to watch: if the helper's output ever routes a glyph that Geist lacks, the cap silently falls back and the declared-family check will not catch it, since it reads the declaration and not the coverage. Measure ⌘ and ↓ coverage explicitly rather than trusting green.
3. `interaction-check.mjs` — no assertion should move, since no handler is touched.
4. **The gap that let this in: add a Mac assertion.** No gate drives a Mac platform, which is why a Timeline keycap that is wrong on every Mac in Chrome survived nineteen rounds. After unifying, assert under one spoofed platform (`userAgentData.platform = "macOS"`, `navigator.platform = "MacIntel"`) that all three products print the same modifier glyph. Without that assertion the divergence returns the next time one product is edited alone, and nothing will see it.

**Size: polish, one afternoon of code, plus one deliberate re-baseline of Notes' frozen master.** Not a build and not a different decision. The one judgement call the founder actually has to make is whether Notes' sheet may move at four widths to buy one keycap grammar — and it should, because the alternative is shipping a suite whose whole argument is that the walls came out, printing one modifier six ways.

confirmed.fix: Write the receipt as one sentence with the destination inline: "Sent to Tasks, filed under The house. Your note stayed here." confirmed.element: .rail [data-rail] — the floating capsule, at desk width
confirmed.problem: The spine's arrow walk is handled differently on each mounted product, and is wrong on two of the three. On tasks.board every arrow press moves TWO tiles: Home↓→Tasks (skips Notes), Notes↓→Timeline (skips Tasks), Tasks↓→Inbox (skips Timeline), Timeline↓→Help (skips Inbox); Up mirrors it. The tiles split into two parities that never meet, so from the Tasks tile — where the rover starts on the Tasks page — ArrowDown/ArrowUp reach only Home, Inbox and the account tile, never Notes and never Timeline. On notes.notebook the arrows do not move inside the rail at all: ArrowDown from any rail tile throws focus 280px away onto .idxRow in the note index, and ArrowUp does the same upward — as do Home, End, PageUp and PageDown. The rail's roving tabindex="0" silently moves to Tasks while the deck is still showing Notes, so the tab stop now names a product you are not on. At desk width ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, PageUp and PageDown on the vertical rail all dump focus onto the account tile, a door that does nothing. Timeline alone walks correctly, one tile per press, both directions. verify.mjs is blind to all of it: it presses ArrowDown three times and only asserts three distinct data-rail values, which the doubled walk satisfies.
confirmed.consequence: On the Notes page at 1440 a keyboard-only person cannot leave Notes: the rail has exactly one tab stop (the Notes tile), and every navigation key on it is swallowed by the note index. On the Tasks board the two other products are unreachable from the tile the rover starts on. This is the suite's whole premise — one spine, three products, nothing torn down — and by keyboard it is three products with the door jammed.
confirmed.fix: Attach one keydown listener to the .rail element (not the document, and not one per mounted product). Let it own ArrowUp/ArrowDown at >720, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight at ≤720, plus Home and End, and call preventDefault() and stopPropagation() on each so Notes' index handler and Tasks' board handler never see them. Move the rover exactly one visible tile per press, skipping only display:none tiles, and clamp or wrap consistently. Make the keys the rail does not own (PageUp/PageDown, the cross-axis arrows) inert rather than jumping to the account tile. Re-stamp tabindex="0" on the tile whose data-rail equals deck's data-product on every render, so the rover can never name a product that is not showing.
confirmed.assertion: For each of tasks.board, notes.notebook and timeline.owner-flight at 1440: focusing each visible .rail button and pressing ArrowDown moves focus to exactly the next visible .rail button in DOM order, and ArrowUp to the previous one; no rail key moves focus outside .rail; and after any rail key document.querySelector('.rail [tabindex="0"]').dataset.rail === document.getElementById('deck').dataset.product.
confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED, and reproduced key-for-key in chromium at 1440x1000 against _gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=<state>. The mechanism is exactly two handlers walking one rover.

Root cause, in master.html:
- Suite handler, master.html:7940-7959 — delegated on `deck`, correct in shape, but it walks `deck.querySelectorAll(".rail [data-rail]")` with NO visibility filter, and calls preventDefault() without stopPropagation().
- Tasks' `groupKeys`, master.html:8362-8383 — reached from onKey (9783) via the document listener at 10760. The rail carries `data-group="rail"` (7692), so groupKeys claims it too, and it filters `offsetParent !== null`. deck's bubble handler fires first and moves focus; groupKeys then reads `document.activeElement` (already moved) and moves it again. Net: two tiles per press.
- Notes' handler, master.html:14178 — bound on window, gated only on `__SUITE.active("notes")`, never on where focus is. A rail tile is not `typing`, so ArrowDown/ArrowUp fall through to moveCursor (14487-14490), Home/End to jumpCursor, PageUp/PageDown to pageCursor — all of which `refocus`/`paint()` into `.idxRow`.

Driven results, ArrowDown x8 starting on the Tasks tile:
- tasks.board: tasks → inbox → me → home → tasks → (repeats). The rail's visible list is 8 (mark home notes tasks timeline inbox help me; `add` is display:none at desk), even, so the +2 walk splits into two parities. Notes and Timeline are unreachable from the Tasks tile in both directions. Exactly as the seat wrote it.
- notes.notebook: focus lands on `.idxRow` on press one and stays there for all eight, while `.rail [tabindex="0"]` silently migrates to `timeline` — a roving stop naming a product that is not on the deck. Home, End, PageUp, PageDown all do the same.

Two corrections to the finding, both of which make it worse, not better:
1. "Timeline alone walks correctly, one tile per press, both directions" is FALSE. Timeline walks one tile per press and then dead-ends: tasks → timeline → inbox → help → STUCK. Because the suite handler does not filter hidden tiles, the rover lands on `add` (display:none at desk), `focus()` is a no-op, focus is stranded on `help`, `tabindex="0"` is stranded on an invisible button, and every further ArrowDown recomputes the same dead move. `me` is unreachable by ArrowDown on every product. The same dead-end fires at 390: on the phone dock ArrowRight goes tasks → timeline and then stops forever, because `inbox` is the next entry and it is hidden. So the walk is broken on three of three, not two of three.
2. "At desk width ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, PageUp and PageDown all dump focus onto the account tile" is FALSE. Tested clean (fresh page per key, no leftover rover): on tasks.board and timeline.desk all four are already fully inert, focus and rover unchanged. The seat almost certainly read a rover left over from a prior End press in the same session. On notes.notebook PageUp/PageDown are not inert — they jump to `.idxRow` — but that is the Notes leak already named, not an account-tile jump.

Gate blindness is accurate as stated. verify.mjs:511-518 focuses the rover, presses ArrowDown three times and asserts only `walked.length === 3 && new Set(walked).size === 3`. On tasks the doubled walk yields inbox → me → home: three distinct values, green. Zero console errors throughout, so nothing else flags it.

Class is blocking, not defect: the rail is a roving-tabindex toolbar with `role`-bearing tiles and the brief advertises "Arrows walk it (down/up at desk, left/right at ≤720)". On the product the suite opens on, the arrows cannot reach two of the three products at all, and on Notes they do not move the rail whatsoever. A keyboard-only operator cannot cross the suite by the mechanism the suite documents.

The proposed fix is right in thrust and wrong in two specific clauses, both corrected in sharpenedFix: (a) binding to `.rail` is wrong — paintRail (7712-7724) does `nav.outerHTML = railHtml()`, destroying that node on every product switch and every disabled-door press, so the listener would be dead after the first switch; it also contradicts the file's own stated discipline at 10678 ("One delegated listener per event, on the container, so a repaint can never leave a handler behind"). The existing `deck` delegation is already the correct home. (b) "Re-stamp tabindex=0 on the tile whose data-rail equals deck's data-product on every render" would break documented, deliberate behaviour: `railCurrent` is persisted on purpose (7650, 7760, 7921, 7957; comment at 8377) so the rover can rest on a door. Clicking Inbox sets railCurrent="inbox" and calls paintRail, which restores focus to Inbox — re-stamping would force tabindex=0 back onto the product tile while focus sits on Inbox, reintroducing the same focus/rover desync from the other direction and making the honest doors lose the tab stop the operator just moved to. The desync on Notes is a symptom of focus being stolen, not of the rover being stamped wrong; fix the theft and the two stay in lockstep on their own. Also, the fix says nothing about groupKeys, which is the actual cause of the doubling — and note that its rail branch is already half-dead: line 8380 writes railCurrent only `if (items[to].dataset.key)`, and suite tiles carry `data-rail`, not `data-key`, so it moves focus and updates nothing. It is vestigial Tasks code and should be deleted, not merely propagation-blocked.
confirmed.sharpenedFix:
Keep the one delegated listener where it already is — on `deck` (master.html:7940) — and make it the sole owner of the rail's keys. Four changes:

1. Delete the rail branch from Tasks' `groupKeys` (master.html:8363-8365, 8380): make it bail immediately when `group.dataset.group === "rail"` (`if (group.dataset.group === "rail") return false;`), drop the now-constant `horizontal` ternary, and drop the dead `items[to].dataset.key` railCurrent write. That alone removes the doubling on Tasks and removes a second writer of one piece of state.

2. In the deck handler, walk visible tiles only: build `keys` as `[...deck.querySelectorAll(".rail [data-rail]")].filter(n => n.offsetParent !== null)` — the same predicate groupKeys already uses. This is what unsticks `add` at desk and `inbox` on the 390 dock; the rover can then never be stranded on a button that cannot take focus. Keep the existing wrap (it is a toolbar of eight; wrap is right and Home/End already exist). Guard `i < 0` after the filter so a press while focus sits on a hidden tile recovers to index 0 rather than computing from -1.

3. Scope-limited stopPropagation: for the four keys the rail owns (fwd, back, Home, End — chosen by the existing `matchMedia("(max-width: 720px)")` test), call `event.stopPropagation()` alongside the existing preventDefault, so Notes' window listener (14178) and Tasks' document listener (10760) never see them. Do NOT blanket-stop all keydown on the rail: Ctrl/⌘Z and Ctrl/⌘K currently reach their products from a focused rail tile and must keep doing so. For the keys the rail does not own, add a narrow pass-through guard so the leak is closed without swallowing scroll: `if (["PageUp","PageDown","ArrowLeft","ArrowRight","ArrowUp","ArrowDown","Home","End"].includes(event.key)) event.stopPropagation();` before the ownership test — propagation stopped, default left alone, so PageUp/PageDown still page the sheet natively and Notes' index no longer answers them. Cross-axis arrows are then genuinely inert, which is where Tasks and Timeline already are; only Notes changes.

4. Leave the roving stamp alone. Do not re-derive it from `deck[data-product]` on render. Once focus can no longer be stolen (step 3) and can no longer land on a hidden tile (step 2), `railCurrent` and `document.activeElement` stay in lockstep by construction, and the door tiles keep the tab stop the operator moved to — which is the designed answer for Home/Inbox/Help/More/account.

Then strengthen the gate, or it will go on passing a broken walk. Replace verify.mjs:511-518 with a full-lap assertion: for each of tasks/notes/timeline, at 1440 and 390, focus the rover and press the forward key `n` times where n = the visible tile count, asserting the exact ordered sequence of `data-rail` values and a clean return to the start; repeat backwards; and after every single press assert `document.activeElement.dataset.rail === document.querySelector('.rail [tabindex="0"]').dataset.rail`. That last invariant is the one that would have caught all three failures on its own.

confirmed.element: Tasks · the Waiting lane and all five .trayAdd "Add here" buttons

confirmed.fix: Put every lane's .trayAdd into the card rover: ArrowDown past the last card in a lane focuses that lane's tray-add, and ArrowLeft/ArrowRight into a lane with no cards focuses its tray-add rather than skipping the lane. Keep them tabindex="-1" so the roving model is unchanged.

confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED by source and by driving. `_gate-suite.html:8654-8657` stamps `tabindex` on `.trayAdd` as `rows.some(t => t.id === focusId) || (!focusId && c.id === B.columns[0].id) ? "0" : "-1"` — the Add row is a tab stop only for the lane holding the roving card. `walk()` at :9654-9667 skips lanes with no rows outright (`for (let x = at.x + dx; ...) { if (rows.length) {...} }`), so an empty lane can never hold focusId. Driven at 1440 and 390 on `tasks.board`: lanes report `todo:3:ti0, doing:3:ti-1, review:2:ti-1, waiting:0:ti-1, done:5:ti-1`; a 90-press Tab sweep of the whole surface never reaches "Add a task to Waiting" (it visits railTile, chips, head tools, one card + its three controls, "Add a task to To do", then the dock); and ArrowRight from Review lands on Done, skipping Waiting. Carrying a To do card right three times does land it in Waiting and drops it there — so the seat's sharpest line is exactly right: the lane exists for the rover only while something is in the air. This is a recurrence of a paid-for class in lessons.md ("the roving model must reach EVERY item"), applied to the tray-add rather than to cards, and it lands against an explicitly designed intent — the comment above the tabindex expression states "One Add row in the tab order — the column the roving stop is in". Nothing in interaction-check.mjs asserts anything about `.trayAdd` or the Waiting lane, so this is not a gate restatement. Two corrections to the seat's text, neither fatal: (1) `.trayEmpty` is a plain `

Nothing held up.

` with no `tabindex` at all — not `tabindex="-1"` as claimed; it is a paragraph and correctly non-focusable, so that clause is both wrong and a non-issue. (2) The other Add rows are reachable by Tab from ANY focused card in their lane, not only the last one. SEVERITY: I hold it at defect, not blocking. A keyboard-only operator can still get work into Waiting — add in To do, Space, ArrowRight x3, Space — and the button works under a pointer, so the product still does what it says end to end. But it sits at the top of defect: a visible, named, hit-target-sized button that no key sequence can press is an accessibility hole one lane wide, and on a board whose Waiting column is empty most of the time it is the lane an operator most often needs to seed. FIX JUDGEMENT: the direction is right and is an improvement, but one clause of it is wrong against the source. "Keep them tabindex='-1' so the roving model is unchanged" misreads the code — the model already promotes one `.trayAdd` to `tabindex="0"`, and if the rover's position were an Add row left at -1, the board would have no tab stop at all and Shift-Tab out of it would be undefined, reproducing the same defect one lane over. The fix is also silent on the return path: `onKey` bails at `const card = event.target.closest(".card[data-id]"); if (!card) return;` (:9868-9869), so arrows on a focused `.trayAdd` do nothing today and the rover would be a one-way trip into a dead end.
confirmed.sharpenedFix: Do the smaller of the two available fixes: make `walk()` stop at an empty lane instead of skipping it, and leave lanes that hold cards exactly as they are — drop the ArrowDown-past-the-last-card change entirely. It doubles the rover's row count in every lane, changes the `Math.min(at.y, rows.length - 1)` column arithmetic on every sideways move, and has to be excluded from `carryMove` so a card in hand never targets an Add row; none of that is needed to close the hole. Concretely: (1) in `walk()` (:9654), when the neighbouring lane has no rows, set the rover to that lane's Add row rather than continuing the loop — which needs a rover position that is not a task id, e.g. `focusAdd = laneId` with `focusId = null`, since `place(focusId)` is task-typed. (2) Update the tabindex expression at :8655 so the lane that owns the rover gives its `.trayAdd` `tabindex="0"` whether the rover is on a card or on the Add row — every other one stays -1, one tab stop on the board, invariant preserved. Do NOT keep all five at -1. (3) Extend the arrow branch of `onKey` past the `.card[data-id]` guard at :9868 to `.trayAdd`: ArrowUp returns to the lane's last card, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight walk to the neighbouring lane, and Space must be inert there (it must not pick anything up) while Enter keeps its existing meaning of opening the composer. (4) Skip any lane whose Add row is not rendered: `.board[data-filtered] .tray[data-empty] .trayAdd { display: none; }` (:2058) and `.board[data-blank] .trayAdd { display: none; }` (:2080) both remove it, and `.trayAdd[data-under]` (:1726) makes it `opacity: 0; pointer-events: none` when the carry strip overlaps it — landing the rover on any of those is the "invisible-but-focusable control" defect in the same lessons file. (5) Fix the fallback in `leaveDraft()` (:9734-9740), which reaches for `.card[tabindex="0"]` and would find nothing when the rover is on an Add row. The focus ring needs no new work: `[data-app="tasks"] button:focus-visible` (:625) already covers it.
confirmed.breaks: Plausible breakage: the single-tab-stop invariant, if step 2 is skipped — a rover on an Add row left at -1 leaves the board with no tab stop and strands Shift-Tab. The filtered and blank branches, where the Add row is `display: none` and the lane still has zero cards — without step 4 the rover walks onto an undrawn button and focus vanishes to `<body>`, which is strictly worse than today. `leaveDraft()` and `returnFromDrawer()`, both of which assume the board's tab stop is a card. And at 390 the board is `scroll-snap-type: x mandatory` with 86% columns, so focusing an empty lane's Add row scrolls the board — that scroll must survive the `mount()` repaint that follows, or the operator lands focused on something off screen. Re-measure after it lands: interaction-check.mjs in full (194 assertions, none currently touching `.trayAdd`, so add one that Tab or the rover reaches every lane's Add row in `tasks.board`, `tasks.dense`, filtered, and blank); the Tasks audit for hit target, radius and AA on the Add row now that it can carry the focus ring in a lane rendered at `data-empty` recession; the four-width fidelity check, since nothing visual should move at all — any pixel diff means step 2 changed rendering rather than only tab order; and drive the carry path again at 390 and 1920 to confirm `carryMove` still walks a card into and out of an empty Waiting with no Add-row interference.

confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED by driving, and it is worse than filed. At 390x844 on tasks.board the capsule paints nine members; geometry matches the finding exactly — home 28, notes 96, tasks 164, timeline 232 all 44x44, .railAdd 44x44 at x=295, .railAvatar 32x32 at x=341. Driving the rover from the Tasks tile: ArrowRight goes tasks -> timeline, then stops dead. Six further ArrowRights never move focus off timeline and never reach Add task or the avatar. ArrowLeft reaches home and then stops dead. End does land on the avatar, skipping Add task. Add task is reachable by no key at all — it carries tabindex="-1" and only becomes the roving stop if it is clicked.

The seat's DIAGNOSIS is wrong, though, and that matters for the fix. The handler at _gate-suite.html:7949 does not clamp and .railAdd/.railAvatar are not excluded from the rover: it selects `.rail [data-rail]` — all nine, add and me included — and walks it with a modulo wrap. What actually happens is that at <=720 `.railMark`, `.railDivider/.railSpacer` and `.railUtil` (inbox, help) go `display:none` (line 453/456) while staying in the queried group. ArrowRight from timeline picks `inbox`, the handler sets `inbox.tabIndex = 0` and every other member to -1, then calls `inbox.focus()`, which silently no-ops on a display:none element. Focus is left on timeline with tabindex -1, `event.target.closest` still resolves to timeline on the next press, so it re-picks inbox forever. Same trap on ArrowLeft at home -> mark.

The consequence the seat did not measure is the blocking one: after two ArrowRights the only member of `.rail [data-rail]` with tabIndex 0 is a display:none element, so the capsule has ZERO visible tab stops. Measured directly — the visible-tab-stop list is empty. On a phone the capsule is the only way between the three products, so two arrow presses remove Notes, Tasks and Timeline from the keyboard entirely until the page is reloaded. That is the advertised keyboard model ("Arrows walk it, left/right at <=720") not doing what it says: blocking, not defect. I also saw End-then-Home leave two members at tabIndex 0 simultaneously (mark and home) — the exact "two zeros in one roving group" regression the source comment near line 8462 claims to have retired.

The filed FIX is a no-op as literally written — add and me are already members of the roving group, so "just make them members" changes nothing and the trap survives. Corrected fix in sharpenedFix. I am confirming rather than refuting because the observed behaviour, the elements, the coordinates and the intended end state (ArrowRight walks to the end of the capsule, End lands on its last tile) are all correct and verified; only the mechanism needs replacing, and the sharpened fix reaches the end state the seat asked for.
confirmed.sharpenedFix:
Do not touch tabindex authoring or group membership. Filter the rover to members that are actually rendered, at every width, in the keydown handler at _gate-suite.html:7951:

  var keys = [].slice.call(deck.querySelectorAll(".rail [data-rail]"))
    .filter(function (el) { return el.getClientRects().length > 0; });

That yields home·notes·tasks·timeline·add·me at <=720 (add·me now walked to, End already correct), and mark·home·notes·tasks·timeline·inbox·help·me at the desk — where the same latent trap exists in reverse, because base `.railAdd { display: none }` (line 348) puts a hidden member between help and me.

1. Guard the declared stop in `railHtml()` (line 7691): `stop(key)` compares against `railCurrent`, and railCurrent can hold a key that is hidden at the current width (click Add task at 390, resize to desk). Fall back to `current` when railCurrent names a member that is not rendered, so the rail always keeps exactly one usable tab stop.
2. Same guard in `paintRail()` (line 7729): `back.focus()` no-ops if the remembered key is hidden after a repaint or a product switch, which strands focus the same way.

It is nine elements inside one nav, so it is cheap, but if the capsule is ever animated in or out (or a product switch repaints mid-transition) the group can be measured empty; guard with a fallback to the unfiltered list when the filter returns nothing, or the arrows go dead during the transition. confirmed.element: Notes · Ctrl/⌘Z after [data-act="send"]
confirmed.problem: The seam end to end keeps focus properly — the peel puts focus in .peelField, the send puts it on the "Open in Tasks" .deskFactLink — and the undo restores the data correctly and announces "Taken back. Nothing went to Tasks." But it leaves document.activeElement === document.body. Tasks' own tick-then-undo does this right: focus comes back to the .tick it left from, on the card restored to To do.
confirmed.consequence: The person reverses the suite's flagship action and is dropped at the top of the document. Every route back into what they were doing costs a fresh walk through the whole tab order, and a screen-reader user hears the announcement with no context for where they now are.
confirmed.fix: On the seam undo, restore focus the way the Tasks undo already does — to the element the undo brought back, or failing that to the .readBody the words were peeled from — in the same frame as the repaint.
confirmed.assertion: On notes.notebook, run the seam to a completed send, press Ctrl+Z: document.activeElement is not document.body and is contained within the Notes sheet.
confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED by driving, and the seat understated it — the same defect is on both routes, including the one the source claims is handled. Measured at 1440 on `?v=paper&state=notes.notebook`: lift `.idxRow` → select in `.readBody` → `[data-act="peel"]` (focus lands on `.peelField`, correct) → `[data-act="send"]` (focus lands on `button.deskFactLink[data-act="open-task"]`, correct) → `Ctrl+Z`. Result: `document.activeElement === document.body`, live region reads "Taken back. Nothing went to Tasks.", data reverts correctly. The very next Tab lands on `.filingBtn` — the top of the sheet, not where she was. The Tasks comparison in the finding also holds: tick then `Ctrl+Z` gives `{cls:"tick", lane:"done"}` then `{cls:"tick", lane:"todo"}` — focus rides the card back. The mechanism is `doUndo()` at master.html:11101. It claims focus only when `document.activeElement.closest(".undo")` — after a send, focus is on the fact link, not in the strip, so `refocus` is never set and `paint()` drops the caret. The comment above it defends the narrowness ("a stored destination breaks the cross-room case"), so this is a known, deliberate narrowing — but it was reasoned for the search room and never re-checked against the seam, which is the one gesture the whole suite exists to justify. Worse, and not in the finding: the `inStrip` branch it does claim to handle is also broken here. Focus `.undoAct` and press Enter in the same flow and you still land on BODY, because that branch refocuses `phone.matches ? ".phoneField" : ".topField"` and **neither field exists while a note is on the desk** (measured: `{top:false, phone:false}` in the reading state). So both the keyboard route and the strip route strand a keyboard user, and the second one fails silently through a stale selector. Not gate-restatement: verify.mjs §3 asserts the seam's data ("the card is gone from the board", "and gone from the ledger") and never asserts focus after the undo; interaction-check.mjs has no undo assertion at all. This is exactly the class the round notes name as gate-blind. Severity is defect, not blocking: the undo does what it says and announces it, so nothing the product promises fails — but a keyboard operator is put on the floor at the end of the suite's flagship gesture, which at the Linear/Stripe bar is visibly wrong. On the fix: directionally right and it uses the mechanism already in the file (`refocus` consumed by `paint()`, which is "the same frame as the repaint"). Its numbers check out — `.readBody` is `

`, so it is genuinely focusable as a fallback. Two things it under-specifies, corrected below.
confirmed.sharpenedFix:
Do not widen the shared `doUndo()` heuristic — the comment at master.html:11101 correctly names why a stored destination breaks the search room. Instead give `offerUndo(label, undoneLabel, revert)` an optional fourth argument, `home`, that the arming act supplies, and have `doUndo()` use it in this precedence: (1) `home` if the act supplied one and it resolves after the repaint; (2) the existing `inStrip` rule; (3) the current field fallback. Every existing call site that passes no `home` keeps today's behaviour exactly.

Then supply `home` at the two seam call sites:
- notebook branch (master.html:11915): the revert sets `peeling = note.id`, so the element the undo actually brings back is the peel sheet — `home` is `{ kind: "field", sel: ".peelField", end: true }`, matching what `peelWords()` already sets at :11836. `.readBody` is the second fallback, not the first: the peel sheet is on screen after the undo (verified: `peelField:true` post-undo), so sending the caret to the note body skips past the thing that just reappeared.
- review/hand branch (master.html:11881): there is no peel sheet — the revert pops `decided` and returns the card to the queue — so `home` there must be the restored queue card's own control, not `.peelField`.

Fix the stale selector in the same change: the `inStrip` fallback must resolve to a field that exists in the current state, i.e. `.peelField || .topField || .phoneField || .readBody`, or it goes on failing silently in the reading state.
confirmed.breaks:
Plausible breakage, and what to re-measure.

1. The search room is the reason the narrowing exists. Adding a precedence tier rather than a stored default is what keeps it safe, but re-drive `Ctrl/⌘K` → make a change → `Ctrl/⌘Z` and confirm the caret is still in the search field and not on body. That is the case the original comment says a naive fix regresses.

2. `.peelField` is a textarea and `end: true` moves the caret to the end. Confirm the undo does not re-select or scroll the sheet: `paint()` plus `focus({preventScroll:true})` is the existing contract, so check `window.scrollY` and the index scroll offset are unchanged across the undo (they are 0/unchanged today).

3. The 30-second expiry path at :11081 has its own focus rescue that also targets `.topField, .phoneField`. If the `inStrip` selector is corrected, correct that one identically or the two drift apart again — that is precisely how the five exits drifted before `backToNotes()` was centralised.

4. Phone: re-run at 390 in `notes.seam` and `notes.notebook`. `.phoneField` vs `.topField` is a media-query branch and the peel sheet is laid out differently there.

5. Re-run `node gate.mjs` and `node verify.mjs`. Neither should move — no palette, weight, type or geometry is touched — but verify.mjs §3 walks this exact flow and a changed focus target can change what its `revealed.focused` assertion sees two steps later.

6. Add the missing assertion while it is open: after the seam undo, `document.activeElement !== document.body` on both routes (keyboard `Ctrl/⌘Z` and the strip's own button) at 390 and 1440. This defect was invisible to two green gates; without that assertion the next refactor puts it straight back.

confirmed.element: The three sheet heads · .word vs Timeline's footer
confirmed.problem: Tasks and Notes each carry their wordmark at (128,37) on the sheet's own head: 17px, weight 600, Geist, full ink, with the full stop. Timeline carries no head mark at all; its identity is "Signal Timeline" at (1219,851) in the footer — 11px, weight 400, Geist Mono, 62% ink, no full stop, and a two-word suite-form name rather than a lowercase wordmark. Three sheets, three answers to "what am I looking at": two say it at the top in the display voice, one says it at the bottom in the quietest voice in the system. This has never been visible before because the three were never adjacent.
confirmed.consequence: Walking the spine — the gesture the whole suite exists to make cheap — makes the application's own name jump from top-left to bottom-right and change typeface. It is the single loudest signal on the surface that these are three products wearing a shared rail rather than one application.
confirmed.fix: Put a `timeline.` wordmark on the Timeline sheet's head in the same slot and the same token as Tasks and Notes (17px/600 Geist, ink, with the full stop, the accent decision per that lock's own rule). Keep or drop the footer line as a colophon, but it is no longer the identity.
confirmed.assertion: For each of tasks.board, notes.notebook and timeline.desk, the element carrying the product wordmark resolves the same font-family, font-size, font-weight and colour token, and its bounding rect sits within 8px of the same offset from the sheet's top-left corner.
confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED on the source, with one factual correction to the finding's own numbers.

Measured live at 1920 (paper), per state:
- tasks.board: `.word` = "tasks", x=128 y=37, 17px, 600, Geist, rgb(17,17,17).
- notes.notebook: `.word` = "notes", x=**311** y=38, 17px, 600, Geist, rgb(17,17,17). The finding says both sit at (128,37); they do not. Notes' head is inset 183px further in. The two wordmarks share a *role and token*, not a slot — which matters, because the fix's "same slot" instruction is therefore unbuildable as written.
- timeline.owner-flight / .desk / .phone: `[data-app="timeline"] .word` returns **null**. There is no head mark. `bar()` at line 15809 emits `.b-where` (workspace) → `.b-switch` (project + "one of three") → acts, with the wordmark cell simply absent. Tasks' head reads "tasks. | The Orchard, events | …"; Timeline's reads "The Orchard, events | Mara & Finn ONE OF THREE | …". Same object, same order, one cell missing.
- The footer claim checks out: `foot()` at 15781 emits `Signal Timeline` as a plain `<span>` in `.b-foot` — 11px, 400, Geist Mono, rgba(17,17,17,0.62), text-transform none, at x=1699/1700, y=851 (desk) and y=1015 (owner-flight). Two-word suite form, no full stop.

Not already handled, and not a known-and-left: `BUILD-LIST.md` lists seven items and this is none of them; `COMPOSITION.md` §5 defends the two wordmarks' full stops as product-scoped and §7 documents the Timeline mount in detail (including removing the lab caption from the head region) without ever noticing that the head it mounted onto carries no identity. So this was overlooked, not decided.

It also bites a stated non-negotiable rather than taste: the locked Studio Floor architecture in `brief.md:93` says "Identity on the sheet's own head." One of three sheets does not do it. And it is exactly the class this round exists to catch — invisible while the three were separate, obvious the moment the spine walks tasks → notes → timeline and the one anchor naming the sheet vanishes on the third stop.

SEVERITY: **defect**, not misleading. Nothing untrue is asserted — "Signal Timeline" in the colophon is accurate, and the lit capsule tile plus an unmistakably timeline-shaped page mean nobody is ever lost. It is an empty cell in a three-across comparison: visibly wrong, passable. I would rank it at the top of the defect pile, not above the line.

The proposed fix is directionally right but carries two specifics that would break things, corrected in sharpenedFix: "full ink" is wrong for Timeline (it kills the wordmark on the ink twin), and "the accent decision per that lock's own rule" points at a rule that does not exist — the Timeline lock has no wordmark and therefore no full-stop rule to defer to.
confirmed.sharpenedFix:
Put a `timeline.` wordmark in the first cell of Timeline's own head row — `bar()` in `_gate-suite.html:15809`, before `.b-where` — matching Tasks and Notes in role and token, at Timeline's own inset (x≈196, where `.b-where` and the footer's "Kept by Orla" already start), not at Tasks' x=128. There is no shared slot to copy; Notes is at 311 and Tasks at 128.

Four specifics that differ from the finding as written:

confirmed.sharpenedFix:
The fix's scoping sentence — "the divergence that shows is the eyebrow, not the prose" — is the wrong cut. In all three products the caps treatment is a *caps* token, not a *section-label* token, so "route all three products' section labels through it" would leave each product's own siblings behind and manufacture new divergence directly adjacent to the thing being fixed:

- Timeline: `--track-label` (0.16em) is used at 24+ sites across `timeline.css` plus `across.css` — the measure head, but also `.b-layoutBtn` and `.b-grab` sitting on that same head, `.b-foot`, and the day labels. Retracking only `.b-measureHead` leaves the orientation control beside it on a different tracking.
- Tasks: 0.1em is hardcoded (not tokenised) at ~6 sites including `.tag`, the chip that sits on every card directly under `.trayName`. Retrack the tray head alone and the head stops rhyming with the chips beneath it. There is also a fourth Tasks value, 0.14em on `.trayName` under `[data-type="expressive"]` (`tasks.css:1555`), which must move in lockstep or become the new outlier.
- Notes: `--tr-cap` has 8 users including `.peelLabel`, `.darkTag`, `.specName`, and — critically — `.dockAvatar`, where it is *also* the `text-indent` value that optically re-centres the tracked "OR" initials (`notes.css:802`). Change the tracking without changing the indent and the avatar initials sit off-centre.

Corrected fix, in three steps rather than one:
1. Tokenise Tasks first. Its 0.1em is a literal repeated at ~6 sites with no name; give it `--tr-cap` so all three products declare the role before any of them changes value.
2. Declare one suite-level caps token in `shell.css` — one family, one weight, one tracking — and have each product's `--tr-cap`/`--track-label` resolve to it. Route the whole caps role through it, not just the section heads: heads, chips, small buttons, peel and spec labels. Keep Timeline's `--track-labelWide` as the declared ceremonial exception it already is; it is one site with a stated reason and collapsing it would cost the sheet its top line.
3. Pick the value on evidence, not compromise. Geist Mono 400 at 0.100em is the defensible landing: it is already the majority treatment (Tasks and Timeline are both mono; only Notes is not), and 0.100em is the mid value, so nothing has to travel the full 0.085em. `shell.css:205` already hardcodes `0.075em` with the comment "Notes' `--tr-cap`" — that line is the shell having silently adopted one product's value as the suite's, and it is where the token belongs.

Also worth folding in, because it is a strictly worse instance the finding did not reach: `.dockAvatar` is the *same shell object* — the account tile — styled independently per product, Geist 600 at 10px/0.04em in Tasks (`tasks.css:1034`, `:1757`) and 11px/0.075em in Notes (`notes.css:802`). Same object, two sizes and two trackings, in a suite whose stated architecture is one rail rendered once. Fix that in the same pass.

```css

   across the full width of the words above the final moment. On this
   axis the item is a zero-width position, so the same declaration
   resolves to a 27px orphan floating above the track. The horizontal
   measure names its far end with the moment's own weight. */
[data-app="timeline"] .b-measure[data-across="true"] .b-item[data-anchor="true"]::before { content: none; }
```
