confirmed.seat: UX and information design — Orla, venue manager at The Orchard
confirmed.element: the shared fixture — Notes subject head + Tasks card copy vs Timeline hero and terminus
confirmed.problem: The same couple carries two irreconcilable dates across the suite. Notes' head is a button reading "Mara & Finn · Saturday 18 July, in 2 days", its index groups Mara & Finn under that date, and the note itself says "Saturday wedding, Mara & Finn. Ceremony 2pm in the orchard… Confirm marquee sides with the hire company by Thursday." Tasks has "Build the Saturday run-sheet — Ceremony 2pm orchard, drinks terrace, dinner 5.30pm" due Today, and "Confirm marquee sides… they need the call by Thursday." Timeline, one click away on the same spine, renders MARA & FINN / 79 / days / Saturday 3 October 2026 / Wedding day, with their menu tasting placed 16 days out — which Notes independently confirms is 1 August, i.e. two weeks AFTER the wedding Notes and Tasks are running. The three couples in the fixture (Mara & Finn, Nora & Cian, Aisling & Tom) match Timeline's "ONE OF THREE", so this is one couple with two weddings, not two couples. The same slot in each sheet head compounds it: bold "Mara & Finn" in Notes means "your next event", bold "Mara & Finn" in Timeline means "the timeline you are reading" — identical type, identical position, different meaning, different date.
confirmed.consequence: Orla runs weddings for a living and the one number she cannot be wrong about is which Saturday. The application tells her, on two screens one keystroke apart, that the same wedding is in two days and in seventy-nine. Acting on either screen alone she either builds a run-sheet eleven weeks early or misses a wedding on Saturday. It also spends the credibility of the whole product: once she catches this, no count on any of the three surfaces is trustworthy, and "one world of data underneath all three" — the only reason the suite exists rather than three apps — is disproved by the artefact itself.
confirmed.fix: Give a cast member exactly one headline date, held once, and have all three products read it through a single accessor rather than each fixture stating its own. Cheapest true resolution: move Timeline's 79-day approach onto Nora & Cian or Aisling & Tom (both already on the board with autumn/spring work and neither with a fixed date elsewhere), leaving Mara & Finn as the Saturday couple that Notes and Tasks are running. If Mara & Finn must stay the Timeline subject, move their wedding to Sat 3 Oct in Notes and Tasks and rewrite the four card and note strings that assert "Saturday", "Today" and "by Thursday".
confirmed.assertion: A gate opens the suite once and, for every named cast member, resolves the headline date asserted by (a) the Notes subject-group head, (b) any Tasks card whose copy names a day for that cast member, and (c) the Timeline terminus for that subject, and fails on any pair that does not resolve to the same ISO date. It also fails if any moment on a cast member's Timeline falls after that cast member's headline date.
confirmed.verdict:
The problem is exact and I confirmed every string by driving the master, not by reading frames. Notes' subject head renders "Mara & Finn / Saturday 18 July, in 2 days" and its index groups under the same; Tasks renders "Build the Saturday run-sheet / Due Today / Ceremony 2pm orchard, drinks terrace, dinner 5.30pm / Mara & Finn"; Timeline renders "MARA & FINN / 79 / days / Saturday 3 October 2026 / Wedding day". All three carry the same clock (WORLD.today "2026-07-16", "TODAY IS 16 JULY", "Thu 16 Jul", "Thursday 16 July, today"). One couple, one clock, two wedding days, one click apart on the same spine.

It is worse than the seat states, and the fixture itself is the witness. src/fixture.js's header declares "Three products, one venue, one cast, one day" and promises "a suite that quietly starts disagreeing with itself fails at load rather than in front of somebody." The join at the footer asserts today, workspace, operator, the milestone titles and dates, the six-note-to-six-task link — and `agree("Timeline's project", T.project.name, WORLD.project)` plus `agree("Notes' project", N.project, WORLD.project)`, i.e. it asserts the two products are about the SAME project and then never asserts that project's date. The one fact the guard was built to catch is the one hole in it. So the artefact asserts something untrue on its largest number, and separately asserts a guarantee about itself that is false.

Not blocking, and I correct it down if the seat filed it there: every mechanism does what it says. The seam works end to end, the spine never rebuilds, the measure computes real distances, both orientations draw. Nothing is broken; the world is untrue. That is the definition of misleading, and it sits at the top of that class — this is the single most prominent number in Timeline contradicting the subject head of Notes.

THE PROPOSED FIX IS REFUTED ON ITS PREFERRED BRANCH, on the fixture's own strings. "Move Timeline's 79-day approach onto Nora & Cian or Aisling & Tom (both already on the board ... neither with a fixed date elsewhere)" is factually wrong twice. Nora & Cian DO have a fixed date elsewhere: SIBLINGS gives them "2027-04-17", and tasks.dense gives them "Book the tasting date for Nora & Cian" and "Check the spring menu against the new supplier list" — spring 2027, not autumn 2026, and no tasting date yet, against a Timeline whose tasting is covered ground. Aisling & Tom carry date: null, "At the start of its planning", "Pencil the autumn date in the diary", "Tom's guest number, before we hold the room" and "First call with Aisling & Tom" completed 8 July — a couple whose room is not yet held cannot be the subject of a nine-milestone approach with "The Orchard reserved" already covered on 18 April and a wedding day fixed to the day. Both named targets contradict themselves the moment they are moved.

Worse, that branch strands the one thing all three products already agree on. The menu tasting is Mara & Finn's in Notes ("Mara & Finn's menu tasting ... booked for 1 August"), Mara & Finn's in Tasks (demo-t-02, tag "Mara & Finn", "Milestone due 1 Aug"), and Timeline's demo-audience-item-menu at 2026-08-01 — and B.planning.milestones is joined to T.milestones BY TITLE at load. Move the Timeline to another couple and the same milestone belongs to two couples at once: the contradiction is not resolved, it is relocated into the one cross-product join the guard actually checks.

That also settles the direction. Since 1 August is agreed by all three and a tasting precedes a wedding, and since neither sibling can host either date, Mara & Finn's one wedding must be 3 October. Timeline is right; the July urgency in Notes and Tasks is what has to move. The seat's fallback branch is therefore the correct direction, but "four card and note strings" is the wrong count — it is nine or ten, plus SUBJECTS.when/days, plus dueAt/dueTone, plus the derived head counts, plus "Send registrar paperwork two weeks before the date" completed 2 July, which is exactly two weeks before the 16th and becomes false.
confirmed.sharpenedFix:
Hold the wedding once and derive everything, then re-cast the urgency rather than re-dating it.

1. WORLD gains `wedding: { couple: "Mara & Finn", date: "2026-10-03" }` next to `today`. Notes' `SUBJECTS["mara-finn"].when` and `.days` derive from it via the existing formatter; Timeline's `PROJECT.primaryDate.date` is read from it rather than restated. Extend the footer join with `agree("the wedding day", T.project.primaryDate.date, WORLD.wedding.date)` and a check that no task or note tagged with the couple asserts a date after it. That closes the hole the header already claims is closed, and it is the seat's own stated principle — one headline date, held once, read through a single accessor. Keep this part; it is right.

2. Do NOT move the Timeline to a sibling. Do NOT re-date Notes and Tasks to October wholesale either — that costs "in 2 days", "Due today" and stake 1, which is the composition Notes' subject ordering and Tasks' board head were built on, and it leaves the venue running nothing this week, which is a duller and less honest world.

3. Instead move the imminent Saturday off the couple and onto the venue's own event, which the fixture already contains. demo-t-03 "Reprint the faded welcome sign before the open day" and demo-t-09 "Open day, nine couples through" establish it. Re-cast demo-t-05 as the run-sheet for the Saturday open day, tag "Venue", keeping `due: "Due today"`, `dueAt: "2026-07-16"`, `dueTone: "today"` untouched — the head's "1 today" survives byte-identical. Re-word its note off "Ceremony 2pm orchard" onto the open-day sequence.

4. Re-word the four remaining July-wedding assertions so they are true 79 days out: Notes n01 (drop "Saturday wedding" and "Ceremony 2pm in the orchard"; make the marquee a booking deadline with the hire company, which "they need the call by Thursday" already supports); Notes n03 ("8am on the Saturday" → 8am on the day); Tasks demo-t-01's note ("Mara & Finn, Saturday" → the booking deadline); demo_task_registrar ("two weeks before the date" is false at 79 days — make it the registrar paperwork filed, or move `completedAt`). demo-t-07 seating plan and demo-t-02 tasting need no change; both are true at 79 days.

5. Notes' `SUBJECTS["mara-finn"].stake` stays 1 — it is still the day the venue is running, just further out — but confirm the group order the index opens on is still the intended one now that `days` is 79 rather than 2, because the ordering comment says stake beats proximity and this is the first time that rule is tested with a large number.

Cost: one WORLD key, one derivation, one added assertion, and roughly nine fixture strings. No layout, palette, type or architecture change. Half a day of work and half a day of re-freezing.
confirmed.breaks:

confirmed.seat: UX and information design — Orla, venue manager at The Orchard
confirmed.element: .rail — the floating capsule spine, arrow-key roving model
confirmed.problem: Every rail tile except the one for the current product is tabindex="-1", so the arrow keys are the only keyboard route to the other two products and to Home, Inbox, Help and the account tile. That rover steps two tiles per press. Driven at 1440: from Tasks, one ArrowDown lands on Inbox (skipping Timeline); the full walk cycles Tasks → Inbox → account → Home → Tasks forever and never lands on Notes or Timeline at all. From Notes, ArrowDown lands on Timeline, skipping Tasks. From Timeline it lands on Help, skipping Inbox. ArrowUp has the same parity in reverse, so the tiles reachable going down and going up are disjoint sets. At 390, where the capsule and the dock are the same object, ArrowRight from Tasks moves once to Timeline and then does nothing on every subsequent press — five presses, no movement.
confirmed.consequence: A keyboard-only Orla cannot leave the product she is in. The spine is the object the entire suite argument rests on — "one rail, rendered once, three products mounted at once" — and by keyboard it reaches one of the three. On a phone it dead-ends after a single press. The four honest doors are stranded with it: from Tasks, Help and the studio mark cannot be reached by any input other than a mouse, which quietly withdraws the "present, reachable, in the tab order" claim the doors were designed to make.
confirmed.fix: Bind the rover's key handling once. The two-tile step is a handler firing on two events (keydown and keypress, or on both the rail and the tile) — remove the duplicate, and rebuild the enabled-tile list from the tiles actually rendered at the current width so the 390 dock's list is not the desk's. Give the walk Home/End and wrap-around, and keep the disabled doors in the walk so they stay reachable and can speak their sentence.
confirmed.assertion: From every rail tile, at 1440 and at 390, one ArrowDown/ArrowRight press moves the rover to the immediately adjacent visible tile and no further; walking the rail in one direction visits every visible tile exactly once before returning to the start; and from each of the three product tiles, both other product tiles are reachable in that walk.
confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED by driving, with two of the seat's five traces corrected. Reproduced verbatim at 1440 on tasks.board: rail DOM order is mark home notes tasks timeline inbox help add me; from the tasks tile one ArrowDown lands on inbox, and the walk cycles tasks -> inbox -> me -> home -> tasks forever, never touching notes or timeline. Reproduced verbatim at 390: ArrowRight from tasks moves once to timeline and then does nothing on nine further presses. Every tile but the current one is tabindex="-1" (railHtml, _gate-suite.html:7690), so the arrows are the only keyboard route to Home, Inbox, Help, the mark and the account tile — and the arrows do not work. That breaks the non-negotiable that the honest doors are "present, reachable, in the tab order", so blocking is the right class, not overstated.

Two of the seat's traces are wrong and one diagnosis is wrong. From Notes at 1440 (notes.notebook and notes.seam) ArrowDown does NOT land on Timeline — the first press ejects focus out of the spine entirely into .idxRow and it never comes back, while the roving stop is left on "tasks"; that is worse than reported. From Timeline at 1440 ArrowDown lands on inbox, then help, then sticks on help permanently — it does not skip inbox. And the double step is not "keydown and keypress, or the rail and the tile": I traced it. One keydown, two focus() calls — the suite rover at _gate-suite.html:7967 moves tasks->timeline, then Tasks' generic groupKeys at :8389, reached from onKey at :9791 via the document listener at :10768, moves timeline->inbox because event.target.closest("[data-group]") matches <nav class="rail" data-group="rail">. That is why the double step happens only while Tasks is the active product, which is exactly why the seat's Notes and Timeline traces came out wrong. The Home/End and wrap-around clause of the fix is already implemented (:7959-7961, Home, End, and % keys.length both ways) and the disabled doors are already in the walk, so half the proposed fix is a no-op. The fix's one load-bearing clause — rebuild the list from what is actually rendered — is correct and is the real cause of both dead ends: [data-rail="add"] is display:none at >=721 and mark/inbox/help have zero boxes at 390, so focus() no-ops while tabindex="0" is parked on an unfocusable node.

This is not a gate restatement. verify.mjs:512-518 presses ArrowDown three times and asserts only that three distinct tiles were hit; the broken double-stepping walk satisfies that. The gate is blind here, which is a finding in itself.

The **identical move by mouse is fully reversible**: I dragged the same card to Review and got the strip "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company moved to Review · Undo · Ctrl Z", and Ctrl+Z put it back with "…is back in the to do column." That path builds a complete receipt at `:10278-10305`, carrying `wasHeldSince` and `wasCompletedAt`, under a comment that says in so many words "A drop is the most mis-fireable gesture on a pointer board and had no way back; only a keyboard-carried card had Escape." The pointer route was paid for and the keyboard route was left behind — so the same act on the same card is reversible with a mouse and not with a keyboard, and the file already contains the exact receipt the keyboard branch needs.

(b) Confirmed verbatim. From `state=notes.seam`, press Send → the Notes strip reads "Sent to Tasks. · Undo · Ctrl+Z · for 30 seconds" (`UNDO_SECONDS = 30` at `:11058`, ticking at `:11080-11086`). The decision does not license the announcement.

Severity: **misleading**, not blocking. The seat's line "the board's most consequential action is irreversible" overstates — a pointer drag is reversible, and Escape cancels a keyboard carry mid-flight (`:9830-9840`). What is actually wrong is that the product asserts something untrue: "Nothing left to undo." spoken while a 30-second window is open and advertising that exact keystroke one product away, and spoken immediately after a move the operator just made by the only route a keyboard user has.

On the proposed fix: the direction is right and the last clause ("never emit 'Nothing left to undo' while a window is open") is exactly right and nearly free. But "make the undo stack an application-level stack" as literally written is a rearchitecture of three separately ratified undo models and I would not ship it as stated. It silently drops Timeline, which has its own `Ctrl/⌘Z` (`:16649`) and its own `.b-undo` bar with a rendered empty state — unifying two of three products makes the suite less of a system, not more. It does not reconcile two incompatible retention models: Tasks keeps a 10-deep `history` whose record deliberately outlives its 6-second strip (`:9494-9500`, "The strip retires; the record does not"), while Notes hard-expires at 30s and `doUndo()` then returns false. Most dangerous: a single global Ctrl+Z owner has to re-derive Notes' typing guard at `:14192-14203`, which is the file's own paid-for scar — intercepting Ctrl+Z over a live draft "reverted the previously saved note and overwrote the draft the person was in the middle of writing". The expiry path in the same file handles exactly this case correctly (:11088–11104); the undo path does not.
confirmed.consequence: The seam's own reversal — the single act the whole suite argument rests on being safe — is the one that loses the keyboard. A person takes back a send and is silently returned to the top of the document, then has to Tab back through the desk to find where they were.
confirmed.fix: Extend the `inStrip` test in `doUndo()` (:11123) to also claim focus when the active element is inside the region the revert is about to remove, and point the refocus at the ledger row or the note the undo restored — the same shape the expiry path already uses.
confirmed.assertion: After a completed seam send followed by Ctrl+Z, `document.activeElement` is not `document.body` and is a descendant of the Notes app; assert the same for the undo strip's Undo button, the tick path on Tasks, and the Timeline stepper path.

Driven at 768, 1280 and 1920, mouse and keyboard alike: after `Send to Tasks` activeElement is `BUTTON.deskFactLink`; after Ctrl+Z it is `BODY`; the first Tab lands on `BUTTON.filingBtn` (`data-act="refile"`) and the second on `.peelField`. The seat's measurement is exact, down to `.filingBtn`. Not covered by the gate — `interaction-check.mjs` has one `activeElement` assertion (:178, `.thing`) and nothing on undo focus. It is also the only one of the eleven `offerUndo` call sites whose refocus target is a node its own revert deletes (save, edit-save, refile, rejoin, drop, voice-discard, voice-keep all refocus at controls that survive), so it is a real hole rather than a general property. Severity is `defect`, not blocking: undo does what it advertises — the card leaves the board, `uncross` fires, the live region reads "Taken back. Nothing went to Tasks." — and the person is two Tabs from where they were. But it breaks the contract `doUndo()` writes down in its own comment, on the one gesture the suite exists to justify, and the expiry path eleven lines above handles the identical case. The proposed fix's mechanism is right and its destinations are wrong, corrected in sharpenedFix: the "ledger row" is exactly what `CROSSED.shift()` removes inside the revert, so it does not exist to receive focus; and "the same shape the expiry path already uses" is `.idxRow[data-cursor] || .topField/.phoneField`, a cross-room destination that would eject a person from the desk they are still standing on — the precise failure the `doUndo` comment warns against. After `revert()`, replace the single `inStrip` branch with two: (1) unchanged — `was && was.closest(".undo")` keeps the existing field destination; (2) new — `was && was.closest('[data-act="open-task"]')` sets `refocus = { kind: "act", sel: '[data-act="send"]' }`. Do not use a generic "is the active element in the region the revert will remove" test — `revert` is an opaque closure and no region is knowable before it runs; the checkable fact is the one link. refuted.problem: The word-safe trim targets the full column width rather than a measure, so a note line runs 128 characters at 1280, 149 at 1440 and up to 170 at 1920 — widest painted line 1,146px at 15px/1.45. At 768 the same rows sit at ~55 characters, which is correct, so the measure was right and was given away above 768. Confirmed live by resizing: 1920→1280→1920→768 returns 155/130/155/55 characters, i.e. the trim is idempotent and correctly re-runs, and is faithfully producing an oversize line.
refuted.why:
The measurements are right and the conclusion is wrong. Driven at file://.../_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=notes.notebook, resizing 1920→1280→1920→1440→768: the .idxText column is 1153/875/1153/1035/397px, widest painted run 1146px at 170 chars (1920), 1029/154 (1440), 875/136 (1280), 397/51-60 (768). The trim is idempotent and re-runs. So the observation is confirmed; what is refuted is that a measure was "given away above 768".

Three reasons.

1. The central inference is factually wrong. `--stack: min(100%, 1440px)` (_gate-suite.html:2411). At 768 nothing caps the index — 100% of the window minus rail, sheet inset and 30px gutters resolves to 397px. The ~55 characters there is a consequence of a small window, not the residue of a 55-character measure that a wider window discarded. There was never a measure on this column to lose.

2. The decision is documented and argued, not overlooked. _gate-suite.html:2394-2410 states it explicitly: `--measure` (31em, calibrated in em precisely because Geist's average glyph is ~0.45em and `ch` is not that) caps every surface carrying prose — .readBody, .readLong, .darkNote, .handBody, .saidHead all take `max-width: var(--measure)`. `--stack` governs the INDEX, "whose rows are scan lines rather than prose, and every pixel of width there is another few words of a person's own note visible before the ellipsis." That is the right distinction. Measure exists to protect the eye's return sweep across multiple lines; a one-line list row has no return sweep. Against the named benchmarks it is also standard: a Linear issue row and a Gmail subject+snippet both run the full window and truncate at the container. And the width is doing visible work here — at 1920 four of the first four rows render at 155/155, 143/143, 128/128 characters, i.e. the whole preview, untrimmed, which is exactly the payoff the comment claims.

3. The fix's numbers are wrong by its own stated goal, and it regresses a documented decision. Measured in-page: Geist's "0" at 15px with --tr-14 is 9.77px, so 68ch = 664px, not "≈640px"; and this text averages 6.74px/glyph (1146px/170ch), so 664px paints ~98 characters, not 68. The fix asks for 68 and specifies a width that gives ~98 — and it reaches for `ch`, the unit the source already reasoned past in writing. Worse, moving .idxTag/.idxWhen off the row's right edge breaks the rule at :2955 ("The metadata columns are fixed, so the right-hand verticals hold down the whole index instead of stepping in and out"); "a constant distance from the last word" makes the tag and date columns ragged per row and destroys the vertical scan. Even read charitably as a fixed 664px+gap offset, it parks ~640px of dead white inside the index at 1920 — the 45% white sheet this round was convened to remove — while `.idxRow { width: calc(100% + 20px) }` and the `left:10px; right:10px` hairline keep painting the full 1400px, so every hover, `[data-cursor]` wash and search-hit ring becomes a 1400px band with 700px of nothing in it.

Severity, had it been real, would be refinement at most: the surface asserts nothing untrue and does what it says. The one grain worth keeping is not a measure problem — at 1920 the gap between a short row's last word and its tag runs to 378px (13-100px at 1280), so the meta pairs weakly with its own row on the shortest rows. That is a composition note, not a lost measure, and it does not justify this fix.

refuted.problem: Tasks carries a reversed-type letterfit rule and applies it exactly: `.late` 12/600 goes −0.006em → +0.002em, the overdue `.when` 11/600 goes normal → +0.008em, `Add task` 13/600 goes −0.010em → −0.002em. Three tokens, all a +0.008em delta — an unambiguous declared rule. Notes and Timeline apply 0.000em: 'Go through 8' stays −0.006em on ink, 'Cancel' −0.012em, `Esc` −0.016em, and the person's own dictated words at 27px stay at −0.034em white on #111. Flipping to `v=ink` moves not one value in Notes or Timeline while Tasks' five compensated tokens are the only type in the application that adapts.
refuted.why:
The seat's Tasks facts are exactly right and I confirmed every one by driving the file at 1440. `--tr-rev: 0.008em` is declared at `_gate-suite.html:557` INSIDE the `[data-app="tasks"] {` block that opens at line 512, so it is literally a Tasks-private token; it is spent five times (lines 1151, 1155, 1158, 1159, 1686) and computed letterfit confirms `.late` +0.0020em, overdue `.when` +0.0080em, `Add task` −0.0020em. Notes and Timeline spend it zero times. I dumped every visible text node in Timeline under `v=ink` and `v=paper`: all 28 role/size/weight groups carry byte-identical tracking on both grounds — not one value moves when the ground inverts, and Timeline has an elaborate nine-line `--fore/--back` polarity ladder (lines 4188–4213) that handles alpha and has no tracking branch. So the observation is true.

It is refuted on three counts: the rule is misread, the severity is inflated by roughly an order of magnitude, and the fix is wrong in four separately checkable ways — including one that would silently defeat the audit.

MISREAD RULE. The finding calls this "an unambiguous declared rule" and generalises it to "wherever composited foreground luminance exceeds background luminance." That is not what Tasks declares. The source says the opposite in its own comments: line 1152, "The reversed branch belongs to the filled chip only. The outlined 'N today'…"; line 1156, "The idle dock paints ink on wash, which is not reversed out." I enumerated every light-on-dark text node in `tasks.board`: the five compensated tokens are 10–13px and ALL are weight 600, while `.railAvatar` (11px/600, white on the ink floor, `_gate-suite.html:366`) sits at the ceremonial 0.075em and is deliberately not compensated. Tasks' actual rule is *small bold reversed fills*, not *all reversed type*. Extending it to 27px/400 display and to a 148px numeral is a new and larger rule invented in the fix, not a promotion of an existing one.

INFLATED SEVERITY. The one genuinely like-for-like case is Notes' `.chip` (line 2533: `background: var(--ink); color: var(--white); font-size: var(--t-12); font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: var(--tr-12)`) against Tasks' `.late:not([data-soft])` — the same 12px/600 white-on-filled-ink pill, one at −0.006em and one at +0.002em. The entire delta is 0.096px per glyph; across "Go through 8" that is 1.15px of total width. Nothing is visible and nothing is asserted untrue to Orla. This is system coherence, i.e. refinement, and the finding's rhetoric ("the person's own dictated words… stay at −0.034em white on #111") dresses a tenth of a pixel per letter as a failure.

WRONG FIX, four ways.
1. It compensates a button that is not reversed. `.darkAct[data-primary]` ("Stop and read it back") is `background: var(--white); color: var(--ink)` (line 3197) and inherits letter-spacing from `.darkAct`. Moving `.darkAct` −0.012em → −0.004em loosens ink-on-white type — precisely the mistake Tasks' line 1156 comment records itself avoiding. The fix breaks the rule it claims to generalise, in the first place it lands.
2. Its kbd numbers are self-inconsistent and unimplementable as written. `.darkAct kbd` (line 3195) authors no letter-spacing; `font: inherit` does not carry it, so the cap inherits the computed −0.18px from `.darkAct`, which at 11px is −0.0164em. There is no −0.016em token to change. And if you also apply the fix's own `.darkAct` −0.012em → −0.004em, the inherited cap lands at −0.0055em, not the −0.008em the fix specifies. The two instructions contradict each other.
3. A flat em delta is the wrong shape for the effect. Irradiation compensation is size-inverse — it is real at 11–13px and gone by 24px — but an em delta grows with size. +0.008em is +0.088px/glyph on the overdue chip and +0.216px/glyph on `.darkSaid` at 27px, ~8px of added width across the one sentence the dictation surface exists to show; "every Timeline sans token" would put +1.18px per glyph into the 148px count that is tracked −0.05em on purpose. It loosens hardest exactly where the effect is weakest.
4. The token name would defeat the gate. `audit.mjs:179` builds the gated ladder as `ladder("--track-")` — it scrapes every custom property whose name starts `--track-` and treats its value as a permitted tracking VALUE, then tests `Math.abs(em * size - spaceNow) < 0.02`. Declaring `--track-reversed: 0.008em` as the fix instructs would enter 0.008em onto the ladder and legalise +0.008em at every size, in all three products, on both grounds — permanently widening the one letterfit check that is actually automated, in the name of tightening the system.

refuted.problem: One device, two typefaces, two weights, four letterfits. Tasks `.trayName` and `.tag`: Geist Mono 11px/400/+0.100em. Timeline `.b-todayLabel`, `.b-measureHead`, `.b-behindLabel`, ACROSS/DOWN: Geist Mono 11px/400/+0.160em, and `.b-who` at Geist Mono 12px/400/+0.200em. Notes FILING UNDER, OTHER WAYS IN, YOUR NOTES, TURN THIS INTO A TASK, THE TASK WORDING, ALREADY IN TASKS, LISTENING: Geist **sans** 11–12px/**600**/+0.075em. Notes uses no Geist Mono anywhere, in any state, at any width.
refuted.why:
The PROBLEM is real and the numbers are right. Measured at runtime across all eight states: Notes returns **zero** Geist Mono elements in notebook, seam and voice at 390/768/1280/1440/1920 — every uppercase caption is Geist sans, 11px, weight 600, letter-spacing 0.825px (`--tr-cap: 0.075em`). Tasks' `.trayName`/`.tag` are Geist Mono 11px/400/1.1px (0.1em, hard-coded at _gate-suite.html:908 and :1180 under a comment claiming "Every micro-label in the product is one rule"). Timeline's `.b-todayLabel`/`.b-measureHead`/`.b-behindLabel`/ACROSS/DOWN are Geist Mono 11px/400/1.76px (`--track-label: 0.16em`, :4078) and `.b-who` is 12px/400/2.4px (`--track-labelWide: 0.20em`, :4079). So one device, two families, two weights, three fits — and family+weight is a different device, not a rounding difference the round notes' "three tracking curves" question already covers. It is invisible to every gate. Severity is **defect**, not higher: only one product is on screen at a time, so nothing is asserted untrue and nothing fails to work.

The FIX is wrong on three counts, which is why this is refuted.

1. **It undercounts its own blast radius by ~4x.** "Timeline's five" is actually 21 consumers of `var(--track-label)` — including `.b-layoutBtn` (the orientation control, this round's largest new surface), `.b-behindCount`, `.b-behindSummary::after` (the +/− mark), `.b-terminusWhat` (new `across` surface) and `.b-press .b-who`. "Notes' seven labels" is 7 consumers of `var(--tr-cap)`, one of which is `.dockAvatar` (:3057) — avatar initials, not a micro-label, whose optical centring is `text-indent: var(--tr-cap)`, so retargeting the token silently decentres the disc. Notes also has uppercase captions the finding never names ("How it arrived", "What it is about", "Length" on the seam) and `.headKbd`, a keycap.

2. **It measurably breaks the protected object.** I applied the proposed fix in-browser across five widths. At 390 on `notes.seam`, `.indexHead` "ALREADY IN TASKS" wraps: height 25px → 49px. That is the seam sheet at the phone width — the one gesture the suite exists to argue for.

3. **It flattens a hierarchy step a prior round paid for.** `--size-labelWide` is declared in-file as "the ceremonial top line, and only that", and `.b-press .b-who` (:4473) was deliberately stepped DOWN from labelWide to label in an earlier round to mark a section head as distinct from a top line. Collapsing `.b-who` onto the micro-label token abolishes that step and demotes MARA & FINN — the one owner-written string on Timeline's head — to the setting of DAYS AWAY. The Timeline half reflows cleanly otherwise (I tested both orientations × three states × four widths: only `.b-who` height moves, 17px → 15px), so the cost there is semantic, not geometric.

There is also a recorded-decision cost the finding misses: the shell already ran this reconciliation four times and wrote it down. `.railAvatar` (:358) hard-codes 11px / 600 / +0.075em with the comment "the spine takes **Notes'** disc… Recorded in COMPOSITION.md", and `#deck .word` took the **Tasks** tracking. Abolishing Notes' 600/+0.075em register outright orphans a decision COMPOSITION.md still asserts.

refuted.problem: The same fact is set in two typefaces one spine-click apart. Tasks paints the menu tasting's date as '1 Aug' in Geist sans 11px; Timeline paints the same moment as 'Sat 1 Aug' in Geist Mono 11px/+0.040em; Notes paints 'Saturday 18 July, in 2 days' in Geist sans 13px. The same split hits identity: the literal string 'The Orchard, events' is Geist sans 20px/600 in the Tasks head, Geist sans 15px/400 in the Notes head, and Geist **Mono** 11px/+0.040em in the Timeline head.
refuted.why:
REFUTED. The observation is partly true but loosely stated, and the fix is wrong on numbers, wrong on role, and self-defeating.

FACTS, driven at 1920 (computed styles, not frames). Tasks `.when` is Geist 11px but **600**, not 400, and the visible chip is not "1 Aug" — it reads "Milestone 1 Aug" / "Due Today" / "Overdue, due 14 Jul". Notes `.dateStamp` is Geist 13px/400/-0.012em. Timeline `.b-date` is Geist Mono 11px/400/+0.04em, sentence case. `.b-where` is mono 11px/+0.04em. Tasks `.headName` 20px/600; Notes `.headName` 15px/400. So the family split is real; the "same fact, same string, two typefaces" framing is not — three different strings doing three different jobs (a severity chip whose payload includes a date; a date register with a relative count; a reading off a distance instrument).

THE FIX BREAKS ITS OWN CASE. `.b-date` is one of six elements in a single ratified register at `_gate-suite.html:6015` — `.b-date, .b-behindDate, .b-behindCount, .b-unit, .b-origin, .b-where` — created by a confirmed round-6 fix ("twenty-seven of the thirty-two uppercase strings ... were one typographic object"). `.b-behindDate` is built from the **identical formatter** as `.b-date` (`F.fmt.weekdayShort(item.date) + " " + F.fmt.short(item.date)`, lines 15180 and 15668), and `.b-origin` renders "Today, 16 July" at the identical spec, on the same screen, 106px below `.b-date` in timeline.owner-flight. Moving `.b-date` to sans and leaving those two in mono puts the same string form in two families inside one product — the finding's own stated defect, manufactured at closer range.

THE NUMBERS ARE WRONG. Timeline's tracking ladder is declared as six steps with the comment "Six steps and no seventh" (`--track-label` .16, `--track-labelWide` .20, `--track-data` .04, `--track-body` -.015, `--track-head` -.03, plus display/title steps). **-0.004em is not on it.** The Timeline elevate audit builds `TRACK = ladder("--track-")` straight from the stylesheet and fails anything further than 0.02px from a declared step; -0.004em at 11px is -0.044px, and the nearest declared value (-0.015em → -0.165px) is 0.12px away. That is a `trackingLadder` failure on a gate the round notes report as zero. Worse, 11px in Timeline is bound to mono **by role in two ladders**: `--size-label: 0.6875rem /* mono micro-labels · 11px */` and `--lead-label: 1.4 /* mono micro-labels and single-line controls */`. A sans 11px has no declared role at all, so the fix silently invents a seventh tracking step and a new size/leading role.

AND IT MAKES THE BAR WORSE. `.b-where` at 15px/-0.015em sans lands byte-identical to `.b-act` (15px/400/-0.015em — three of them sit in that same bar) and one weight step from `.b-switch` (15px/600). The ratified reading of that bar is "the place, then the project, then the actions" (comment at 5073, which records fixing exactly this: `.b-where` once "sat beside three real buttons drawn identically, so the bar read as four controls of which one was dead"). Flattening the place to the project's and the buttons' size walks that back.

SEVERITY. Nothing here is untrue and nothing fails to work; each product's register is internally consistent and the three never co-occur. This is a refinement, not a defect — and the half of it worth acting on is not the typeface.

refuted.problem: Between 1024 and 1280 the above-line labels break onto three baselines. Measured tops at 1280: 543 / 649 / 671. 'Final guest numbers' is lifted ~128px clear of its neighbours and joined to its tick by a long hairline leader, and its day-count '51' then sits ~250px from the measure where 16, 37 and 79 sit ~55px from it. The same three-tier break occurs at 1024 and 1100. At 1440 and 1920 the row is correct — two tops, 521 and 543, which is only the 22px that bottom-aligns a two-line title, and that part is well done.
refuted.why:
The primary observation reproduces exactly, but the finding misreads half its own evidence and the fix would make the artefact worse, so it is refuted with a corrected fix.

VERIFIED, driven at 900/1024/1100/1280/1440/1920 on `?state=timeline.owner-flight&layout=across`. Title tops at 1280: 649 / 671 / 543 above the rule — the finding's three numbers are right to the pixel. At 1440 and 1920: 521 / 543. `--step` is 128px at every width, and "Final guest numbers" (away=51) is the only item that takes `data-rank="1"`.

WHAT THE FINDING GETS RIGHT, and gets right for a better reason than it states. The rank is assigned in `placeAcross` (_gate-suite.html:15368) by testing a CONSTANT `ACROSS_LABEL = 168` box, not the label's ink. At 1280 (px=12.18) the rank-0 boxes for day 37 and day 51 land 2.5px apart, fails the `+14` gutter, so day 51 is thrown a whole rank out. But the actual rendered ink is 90–135px wide, never 168: at 1280 "Final dress fitting" ends at x=707.8 and "Final guest numbers" begins at x=753.4 — 45.6px of clear air on a single baseline. The lift is decluttering against a phantom collision. That part is a real defect and worth fixing.

WHERE IT IS FACTUALLY WRONG. (a) "The same three-tier break occurs at 1024 and 1100" is presented as the same defect; it is not. At 1024 the two above-line labels have 0.2px of ink air on one baseline (centre gap 125.1px vs 124.9px of combined ink half-widths) — they literally touch. At 1100 it is 13.7px. At those two widths the stagger is the mechanism working correctly, and the finding's own remedy is impossible there. Only 1280 is unearned. (b) The secondary figures are wrong: the lifted "51" sits 154px from the rule (bottom-to-rule), not ~250px, and 16/37/79 sit 26px from it, not ~55px. (c) "reserve the tallest group's height in real layout" is already handled — `measureEl.style.height = above + below` with `--step` measured from the tallest `.b-away`/`.b-copy` actually rendered and `--rule-y` set from `deepest` per side.

WHY THE FIX IS WRONG. "One baseline each at every width, and spill into the scroller when a row cannot fit" inverts the trade. `data-scrolls` is not a ≤900 width rule; it fires when `span > usable`, i.e. when the 8px/day `ACROSS_FLOOR` bites. To buy 14px of gutter between day 37 and day 51 at 1024 you need px ≥ 9.92, span ≥ 784 against usable 714 — so the fix puts a horizontal scrollbar under 1024 and 1100 on compositions that currently fit. That destroys the stated premise of the orientation ("the whole approach is one object... the horizon never moves because the whole approach is in frame") to remove a stagger the surface uses deliberately, with a stem drawn precisely so a stepped label is never orphaned. Trading the in-frame guarantee for a flat row is a net loss.

SEVERITY. Defect, not worse. Nothing is asserted untrue: the stem and the travelling `.b-away` figure keep ownership of "51" unambiguous, and it is confined to a 1024–1280 band. But at 1280 one label floating a full 128px clear on a hairline leader while its neighbours sit in a tidy row is visibly below the Linear/Stripe bar, so it is not mere refinement either.

refuted.problem: Same element, same size (11px), same weight (600), same radius (4px), same padding (1px 5px), three typographic settings: `.headKbd` carries `text-transform: uppercase` and +0.075em and paints **CTRL ↓**; the dock's search hint is sentence case at −0.014em and paints **Ctrl K**; the dictation overlay's are sentence case at −0.016em and paint **Esc** and **Ctrl+Enter**. Two of the three are on screen simultaneously in `notes.notebook`.
refuted.why: Factually wrong about the code on its load-bearing claim, and already handled on three of its four sub-claims. Measured computed styles at 1920: .headKbd = 11px/600, ls 0.825px, uppercase, pad 1px 5px, radius 4px; .dockField kbd = 11px/600, ls -0.156px, none, 1px 5px, 4px; .darkAct kbd = 11px/600, ls -0.18px, none, 1px 5px, 4px. (1) The two "different" tracking values are ONE declared token. `.dockField` is font-size 13px + `letter-spacing: var(--tr-14)`; `.darkAct` is font-size 15px + `var(--tr-14)`; `[data-app="notes"]` declares `--tr-14: -0.012em` (line 2362). em letter-spacing resolves against the DECLARING element's font-size and inherits as an absolute length: -0.012x13 = -0.156px, -0.012x15 = -0.18px. The finding divided those inherited px back by the chip's own 11px, producing "-0.014em" and "-0.016em". That is a measurement artifact of CSS inheritance, not two design decisions. There are not three typographic settings; there are two, and the second is one token applied at two host sizes. (2) "One padding, one radius" asks for what is already true — all three are 1px 5px / 4px / 11px / 600, identical. All six keycap classes are also hidden together under one selector list at <=720 (lines 3933-3938), so the system is already unified everywhere except case. (3) The fix's target number is wrong against the real source twice: -0.014em is the SUITE-scope `--tr-14` (line 553), not Notes' (-0.012em), and at 11px the Notes curve's step is `--tr-11: 0em`. (4) The one true residue — .headKbd painting CTRL down-arrow next to the dock's Ctrl K, both visible in notes.notebook — has a defence in the source rather than being drift: .headKbd sits inside `.indexHead`, a caps label band (`text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: var(--tr-cap)` = 0.075em), and its sibling `.cnt` in that same head carries an explicit `text-transform: none`. The author enumerated that head's children and set case per child: prose resets, the keycap stays in the band. That is an argument to have, not an oversight, and it is a refinement — nothing is untrue and nothing fails. Severity as packaged (a Typography defect spanning three elements) is overstated for what is actually one debatable case call on one desk-only chip.

refuted.problem: At 1920 — the widest shipping frame — 'Deposit invoice settled, Mara & Finn' breaks as `Deposit invoice settled, Mara` / `& Finn`, a two-word widow line opening with an ampersand. At 390 in dense, 'First call with Aisling & Tom' breaks as `First call with Aisling` / `& Tom`. Single-word widows also occur from 390 to 1440: `Build the Saturday` / `run-sheet`; `Sign off the recommended-suppliers` / `list`; `Clear Sunday 11am` / `late checkout with` / `housekeeping`.
refuted.why:
The observation is largely real but the finding is wrong about the code in both halves of its fix, and wrong about one of the frames it cites — so as written it is not actionable.

CONFIRMED by driving (Range-per-character line reconstruction at 390/768/1280/1440/1920, both tasks.board and tasks.dense): at 1920 "Deposit invoice settled, Mara" / "& Finn" in BOTH states; at 390 dense "First call with Aisling" / "& Tom"; "Build the Saturday" / "run-sheet" at 390-1440; "Clear Sunday 11am" / "late checkout with" / "housekeeping" at 768-1440.

WRONG ABOUT A FRAME: "Sign off the recommended-suppliers" / "list" does not occur at any width. The real break is "Sign off the recommended-" / "suppliers list" — a break inside the compound, not a "list" widow. That card is also the only one of the five with no `.when` chip, so it computes `text-wrap: balance` while its neighbours compute `pretty`; the source comment at _gate-suite.html:1584 states "THE RULE: no text block may have two wrapping laws switched by a sibling" and the selector at :1045 does exactly that. That is a separate, better finding than the one filed.

FIX HALF B IS ALREADY SHIPPED AND ALREADY FAILS. `text-wrap: pretty` is present at _gate-suite.html:1045 and computes to `pretty` on every card the finding names as an ampersand offender. It did not prevent either break, because "& Finn" and "& Tom" are two-word last lines, which Chromium's `pretty` accepts. Adding `pretty` to `.cardTitle` unconditionally is a no-op for the cited cases and would overwrite the deliberate `balance` on chip-less titles — a decision the source documents as re-measured at round 16 ("removes 14 one-word last lines, three-line count unchanged at 21"). It would also not fix the `run-sheet`/`housekeeping` widows, which already run under `pretty` and cannot do better at a 180px measure.

FIX HALF A MISSES THE ACTUAL CAUSE. The non-breaking bind the finding asks for already exists — `bindName()` at :8244 replaces / & / with NBSP-&-NBSP, and it is called on the title at :8350 and the tag at :8320. It is dead code. `esc()` (:8089) runs first and turns `&` into `&`, after which the regex ` & ` can never match. Proven: `bindName(esc("Mara & Finn"))` -> "Mara & Finn"; `esc(bindName(...))` -> "Mara[NBSP]&[NBSP]Finn". The live DOM contains zero U+00A0 in any `.cardTitle` or `.tag` at any width. So the artifact ships a stated typographic rule it does not keep — which is what makes this a defect rather than taste — but a fix written as "render person-pair names with NBSP" invites a second, duplicate mechanism while the broken one stays in the file.

Severity is correctly `defect`, not higher: a couple's name splitting at the ampersand is visibly wrong on the widest sheet and passable; nothing untrue is asserted to Orla, and the board still does what it says.

refuted.problem: The round asks whether three separately ratified curves standing side by side are a system or three. Measured, they are one. At every size the products share, the spread is 0.005em or less: 13px is −0.010 / −0.012 / −0.015em, 15px is −0.012 / −0.015em, 17px is −0.022 / −0.021em. Five thousandths of an em at 13px is 0.065px — below the rendering threshold on any display, and below the difference between two hinting decisions. Nothing visible separates them. What is real is three token sets doing one job.
refuted.why:
REFUTED — the central measurement is wrong, and the truth runs the other way. I drove all eight states at 1920 and dumped computed family/size/letter-spacing for every text-bearing element inside each `[data-app]`.

The claim is "at every size the products share, the spread is 0.005em or less." Two of the three sizes named are misreported, and the shared size with the largest spread was never looked at.

- **20px, unexamined, spread 0.011em.** Tasks `h1.headName` "The Orchard, events" at −0.026em (`--tr-19`, tasks.css:239) against Timeline `p.b-when` "Saturday 3 October 2026" at −0.015em (`--track-body`, timeline.css:482). That is 2.2x the stated ceiling — 0.22px per glyph, ~5.1px accumulated across that 23-character date. Both are a sheet's own headline-class object, in one application.
- **17px is 0.006em, not 0.001em.** The finding compared −0.022 to −0.021, which is Notes' `span.word` against Notes' `.idxDay` — two Notes values. Timeline's real 17px is `p.b-title` (every moment title on the measure, the most repeated object in the product) at −0.015em.
- **13px is the one it got right** (−0.010 / −0.012 / −0.015), and Timeline has exactly one sans element there.

Underneath the arithmetic the structural claim fails too. Timeline's curve is not a finer or coarser version of the same thing — it is a different kind of system: role-banded and **flat**, one value (−0.015em) held across 15, 17 and 20px, where Tasks and Notes grade every step. It also carries a mono side the finding never mentions (Tasks mono 11px +0.100em vs Timeline mono 11px +0.040em and +0.160em, 12px +0.200em — a 0.06em spread, 0.66px per character on short uppercase strings), and a display range to 148px (−0.050em measured live) that neither of the others has. What is actually true is not "three token sets doing one job" — it is two curves that nearly agree (Tasks and Notes are within 0.002em at every shared size) and a third that is a different species. The finding reaches the right question and the wrong answer.

The fix is wrong independently of that.

1. **The proposed curve runs backwards at the top.** "27px −0.034, 30px −0.030em" is looser at the larger size. Notes' real tokens are `--tr-27: -0.030em` and `--tr-34: -0.034em`; the proposal has read Notes' band names as literal pixel sizes and then bolted Timeline's 30px onto the end. Tasks' own token block records having already paid for this exact defect: "there were three values inside the 13px band alone and the curve ran backwards."
2. **It deletes most of the letterfit system.** No `--tr-cap` (0.075em, used by Notes and declared for the suite at shell.css:205), no `--tr-rev` (+0.008em, the reversed-out-of-ink branch that exists because type on ink needs more room to hold colour), no mono steps at all, and nothing above 30px for a surface that renders a 148px count.
3. **"Withdraw the tracking exclusion and run the check as a gate" is a non-sequitur.** Unifying the size→tracking map does not make the shared check runnable. Notes still carries two values at 15px (−0.012 and −0.016) and four at 11px — and two of those four (−0.0142em, −0.0164em) are not declarations at all, they are px letter-spacing inherited from a 13px/15px parent resolving against an 11px child. The exclusion names its own blocker correctly: the check cannot see role, and it withdraws "when a role-aware letterfit check exists." Collapsing the curves builds no such check.
4. **"Nothing on screen moves by more than 0.07px" is per-glyph, not per-line.** Accumulated tracking change is what moves line breaks, and both Notes (`--measure: 31em` with `text-wrap: pretty`) and Timeline (positions computed from real dates on the measure) are width-sensitive.

Severity: the round poses this as an open question, so raising it is legitimate, but as written it is a refinement whose evidence does not survive measurement, and its fix would make the artifact worse.

refuted.problem: Driven at 1440. (a) On Timeline and Notes, ArrowDown from Help sets tabindex="0" on the rail's Add button and calls focus() on it — but that button is `display:none` at every width from 390 to 1920 (measured 0×0 at 390, 720, 721 and 1024), so focus silently fails and the roving group's only tab stop is now an element nobody can reach. Tab from the top of the document then skips the entire spine: before the press, Tab lands on the Timeline tile first; after it, Tab goes straight to the orientation buttons and never returns to the rail. Notes and Tasks become unreachable by keyboard until a repaint. (b) On Tasks, two rovers own the same keys — the suite's own handler in app.js and Tasks' `groupKeys`, which claims any `[data-group]` ancestor and the suite rail carries `data-group="rail"` — so one press moves two tiles: Home → Tasks → Inbox → account, stepping over Notes, Timeline and Help. Arrow-up moves one. (c) On Notes the spine cannot be walked at all: ArrowDown from a rail tile throws focus into the note index. Three products, three different broken models, and the advertised one is "arrows walk it".
refuted.why:
REFUTED ON THE FIX ONLY. The problem is real, reproduced verbatim, and blocking — do not discard it; take the sharpened fix.

Driven at 1440 in chromium against _gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=... , all three limbs confirmed:
(a) Timeline and Notes: baseline Tab from the top of the document lands on `rail:timeline` first. After one ArrowDown from Help the rail reads `mark:-1 home:-1 notes:-1 tasks:-1 timeline:-1 inbox:-1 help:-1 add:0 me:-1` — the only tabindex="0" is the hidden Add — and Tab then runs `b-act, b-act, b-act, "Draw the whole approach across the page", "Draw the approach down the page"`. The spine is gone from the tab order. focus() is a no-op so activeElement stays on Help, which now carries tabindex="-1", so neither Tab nor Shift+Tab returns.
(b) Tasks at 1440: ArrowDown from Home walks `home → tasks → inbox → me → home`; ArrowUp walks `me → help → timeline`. Two rovers, exactly as described — app.js's deck handler (src/app.js:363-384) fires first, then tasks.js's document-level handler (src/tasks.js:2760, gated only on `__SUITE.active("tasks")`, never on the event target) reaches groupKeys (src/tasks.js:362), which claims the shell rail through `data-group="rail"` and moves a second time off the already-moved activeElement.
(c) Notes at 1440: ArrowDown from a rail tile lands on an `.idxRow` — notes.js's bare-arrow index rover (src/notes.js ~3697, `moveCursor(1)`) is likewise gated only on product-active.
Neither gate sees it: verify.mjs:512-518 starts the walk from `[tabindex="0"]` (the active product tile, index 3) and presses ArrowDown three times, reaching timeline/inbox/help and never `add`; the double-rover still yields three distinct keys, so "the arrows walk the capsule" passes green over a broken walk. Genuinely gate-blind, not a restatement.

The fix is refused on one load-bearing, factually wrong claim: "Delete the rail's Add button, which is never rendered at any width." It is rendered. Measured `.rail [data-rail="add"]` on tasks.board: 44x44, display:grid at 390 and at 720; 0x0 display:none at 721, 1024, 1440. `.railAdd` is `display:none` only above the 720 breakpoint (_gate-suite.html:348) and comes back at ≤720 (line 458), suppressed there only for Timeline (line 476), while Notes hides the whole capsule and moves its tiles to the dock. That button is the Tasks phone capsule's add verb, it is a designed decision documented in app.js ("The add verb on the phone capsule belongs to the sheet that is open"), and verify.mjs:612-615 asserts it by name — check("spine", "…and carries the add verb there"). Deleting it turns a green gate red and removes the only add affordance on the Tasks phone. The dependent claim that the "Add task" label is wrong on Notes and Timeline is also wrong: it never renders on either, so no user and no AT ever meets it — except through the very focus bug being fixed, which the offsetParent filter closes.

Severity stands at blocking on my own read: the spine advertises "arrows walk it" and one press makes Notes and Timeline unreachable by keyboard until a repaint.

refuted.problem: One fact — this is not available — is said in three registers in one application. The suite rail: "Every project in one list. Not here yet." / "Your account, in Signal Studio. Not here yet." Tasks: "Sharing arrives when you can invite the couple and your suppliers in." / "Board is the only view for now." / "Project settings come with your account." / "Filter, Sort and Display come with the other views." Notes: "The rest of Signal Studio is on another screen." / "Notes options are on another screen." / "Reading a photo happens on another screen." / "Sending again happens on another screen." The same account tile says "Your account, in Signal Studio. Not here yet." at 1440 and, driven at 390, announces "Orla, venue manager. Account and settings are on another screen." — and the desk one is aria-disabled while the phone one is not.
refuted.why:
The problem is partly real but the finding is refuted on its diagnosis and on its fix.

WHAT I VERIFIED BY DRIVING (chromium, 1440x960 and 390x844, _gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=...):

The registers exist as quoted. Suite rail (_gate-suite.html:7675-7679, railHtml at 7686-7716) uses "<what is behind it>. Not here yet." on mark/home/inbox/help/me. Tasks chrome (8502-8504, 8558, 8566) uses "Board is the only view for now." / "Filter, Sort and Display come with the other views." / "Search comes with the other views." / "Sharing arrives when you can invite the couple and your suppliers in." / "Project settings come with your account." Notes (13843, 13851, 14034-14039) uses "... on another screen." Driving Notes at 1440 I read the live region directly: More actions -> "The rest of Signal Studio is on another screen."; account -> "Orla, venue manager. Account and settings are on another screen."; options -> "Notes options are on another screen."; rail me -> "Your account, in Signal Studio. Not here yet."

But the finding's central factual claim is WRONG. It is not one account tile behaving differently at two widths. There are TWO account tiles, and at 1440 in Notes they are on screen simultaneously: the suite rail `.railAvatar[data-rail="me"]` (aria-disabled="true", title "Your account, in Signal Studio. Not here yet.") and Notes' `.dockAvatar[data-act="account"]` (aria-disabled=null, no title, label "Orla, venue manager. Account and settings"). Notes' dock avatar is unmarked at 1440 AND at 390 - the split is per-product, not per-width. And Tasks' own dockAvatar already carries the suite string and aria-disabled at both widths (probed: `[dockAvatar] ad=true t="Your account, in Signal Studio. Not here yet."`). So "give the phone's account tile the same string as the desk's" describes a defect that does not exist and would leave the actual one (Notes' dock avatar, at every width, sitting beside a differently-marked rail avatar) unfixed.

The FIX WOULD MAKE THE WORK WORSE in two places:
1. Notes' strings are live-region announcements, not tooltips, and three of them end in a reassurance clause that is doing safety work on destructive-sounding controls: "Reading a photo happens on another screen. Nothing here changes." / "Sending again happens on another screen. Your note is still here." / "Deleting for good happens on another screen. Nothing here is deleted." Rewriting these onto "<what is behind it>. Not here yet." deletes the only answer to "did pressing Delete just delete my note?". That is a regression, not a polish.
2. Tasks' strings carry a dependency the rail grammar cannot express. "Filter, Sort and Display come with the other views" and "Search comes with the other views" say these tools are conditional on views that do not exist; "Filter. Not here yet." x3 on three adjacent buttons is strictly less informative and is the templating the source explicitly rejected at 8505-8508 ("Named, not templated"). The finding offers no argument against that decision, only the shape.

Counts are also off: "six 'on another screen' strings" is eight occurrences across seven sites (13843, 13851, 14034-14039), one of which (ELSEWHERE.timeline, "Timeline is another surface in this suite. This lab is the Notes one.") is dead code - no `data-act="timeline"` is rendered - and would have been rewritten to a live string by the proposed sweep.

SEVERITY: the finding declares none; it is a defect, not misleading. Nothing a sighted person reads asserts an untruth - these are title attributes and live-region text. The residual real defects are narrow and named in sharpenedFix.

refuted.problem: This is the round's own declared question, measured. The uppercase mono eyebrow is the single device all three sheets share, and at the same size, the same weight and the same role it carries three fits: Tasks sets TO DO, IN PROGRESS, REVIEW, VENUE, BAR, ENQUIRY at 11px / +0.100em; Timeline sets TODAY IS 16 JULY, DAYS AWAY, BEHIND YOU, ONE OF THREE, ACROSS and DOWN at 11px / +0.160em; and Timeline's own MARA & FINN at 12px / +0.200em. A 2× spread on one idiom. The same divergence runs through the mono numerals — Tasks' tray counts at +0.100em against Timeline's "3 moments", "16" and "Sat 1 Aug" at +0.040em. This is not three curves at three sizes; it is one size, one face, one case, one job, three values.
refuted.why:
The kernel is real but the finding is wrong about the frames, wrong about its own premise, and its fix is not a fix.

FACTUALLY WRONG ON THE HEADLINE. "The uppercase mono eyebrow is the single device all three sheets share" is false. `src/notes.css` contains no mono at all — `grep -n "font-mono\|--mono\|Geist Mono" notes.css` returns zero hits. Notes' eyebrow (`.indexHead`, `.deskFact b`, line 615 / 365) is Geist SANS, weight **600**, 11px, `--tr-cap: 0.075em`. So the shared idiom is two sheets, not three, and the "same weight" claim fails too — Tasks declares 400 with an in-file rule that "a small label is never bolded to make it matter" (tasks.css:428). The finding's own evidence list never cites a Notes selector, and its fix routes no Notes selector, so it does not touch the actual three-way divergence it claims to have measured.

INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT ON SIZE. It concludes "one size, one face, one case, one job, three values" while its own third value is `MARA & FINN` at 12px/+0.200em. That is `--size-labelWide` / `--track-labelWide`, declared in timeline.css:61 as "the ceremonial top line, **and only that**", with a documented prior ruling at timeline.css:449-458 demoting two elements OUT of that role for not earning it. Folding `.b-who` into an 11px eyebrow token erases a ratified role distinction from Timeline's own nineteen-round ladder — the exact "reports role divergence as drift" error the round notes warn about in gate-blindness item 1.

THE FIX NAMES NO NUMBER. "A single tracking value" with the value left blank is a request, not a fix, and the two candidates are not interchangeable. Up to 0.160em: `IN PROGRESS` grows ~11 chars × 11px × 0.06em ≈ 7px inside a flex tray head whose `.trayCount` sits at `margin-left: auto`, at 390 and 768. Down to 0.100em: `.b-measureHead`'s `min-width: 76px` (timeline.css:529, with a comment saying it was sized so the string does not outgrow its box) is now over-wide for a shorter string, in both `across` and `down`.

THE FIX BREAKS A BEARING COMPENSATION IT DOES NOT MENTION. tasks.css:136 sets `.trayCount { letter-spacing: 0.1em; margin-right: -0.1em; }` with the comment "the negative margin absorbs the trailing tracking cell so the digits stay flush with the content edge". Routing `.trayCount` to a 0.04em data token while declaring "no size, weight or family change" and no geometry change leaves the count over-pulled 0.06em past the edge the name and note align to — a new misalignment introduced by a letterfit cleanup.

SEVERITY. Undeclared by the seat; on the evidence it is refinement, not a defect. Tasks trays and Timeline heads are never co-visible — the spine mounts one product at a time — so the 0.100/0.160 gap is only perceivable across a switch, and each value is internally consistent and ratified inside its own product. Nothing asserts anything untrue and nothing fails to work.

Real residue worth carrying forward: Tasks 11px/+0.100em vs Timeline 11px/+0.160em on the same face, size, case and role IS the round's declared question, honestly measured, and worth a decision. But it is a two-product question with a named number, not a three-sheet token sweep.

refuted.problem: The locked architecture puts identity on the sheet's own head. Notes and Tasks do it, in one grammar: lowercase wordmark, full stop, top left — `notes.` and `tasks.`. Timeline's head opens straight on MARA & FINN and names itself nowhere; the only place the product says what it is, is the foot, in 11px mono, as "Signal Timeline" — a naming form the suite's own contract does not use anywhere (products are Notes, Tasks and Timeline under Signal Studio; the rail's own accessible name is "Signal Studio"). So one of three sheets has no identity where the other two put theirs, and the one time it names itself it invents a fourth name.
refuted.why: REFUTED — the problem is real, the fix is wrong on both halves, and the framing is factually wrong about the surface it names. VERIFIED FACTS (driven at 1440 and 390, plus source): - Tasks head: `tasks` + ink `::after` dot, 17px/600, x=128, y=37. Notes head: `notes`, 17px/600, x=130, y=38. Same object, same band, same place. `_gate-suite.html:8528, 8962, 12351`. - Timeline has no `.word` in any state. Confirmed by `querySelector('.word') === null` at owner-flight, desk and phone. - "Signal Timeline" appears exactly once in 17,676 lines — `_gate-suite.html:15787`, `h("span", { text: o.link || "Signal Timeline" })` — and no call site ever passes `link`, so it prints on every timeline surface. Every other suite string in the file says "Signal Studio" (title, rail `aria-label` at 7703/8478/12286, the dictation privacy line at 7131, the mark and account door copy at 7678-7679). The repo's own naming contract (`AGENTS.md`, `docs/SUITE_URL_AND_NAMING_CONTRACT.md`) says one app, four products, and "do not invent … alternate product names". So the fourth-name charge is correct and independently supported. WHY THE FIX IS REFUTED: 1. The fix anchors to the wrong band, because the finding misreads which timeline state is which. `states.desk` is commented in source at 17023: **"Loading this state directly is byte-identical to what a guest gets."** `timeline.desk` and `timeline.phone` are the shared artifact a wedding couple opens through "Get the link" — not Orla's sheet. Stamping `timeline.` on the head there converts the couple's plan into a branded product page. The lab deliberately gives that surface to MARA & FINN and 79 and keeps provenance quiet in the foot; the CSS at 6035 says so in as many words ("Provenance, said where a stranger looks first"). The locked architecture's "identity on the sheet's own head" governs the application's sheet, not the artifact a stranger receives. The finding does not distinguish the two and its fix targets the guest surface in two of the three states it cites. 2. On the one state that IS Orla's sheet, the finding's premise is false. `timeline.owner-flight` does not "open straight on MARA & FINN": it opens on `.b-bar` — "The Orchard, events" (`.b-where`) then "Mara & Finn / one of three" (`.b-switch`) then the three acts. `.b-horizon` with MARA & FINN is the third band down, below the bar and below the "Live since 15 July" strip, ~240px from the sheet top at 1920. "Ahead of MARA & FINN" would therefore land the wordmark mid-sheet and BELOW the workspace name — inverting the exact grammar (`tasks.` | rule | The Orchard, events) the fix claims to be restoring. What is actually missing is one rung: the product wordmark at the head of `.b-bar`, where Timeline already carries workspace and project. 3. "or drop the line" is the wrong branch of the foot fix. That span is the only thing on the guest artifact that says what the page is or where it came from; the finding's own claim that "Kept by Orla and the stamp are enough" is wrong — neither names the product or the maker. The name is wrong; the line is load-bearing. 4. Understated detail the fix omits: the full stop's colour. Tasks spends ink because "the sheet's own claim is that indigo means the next milestone" (6010-6014). Timeline's indigo means the today rule and the lead tick — the same argument, so the Timeline dot must be ink. The fix says "same full stop" without resolving which of the two ratified answers it inherits. Severity is correctly `defect`: visibly wrong and inconsistent, but nothing stops working and nothing false is asserted about the plan's state. Not `misleading` — "Signal Timeline" is an invented name, not an untrue claim about the data.

refuted.problem: The one fact all three heads state is today, and each states it in its own grammar: Tasks "Thu 16 Jul", Notes "Thursday 16 July", Timeline "TODAY IS 16 JULY". The same is true one level down — 15 July is "15 Jul" on a Tasks card, "Yesterday" in Notes and "Updated 15 July 2026" on Timeline's foot. Timeline's own fixture comment declares the rule ("One grammar per fact… it never mixes elapsed, deictic and absolute forms for the same fact on the same screen") and keeps it inside itself; the suite does not keep it across itself.
refuted.why:
REFUTED — factually wrong about the frames, and the fix would damage Tasks.

1. **Notes' head does not state today.** Driven at 1440×960 and 1920×1000, the Notes head reads: `notes / The Orchard, events / Mara & Finn / Saturday 18 July, in 2 days / Go through 8 / Private to you`. That date is `nextUp()` (_gate-suite.html:12310-12321) — the *next event*, 18 July — not today. "Thursday 16 July" never appears on the Notes head in any state (`notes.notebook`, `notes.seam`, `notes.voice`). It appears once, as an `.idxDayNote` day-divider deep in the index at y≈523, which the finding itself says to leave alone. So the premise "the one fact all three heads state is today" is false: two heads state today, not three, and the third states a different fact entirely.

2. **The rule it invokes is scoped to "the same screen", and the three heads are never on the same screen.** The fixture comment at :7242 reads in full: "it never mixes elapsed, deictic and absolute forms for the same fact *on the same screen*." Probed at all eight states: exactly one `[data-app]` ever renders (`visibleApps` = `["tasks"]`, `["notes"]`, `["timeline"]` respectively; the other two are in the DOM but paint nothing). The suite does keep the rule as the rule is written.

3. **"15 July is 'Yesterday' in Notes" is wrong.** Notes' "Yesterday" is `.idxWhen` — the elapsed *capture time* of a note, sitting in a column of "35 minutes ago / 2 hours ago / 9 hours ago". Notes never prints 15 July anywhere (regex over rendered text: zero matches in all three Notes states). Tasks' "Completed 15 Jul" is a completion date; Timeline's "Updated 15 July 2026" is a publication stamp. Three different facts in three products, not one fact in three grammars.

4. **The fix would make Tasks worse.** `todayLabel()` at :8200 has a declared job, stated at :8198: "Every chip on every card was floating without an anchor: nothing anywhere said what today is, so '14 Jul' could be two days late or two months." Its `Thu 16 Jul` form is deliberately the *same* short grammar as the chips it anchors — the board prints "14 Jul", "15 Jul", "1 Aug", "Completed 15 Jul". Rewriting the head to "Thursday 16 July" puts the anchor in a grammar none of its dependents use and re-opens the exact defect the Tasks lock at :8188 says it closed.

5. **The fix's only number is wrong.** "Thu 16 Jul" (10 chars) → "Thursday 16 July" (16) is six characters, not five.

Severity as framed would be misleading-class; nothing here asserts anything untrue, so refinement at most, and as written it is refuted outright.

refuted.problem: Opening a moment's editor on the horizontal measure inserts a 554px-tall .b-edit block above the track and displaces the whole measure down the app scroller: the edited moment's .b-grab moves 588→1170 at 1920×1000 and at 1440×960, and 716→1298 at 1280×900 and 1024×900, against a main.app clientHeight of 924/864. Nothing auto-scrolls, and because editor (554px) plus the measure band (~400px) exceeds the app viewport at every width where across is served, the two can never be on screen together — scrolling main.app to the bottom brings the measure back to y=404 but takes the editor to y=-323. The four .b-step controls do move the moment (its x goes 924→944 at 1920) but write nothing to any aria-live region, so pressing "Move a day later" produces no observable change of any kind. layout=down handles the identical action correctly: it repositions so the edited moment stays on screen at y=466 and the stepper visibly moves it to y=484.
refuted.why:
Compound finding. Half is measured correctly; the half that carries the severity is factually false against the code, and the remedy it proposes for that half is already shipped — so as filed it is refuted.

VERIFIED TRUE (the displacement). Driven at 1920x1000 / 1440x960 / 1280x900 / 1024x900 on ?state=timeline.owner-flight&layout=across. `.b-editHost` is a sibling inside `.b-stick`, sitting between `.b-horizon` and the measure. Opening the editor inserts 554px there: `.b-measure` top goes 506 -> 1088 and the edited `.b-grab` 588 -> 1170 (1920/1440) and 716 -> 1298 (1280/1024). `main.app` clientHeight is 964/924/864/864 — the finding says "924/864" and misses 964 at 1920, immaterial. Nothing auto-scrolls (appScrollTop stays 0); scrolled to the floor (max 766 at 1440) the measure returns to y=322 and the editor goes to y=-323, so the two genuinely cannot share a screen at any width where across is served. The root cause is real and named in the source: the in-column editor rule is `[data-medium="full"] .b-editHost .b-edit` guarded only by `min-width: 1024px`, and its own comment reads "In the rail, where there is a column already." In `down` that premise holds — the measure and the editor are side-by-side columns (verified: the editor spans y=588..1141 while the edited grab sits at y=628, vertically overlapping), which is why down looks correct. `across` is full-width, so the same rule stacks instead of pairing, and `src/across.css` contains not one editor rule. `keepInBand()` — the function written precisely to hold a moved row in a visible band — is a no-op here: it returns early unless the panel is `position: fixed` or `.b-plan` is a live scroller, and in across the panel computes to `relative` and there is no `.b-plan`.

FACTUALLY FALSE (the announcement half, and it is the half that inflates this to blocking). "The four .b-step controls ... write nothing to any aria-live region, so pressing 'Move a day later' produces no observable change of any kind." Measured, in across at 1440, pressing `.b-step[data-delta="1"]`, four things change at once: (1) `.b-stepRead` — `role="status"`, i.e. an implicit polite live region — goes "Saturday 1 August 2026 / in 16 days" -> "Sunday 2 August 2026 / in 17 days", and it is on screen at y=742, 45px tall, directly under the stepper buttons inside the open editor (edTop 443, edBot 996); (2) `.b-undo`, also `role="status"`, goes from empty to "Menu tasting at The Orchard moved 1 day later." at y=460, also on screen; (3) `#b-edit-date` goes "1 August 2026" -> "2 August 2026"; (4) the `.b-grab` aria-label goes "...Saturday 1 August, in 16 days..." -> "...Sunday 2 August, in 17 days...". Identical in both orientations. The finding's own fix — "have every .b-step write the moment's new position to the polite live region" — is therefore already handled, twice, and the code comments show `.b-stepRead` was given its reserved two-line height and `role=status` by an earlier round for exactly this reason. Adding a third announcement in the grab's grammar would make one keypress speak three times.

FIX IS ALSO WRONG on the half that survives. "Pin the .b-measure band to the top of .tl-stage" contradicts the locked architecture — Direction B's horizon is the thing that never moves, and the horizon is what currently occupies the top of the stick; promoting the measure above it inverts the one fixed reference every distance on the sheet is read from. "Position it as an overlay" would paint the editor over the moments it is editing. "A reserved band below the track" is the opposite of what it says in the same sentence, and it makes things worse: with the editor below, the measure holds at 506 but the editor lands at 1088..1642 and now the editor needs a scroll to reach. And its "give the editor its own internal scroll if it does not fit" is already in the base rule (`max-height: 72dvh; overflow-y: auto`) — it is only neutralised by the min-width:1024 override.

SEVERITY. Not blocking: the product does exactly what it says — the stepper moves the moment, the readout and the undo bar report it live and visibly, undo works. Not misleading: nothing asserts anything untrue. It is a defect — visibly wrong, and worth fixing because across is the new surface and the one orientation where pressing a stepper cannot be seen to move anything on the measure itself.

refuted.problem: The carry model is Space to pick up, arrows to walk, and the card announces itself correctly at every step ("Picked up …", "In progress, position 1 of 4.", Escape gives "Move cancelled. … is back in the to do column."). Enter, the key that commits everywhere else on this surface, does not drop. On a grabbed card Enter runs the card body's open-the-note handler: aria-expanded flips to true, aria-grabbed stays "true", and the polite region says "Showing the whole note." The card is still in the air — a further ArrowRight moves it again to Review — and only a second Space drops it ("… dropped in the review column.").
refuted.why:
Every observable claim reproduces exactly — I drove it at 1440x960 and got, in order: "Picked up Confirm marquee sides with the hire company." / aria-grabbed=true; ArrowRight -> "In progress, position 1 of 4."; Enter -> aria-expanded=true, aria-grabbed STILL true, "Showing the whole note.", and draggable flips "true"->"false"; ArrowRight again -> "Review, position 1 of 3."; Space -> "… dropped in the review column." The code matches: in _gate-suite.html the `if (key === "Enter")` branch at line 9907 is reached with no `carriedId` guard, while the Space branch at ~9880 owns both pickup and drop.

But the finding's load-bearing premise is false. It argues Enter is "the key that commits everywhere else on this surface" and therefore should drop. The surface does not claim that, and it says so twice, in the operator's face, at the exact moment of the carry: (1) the card carries `aria-keyshortcuts="Space ArrowUp ArrowDown ArrowLeft ArrowRight"` — Enter is deliberately absent; (2) a carry HUD capsule sits at the foot of the board for the whole carry reading "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company · ↑↓←→ move · Space drop · Esc cancel" (see the screenshot I captured of the grabbed state). Three keys named, all three implemented, exactly as named. On a card, Enter's one documented meaning is open-the-note (brief.md: "Press a card body to open its note"), and it does that. "Enter drops" appears in exactly one place in this repository — brief.md line 183, the lab's own prose — and nowhere in the artefact. So the product neither fails to do what it says nor asserts anything untrue; nothing is blocking or misleading here.

What survives is much smaller than the finding claims: during a carry a non-carry command still fires and mutates the card mid-flight, leaving a state no pointer user can reach — aria-grabbed="true" and draggable="false" at once — and the polite region says "Showing the whole note." without restating that the card is still in the air. That is the same class the code already guards one line above ("Space on a checkbox picked the card up … a labelled control doing an unrelated, unannounced thing"), so the author's own principle argues for a guard. It is a refinement, not a defect: AT still reports the card as grabbed, the HUD still names the drop key, Escape still resolves the carry before the note, and the carry completes correctly.

The proposed fix is also wrong twice over, independently of the premise.
