First, "commit the move … and announce the landing lane" is not the Space path: the Space path branches on `lane === "done" && carriedFrom.lane !== "done"` and calls `completed(task, …)` — the code names it "the fourth door into a completion," with its own receipt and sentence, added precisely because it used to say only "dropped in Done." A literal implementation of the fix as written makes Enter a fifth door that skips the receipt. Second, if Enter is to commit, the fix must also update the HUD and `aria-keyshortcuts`, which currently name Space alone; adding a silent fourth commit key re-creates the advertised-vs-implemented gap in reverse. The fix names neither.

refuted.problem: Switching across↔down with a moment editor open destroys the editor. The typed title survives (the input is live-bound to the moment, and the measure shows the edited text afterwards) and focus stays correctly on the layout control, but the polite region says only "The measure runs down the page." — nothing about the editor that just vanished.
refuted.why:
Every fact in the observation checks out when driven (chromium, 1440x960, ?state=timeline.owner-flight&layout=across): open `.b-grab` on "Final dress fitting", type into `#b-edit-title`, press `[data-layout-to="down"]` — `.b-edit` count goes 1 → 0, `data-editor-open` is cleared, `aria-expanded="true"` count goes 1 → 0, the edited text survives on the row, focus lands on the rebuilt `down` button, and `.b-live` reads exactly "The measure runs down the page." No console errors. The orientation gate in tools/orientation.mjs never opens an editor before switching, so nothing here restates a gate assertion. The finding is REFUTED on its fix and on its diagnosis, not on its observation.

Wrong fix, branch B. The quoted sentence — "The measure runs down the page. Still editing Final dress fitting." — is offered as naming "what closed" while asserting the opposite. Nothing is being edited: the panel is gone, the title field is gone, and focus is on a toggle. A reader told "still editing Final dress fitting" will Tab expecting the field. That converts a silent omission (defect) into a spoken untruth (misleading) — it manufactures exactly the class this engagement is trying to drive to zero, so it makes the work worse.

Wrong fix, branch A, as written. `openEditor()` ends in `node.focus({preventScroll:true})`, so "reopen it on the same moment" via the existing entry point moves the keyboard off the layout control and fails the currently-green assertion `check("orientation", "…and keeps the keyboard on the control", after.focused === "down")`.

Wrong diagnosis, and this is the substantive part. The finding reassures that the loss is cosmetic ("the typed title survives"). It is not. `render()` for the timeline product opens with `history.length = 0;` (~line 17564 of _gate-suite.html) and the orientation handler calls `C.mount()`, which runs it. Measured: press "Move a week later" in the editor, the reversibility bar fills with "Final dress fitting moved 7 days later. Undo Ctrl Z" (`data-empty="false"`); press `[data-layout-to="down"]`; the bar returns `data-empty="true"` and a subsequent Ctrl+Z is a no-op while the 7-day move stands. The product displayed an undo offer and silently withdrew it — that is the misleading-class behaviour on this press, and neither proposed branch touches it. A founder who takes this finding as filed patches the announcement and ships the actual loss.

One correction to the framing, in the fix's favour but against the "silently" charge as a class complaint: closing the editor by Done or Escape also announces nothing on `.b-live`. That is correct design — focus returns to the `.b-grab` whose `aria-expanded` flips to false, and a reader hears the collapse from the control. The orientation path is genuinely different only because focus is parked on the layout button and never passes the collapsed disclosure, which is why some notice is owed here and nowhere else. Also worth noting the class is wider than the element line: a spine round-trip (notes → timeline) destroys the same editor with `.b-live` left empty, so a fix scoped only to `[data-layout-to]` leaves the same hole one press away.

refuted.problem: The orientation control is offered from 721px up, but the horizontal measure carries a 640px min-width and becomes an overflow-x:auto scroller below ~940px with no mask, no fade, no terminal mark and no scroll affordance. At 768 the default press of ACROSS renders a line that runs off the sheet edge and stops: "Final guest number" is cut mid-word, "Venue walk-through" is cut to "Ve", and the wedding day — the object the entire product counts down to — is not on the page at all. The control's own accessible name is "Draw the whole approach across the page". Scrolling to reach it then amputates "Today, 16 July", the origin the composition means by "your feet", with the same silent clip at the other end. The gate cannot see this: it asserts no page-level sideways scroll, and there is none.
refuted.why:
REFUTED — the underlying clipping is real, but the finding is factually wrong about the code on the two points its fix is built from, and both of the fix's numbers and mechanisms are wrong.

Verified true by driving: below ~945px the across measure is a silent clipper. ACROSS_FLOOR=8 x 79 days gives a 632px span + 8px edge = a 640px scrollWidth floor. At 768, .b-measure has clientWidth 476, overflowX auto, maskImage none, and offsetHeight-clientHeight = 0. "Final guest numbers" runs 512->680 against a right edge of 660; "Venue walk-through" shows 36px of a 168px label; the "Wedding day" mark shows 8px. Scrolling to the end puts .b-origin ("Today, 16 July") fully outside the box. Confirmed.

Wrong 1 — "offered from 721px up". There is no 721 rail breakpoint on this control. The gate is acrossAllowed(medium), testing the state's declared medium ("full"|"sheet"), not viewport width. Measured: the control is present, visible and pressable at 390, 500, 600, 700 and 720 in timeline.owner-flight and timeline.desk, with medium="full" at every one of them. owner-flight is the suite's default data-state (line 6519) and is mapped to medium "full" (line 17550), so a phone opening Timeline gets the control. At 390 the box is 332px against the same 640px track and the wedding-day mark sits 136px past the edge — strictly worse than the case the finding names, and outside the band it names.

Wrong 2 — "the phone already proves the pattern by omitting the control entirely". Only the timeline.phone fixture-medium state omits it. The artifact's own behaviour gate contradicts the claim in as many words: tools/orientation.mjs opens ?p=timeline at 390 and asserts [data-layout-to] is a 44px target there. The pattern the fix leans on does not exist.

Wrong 3 — "the wedding day is not on the page at all". .b-horizon prints "79 / days / Saturday 3 October 2026 / Wedding day / TODAY IS 16 JULY" above the measure on the same sheet, and it is the largest thing on it. What leaves the frame is the day's mark at the far end of the measure — a real loss to the orientation's whole argument, but not the absence claimed.

Wrong 4 — "~940". At 940 clientWidth is 630 against a 640 floor and data-scrolls is still "true". Fit begins between 940 and 950 (950 -> cw 640, exactly). The number is short by the margin that matters.

Fix is unbuildable as written. A media query cannot express acrossAllowed, which is a per-state medium test in JS, and no static width is correct in any case: the floor is daysFromToday(primaryDate) x 8, so the same sheet in September fits inside 500px and a project a year out would scroll at 1920. The artifact already computes exactly this condition, measured, as data-scrolls.

Severity, corrected: misleading, not blocking. The control's accessible name says "Draw the whole approach across the page" and below ~945 it draws about a fifth of it and hides the rest behind an invisible scroll — the product asserting something untrue. It is not blocking: the surface still works, the day is named at the head, and the scroll does reach the far end. Note also that the codebase states this principle itself — orientation.mjs: "A horizontal scrollbar at an ordinary desk width is not a smaller version of that, it is the opposite of it" — and then only checks it at 1024 and up, which is the gate blindness worth keeping.

refuted.problem: Above/below-axis placement in `across` is assigned by index parity rather than anchored to the moment. Pressing "Move a week earlier" on "Send the invitations" (23 → 16 days) flips four moments that did not change date across the axis — "Choose the evening music" and "Venue walk-through" move from below the line to above, "Final dress fitting" and "Final guest numbers" move from above to below — and the measure grows 308px → 546px, pushing everything under it down the page. The tie itself is handled well (the two 16-day moments stack in a raised tray and the accessible names read "the first of 2 moments" / "the second of 2 moments"), so the defect is purely the re-rag. The gate's collision check runs on the frozen fixture and never after an edit.
refuted.why:
The OBSERVATION is real and I reproduced it exactly; the PROPOSED FIX is wrong in both halves, so this is refuted with a corrected fix.

Reproduced by driving `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=timeline.owner-flight&layout=across` at 1920x1000, clicking `.b-grab` on "Send the invitations" then the −7 stepper. Before: 16 above / 23 below / 37 above / 44 below / 51 above / 65 below / 79 above, measure `style.height` 308px, `--rule-y` 154px. After: the pair at 16 is above (lead+follow) and every remaining moment flips — 37 below, 44 above, 51 below, 65 above, 79 below — measure 546px, `--rule-y` 273px. That is five flips, not four; the finding under-counts by omitting "Wedding day", which also crosses the axis. The cause is in `placeAcross` (_gate-suite.html:15368): `var side = "below"` then `side = side === "above" ? "below" : "above"` per leader, so the side is pure parity over the live sorted order, and merging two moments into one mark removes a leader and inverts the phase for everything downstream. The gate claim is also accurate: `tools/orientation.mjs:131-151` runs its no-collision check on a freshly opened page and never after an edit.

Why the fix is wrong.

(a) "Assign side from a stable property (its id, or its parity in the original sorted order held across edits)." Alternation is not decoration here — it is the packer's input. `lanes`/`rank` (15420-15427) only steps a label out when it collides *within its own side*, so alternation is what halves the density per lane. Hashing by id gives arbitrary runs on one side, which deepens ranks, grows the band, and makes the composition look random rather than woven. "Parity in the original sorted order" is worse over time: it is undefined for a moment created by "Add a moment", and after two or three edits it no longer alternates with anything, so it produces exactly the adjacent-same-side runs the alternation exists to prevent — and the collision gate that currently passes on the frozen fixture would start failing on it.

(b) "Hold the measure's height at the max of pre- and post-edit height for the duration of the confirmation strip." This defers the 238px collapse to the moment the strip dismisses, i.e. to a repaint the reader did not cause — strictly worse than a jump attached to a press. It also treats the growth as inevitable, and it is not: `--step` is computed once for the whole measure as `awayH + blockH * (stacked ? 2 : 1) + 14` (15466-15470), where `stacked` is a single global boolean and `blockH` is the max `.b-copy` over all items. Measured: before, awayH 18, max copy 95 → step 128. After, max copy 107 (the raised tray) → step 18 + 107×2 + 14 = 247. So every rank on BOTH sides is given a second full label of height because ONE mark on ONE side holds two labels. The 238px is an artefact of that global doubling, not of the tie.

Severity: the seat's element is right but the class should be read as `defect`, not higher. Nothing untrue is asserted — the ticks stay on their true pixel, the printed dates and day-counts are unchanged, `Ctrl+Z` restores the measure to 308px and the original sides exactly. Side-of-axis carries no meaning the surface claims. It is visibly wrong and, at the Linear/Stripe bar, would not survive review — but the product does what it says.

refuted.problem: The sentence that makes each door honest — "Every project in one list. Not here yet." — exists only in the title attribute. The accessible names are bare: "Home", "Inbox", "Help and settings". A title never renders on touch, so at 390 the honesty is unreachable by the input the product ships on. Separately, the doors are inconsistent at 390: Tasks and Timeline carry Home in the dock, Notes carries none, and Inbox and Help are absent from all three. Switch product on a phone and the Home door appears and disappears.
refuted.why:
The headline claim is factually wrong, and the fix does not fix what is actually broken.

DRIVEN, at 390x844 with a touch context (chromium, hasTouch/isMobile), against `_gate-suite.html`:

1. "The sentence exists only in the title attribute" is false. The suite's rail click handler at `_gate-suite.html:9924-9935` intercepts any `[aria-disabled="true"]` door, preventDefaults, and calls `say(tile.getAttribute("title"))` into the one polite live region (`region()`/`say()`, lines 9935-9952). I tapped `.rail [data-rail="home"]` at 390 with a real touch tap: `#say` came back reading exactly `"Every project in one list. Not here yet."` So on the input the product ships on, the honesty IS reachable to a screen reader — it is announced on activation, not left in hover. Separately, `title` on an element that already has an `aria-label` is mapped to the accessible *description* by every major AT, so calling it "only a tooltip" misstates what the attribute is doing. Name = the door, description = the qualification, spoken on press, is the correct pattern, not the bug.

2. The one thing genuinely missing is not the thing the finding names: for a *sighted* touch user the tap is pixel-silent. Screenshot before and after the tap compare byte-identical (53,328 bytes, Buffer.compare === 0). The reason is spoken and never shown. But the proposed fix does not touch that at all — a longer `aria-label` renders nothing to a sighted thumb either. The fix aims at the population that is already served and leaves the population that is not.

3. The fix would actively make the served case worse. The rail is a nine-stop roving-tabindex group; five of those stops are doors. Putting a full sentence in the accessible name means every arrow-walk of the spine reads a sentence per stop, and it collides with the shipped active-state name pattern (`"Notes, the page you are on"` — `_gate-suite.html:7695-7697`), which appends to a short name and would read as a run-on against a sentence. Verbosity on the primary keyboard object to duplicate information already delivered on press is a regression.

4. The second half of the finding is factually correct, and it is the only part worth keeping. Verified at 390: in `tasks.board` and `timeline.phone` the suite rail is the dock and carries Home (`aria-label="Home"`, title present, hit); in `notes.notebook`/`notes.seam` the suite `.rail` is display:none and Notes' own `.dock` takes over, carrying Search / Dictate / Read a photo / (Save it) / Notes / Tasks / Timeline / account — no Home. Inbox, Help and the mark are absent from all three at 390, because `_gate-suite.html:454` and `:456` set `.railMark, .railDivider, .railSpacer { display:none }` and `.railUtil { display:none }` at ≤720. That means at phone width four of the five doors the non-negotiable calls "present, reachable, in the tab order" are in neither the tree nor the tab order. That is the real residue — and it is a door-membership and door-wording problem, not an accessible-name problem.

5. The fix's numbers for that half are wrong too. "Give the phone dock the same door membership in all three products" is not buildable as stated: Notes' dock at 390 already carries eight buttons in a 390px bar, and 390/44 caps a single row at eight targets. Adding Home, Inbox, Help and More to it either breaks the hit-target gate (which is currently 0) or forces a redesign of a protected dock.

6. I also found, while driving, a wording inconsistency the finding did not: tapping the account tile in Notes' dock at 390 announces `"Orla, venue manager. Account and settings are on another screen."` while the same door on the suite rail says `"Your account, in Signal Studio. Not here yet."` Two sentences for one door, decided by which product is open. That is in scope ("a finding that says the sentence on one of those doors is wrong is in") and is a sharper version of the honesty complaint than the one filed.

Severity: the seat's framing implies misleading — the product asserting an honesty it does not deliver. It does deliver it, on press, on touch, at every width. What survives is a phone-width membership and wording inconsistency: visibly wrong, passable, not an untrue assertion. Defect.

Note the behaviour gate asserts nothing about the doors (no match for `aria-disabled`, `Not here yet`, `home` or `inbox` in `interaction-check.mjs`), so this is legitimately gate-blind ground — the seat was hunting in the right place and drew the wrong quarry.

refuted.problem: You asked whether the 1060 → 1440 widening is right or merely wider. Merely wider. At 1920 an index row renders 159 characters of the person's own prose on one 15px line in a 1153px column — over twice the classic measure and well past the ~100-character ceiling a scannable one-line row can hold. Because the text element flexes, the rag on the right is uncontrolled: a long row's sentence stops 13px from its status chip, a short row's stops ~280px from it, so the chips and timestamps sit in a column while the words that matter end at a different place on every row.
refuted.why:
REFUTED on the central claim and on the fix.

1. "Merely wider" is contradicted by measurement. `src/notes.js:trimRows()` fills the row width-adaptively, so extra width buys whole notes, not empty prose. Driven at three widths: at 1280 eleven of fourteen notes are cut mid-sentence with an ellipsis; at 1440 six are; at 1920 exactly ONE is, and thirteen of fourteen render complete in the person's own words. That is the difference between a pile you cannot read and a pile you can. `src/notes.css:145-156` states this argument in the file ("every pixel of width there is another few words of a person's own note visible before the ellipsis") and the measurement bears it out. The widening earned its width.

2. The measure rule is misapplied. 45-75 characters governs multi-line prose, where the failure mode is the return sweep to the next line's start. `.idxText` is `white-space: nowrap` with exactly one line and no return sweep. The asserted "~100-character ceiling a scannable one-line row can hold" is not a typographic rule and no evidence is offered for it; Linear's issue rows, Stripe's dashboard rows and Gmail's subject-plus-snippet all run single-line text past 150 characters at 1920. "Over twice the classic measure" is a true arithmetic statement about the wrong rule.

3. Half the fix already ships. `.idxRow` is `grid-template-columns: 20px minmax(0,1fr) 76px 92px` with `.idxTag { justify-self: start }` and `.idxWhen { justify-self: end }` — the chip and timestamp are already pinned in fixed columns with constant left edges at every row and every width, which the finding itself concedes ("the chips and timestamps sit in a column"). `notes.css:701-706` names this as the reason the columns are fixed.

4. The other half would make the work worse, and cannot do what it claims. The rag comes from note length variance, not column width, so a cap cannot make it "constant" — unless the cap truncates everything. And it would: the shortest note's full ink at 1920 is 788px, so a 760px cap cuts all 14 of 14 notes, a strict regression from 1 of 14. The fix buys a tidy rag by ensuring no note is ever readable in full. The finding is effectively arguing for the 1280 rag (13-100px), and 1280 is tight precisely because everything there is cut off.

5. The number is also wrong on its own terms. Measured rendering is ~6.7px/char at 15px Geist with `--tr-14` (155 chars in 1043px), so 760px is ~113 characters, not "roughly 100"; a genuine 100-char cap would be ~670px and would truncate even harder.

Residual conceded, and it is the opposite of the proposed direction: the place worth a founder's attention is 1280, not 1920. There the index is 1162px, the words get 875px, and 227px — 21% of the row — goes to fixed metadata furniture (20 + 76 + 92 + three 13px gaps) while eleven of fourteen notes are cut. Class is refinement, not a defect: nothing is wrong at 1920.

refuted.problem: Every `.b-copy` is a fixed 168px slot regardless of its text. The tier pass ranks against those slots, so at 1024–1359 "Final guest numbers" is promoted to `data-rank="1"` and lifted 96px off the row on a bare 119px stem. At 1280 the two slots are [567,735] and [737,905] — 2px of clearance — while the rendered ink is ~113px and ~139px wide, centred, clearing by 43px. The promotion resolves a collision that does not exist. It snaps flat at 1360 and never fires again.
refuted.why:
REFUTED — the mechanism is real, the extent is overstated, and the fix does not do what it claims. Verified by driving `_gate-suite.html?state=timeline.desk|timeline.owner-flight&layout=across` in chromium at 768/900/1024/1100/1280/1359/1360/1440/1920.

What checks out: `.b-copy` is `width: 168px` (line ~6362), `ACROSS_LABEL = 168` (15230), and the rank pass at 15441–15448 builds `left = x − 84`, `right = left + 168` and promotes on `left < lane[rank] + 14`. At 1280 the two above-lane slots measure [370,538] and [540,708] relative to the measure — 2px of clearance, exactly the finding's [567,735]/[737,905] in page coordinates — while title ink is 115px and 135px, clearing by 45px. Rank goes to 1, `--step` is 96px, the band grows from 244px to 340px, and it snaps flat at 1360. So a false promotion does occur.

Three reasons it is refuted:

1. **The band is wrong at its low end.** At 1024 the ink boxes are [277,392] and [391,526] — they abut at 391px, one pixel of overlap, zero clearance. The promotion at 1024 is not false; it is required. Re-ranking on ink with the finding's own clearance still returns rank 1 there. The false band starts near 1104 (measure ≈ 792, where 14 days × px first exceeds 139), not 1024. "1024–1359" is about 80px of viewport wider than the defect.

2. **The proposed CSS does not shrink the boxes that matter.** `.b-title` carries `text-wrap: balance` and `-webkit-line-clamp: 2` (4694–4705). With `width: max-content; max-width: 168px`, any title whose single-line max-content exceeds 168 clamps back to a 168px box and balances inside it. Injected and measured: "Menu tasting at The Orchard" and "Choose the evening music" both stay at exactly **168px** while their rendered ink is 98px and 95px. The fix leaves a 70px lie in place for precisely the two longest titles — the ones most likely to crowd. It shrinks only the already-short single-line labels.

3. **"the existing clearance constant" is wrong against the real source.** `.b-copy` paints `box-shadow: 0 0 0 12px` on `:hover`, `:focus-within`, `[data-editing="true"]` and `[data-crowded="true"]` (4812–4823), so the painted box is ink + 24px. 14px of clearance between ink boxes means overlapping halos. Measured at 768 under the proposed rule, "Send the invitations" [123,254] and "Choose the evening music" [272,440] both drop to rank 0 with an 18px gap — their hover halos overlap by 6px.

Two smaller errors. `margin-inline: auto` is inert: `.b-copy` in across is `position: absolute; left: 0; transform: translateX(-50%)`, so auto margins centre nothing; the transform already does. And "re-run on `fonts.ready` and on resize" is already handled — line 14812 `document.fonts.ready.then(settle)` and 14819 the rAF-debounced `resize → settle`, and `settle` calls `place()`. Stem height is 116px (`rank × step + 20`), not 119.

Severity, corrected: **defect**, not misleading. The measure still reports every position and every distance truthfully; what is wrong is that one label floats 96px off its row on a bare stem and the band carries an empty rank, at roughly 1104–1359. Visibly below the bar, not an untrue assertion.

refuted.problem: The paper card is 1722px wide at x140 in `across` and 1180px wide at x411 in `down`, at both 1440 and 1920 — the `down` card is capped at 1180 and centred, so at 1920 it floats in 622px of white sheet, and inside it the measure column starts at x968 leaving a 500px gutter that carries content for only the first 300px of a 1602px document. So roughly 1100 of the sheet's 1802px is blank for the length of the scroll. Meanwhile Notes, Tasks and Timeline-`across` all fill 1802px at the same width.
refuted.why:
REFUTED. The load-bearing claim is factually false, several numbers are wrong, and the composition it attacks is a documented decision whose grammar the artifact keeps consistently.

1. "Roughly 1100 of the sheet's 1802px is blank for the length of the scroll" is the opposite of what the artifact does. `.b-stick` is `position: sticky; top: 40px` and the sheet (`.app.sheet`, `overflow-y:auto`, scrollHeight 1682 / clientH 964) is the scroller. Driven at scrollTop 0 / 400 / 700 at 1920, the horizon block sits at viewport top 99 / 58 / 58 — it stays pinned in that left column at every scroll position, carrying "79 days · Saturday 3 October 2026 · Wedding day · TODAY IS 16 JULY · Nothing is planned until 1 August" the whole way down. The left column is occupied for the entire scroll, and being occupied for the entire scroll is the locked rule ("the day is a horizon that never moves"). The finding measured a static frame and reported a scroll behaviour.

2. The numbers are wrong. At 1920 `down`: `.b-measure` starts at x868, not x968. The gap from the card's inner edge (x412) to the measure is 456px, not 500. The horizon block is 338px tall, not 300. And "1722px wide at x140 in across … at both 1440 and 1920" is false at 1440, where `across` measures x140 w1242 — because `across` is `max-width:100%` and simply follows the sheet, which is the very behaviour the finding asks for.

3. It is a deliberate, documented decision, and the artifact keeps the same grammar everywhere. The CSS at the `across` cap-removal states it: "The stage is capped at 1180px because down the page the artifact is a document and a document has a measure. Across, the artifact IS the distance… The cap comes off for this orientation and only this one." `timeline.desk` renders a guest *artifact* inside the owner's room — the sibling state `timeline.phone` renders a 390px `.tl-device` centred in the same 1802px sheet with 706px of white on each side, under the comment "a device is drawn only when there is room to draw one." Applying this finding's premise consistently would demand the phone bezel be stretched to 1802px too. The round notes further flag this exact trade as already considered and warn that "a finding that says a measure has been lost is a good finding" — this finding pushes the opposite way.

4. Half the proposed fix is already implemented. "Hold the horizon block and the measure as two columns of the full-width card" — `down` already lays `.b-two` as `.b-stick` (344px) + `.b-plan`/`.b-measure` (666px). The only novel half is widening the card to 1722 while capping the measure inside it.

5. That novel half would make it worse. `.tl-paperEdge` draws a visible `1px solid rgba(17,17,17,0.16)` edge on white. Widening it to 1722 with the content capped leaves ~700px of dead space *inside a drawn border*, flush-ragged, for the full 1602px height. Dead space outside a card edge reads as a sheet resting on a floor; the same space inside a card edge reads as a broken layout. The fix converts benign room into visible breakage.

refuted.problem: The scroller is `main.app.sheet` (818px of travel in `down` at 1440×900). Scrolled to 500, pressing ACROSS then DOWN returns scrollTop to 0: the visible moments change from 37/44/51/65/79 to 16/23/37/44. Focus is correctly kept on the pressed control, and the gate asserts that; nothing asserts the reading position. `verify.mjs`'s orientation pass checks stale inline geometry, not place.
refuted.why:
The PROBLEM is real and I reproduced it; the PROPOSED FIX does not fix it and would regress `across`, so this is REFUTED with a corrected fix.

What checks out. `main.app.sheet` is the scroller (document travel is 0 at every state and width I drove). `timeline.desk` at 1440x900 in `down` has 818px of travel. Set scrollTop 500, press ACROSS, press DOWN: scrollTop returns to 0 and the visible band goes from 23/37/44/51/65/79 to 16/23/37/44. Focus is correctly kept on the pressed `[data-layout-to]` and the live region announces; nothing records or restores the reading position. The handler at C:\Users\ethan\signal-studio-workspace\_wt-master-suite\docs\design\labs\master-suite-2026-08\src\timeline.js:2926-2941 does `C.mount()`, refocuses, announces — and touches no scroller. The characterisation of the gate is also accurate: `tools/orientation.mjs:55-87` asserts the measure flips, `aria-pressed`, focus, the announcement, and stale inline `left`/`top` — never place. Two small factual slips, not disqualifying: 818px is `timeline.desk`, not `owner-flight` (that is 1255px at the same size), and the pre-press visible set is 23/37/44/51/65/79, not 37/44/51/65/79.

Why the fix fails. I implemented it verbatim against its own repro. On the ACROSS→DOWN press, "the `.b-item` nearest the top of the visible measure" is evaluated in `across`, where every moment sits in one horizontal band — so the anchor is always the first item (`demo-audience-item-menu`, "16 days away") at across-offset 366. Restoring that item to that offset after the remount lands scrollTop at **6**, showing 16/23/37/44/51. That is the broken state to within six pixels. The information the finding wants back was destroyed one press earlier, when `across` clamped 500 to 0 against 81px of travel; an anchor recorded after the clamp cannot recover it.

Worse in the other direction. On DOWN→ACROSS the recorded anchor is "23 days away" at offset −30. `across` at 1440 has 81px of total travel and it is sheet chrome, not measure. Restoring −30 computes +396 and clamps to 81 — the scroll bottom — pushing the measure's own head, which carries the orientation control, off the top of the frame. The fix makes the new-and-unreviewed orientation strictly worse than landing at 0.

Severity: `defect`, not blocking or misleading. Nothing untrue is asserted and the toggle does what it says; scrollTop 0 is also the legitimate load state of `?layout=down`. But at the declared bar it is a visible wrongness, and it is an inconsistency with this module's own standard rather than a decision — `markPlace`/`takePlace` (src/timeline.js:2173-2206) is precisely this idiom, already written, and the orientation control is the one remount path that does not call it.

refuted.problem: The Stack's two planes put their body text on different left edges. Measured: the wordmark, the desk card's edge and every `.idxDay` heading sit at 130 (311 at 1920); the desk's writing column starts at 154 (335); the index's note text starts at 163 (344). Nine pixels apart, at every breakpoint, in both `notes.notebook` and `notes.seam`. Add the index row band at 120 and the row glyph at 136 and the sheet carries five left edges inside 43px.
refuted.why:
Three of the five numbers check out, the load-bearing one does not, and the fix is arithmetically hostile to an element the seat did not look at.

MEASURED (Playwright, `?v=paper&state=notes.notebook|notes.seam`, 390/768/1280/1440/1920). At 1280: `.wordmark`/`.top`/`.paperStack`/`.idxDay` = 130; `.topField`/`.readBody`/`.deskWrite` = 154; `.idxText` = 163; `.idxRow` band = 120. At 1920: 311 / 335 / 344 / 301. So the 130/154/163 observation is factually right, and the 9px is real and holds at 768, 1280, 1440 and 1920 (at 390 the desk card is not in this form at all, so "every breakpoint" is four of five).

BUT: "the row glyph at 136" is wrong. `.idxMark` measures left=130 — exactly on the rail, its box flush with the wordmark and the card edge; the 15px svg ink centres at 132.5. Nothing sits at 136. That kills the finding's rhetorical core. The real inventory is not five edges inside 43px: it is one rail at 130 carrying four objects (wordmark, desk card edge, day heading, glyph column), one documented -10px highlight bleed at 120 that is a background wash and not a text edge — the source comments it as the fix for a past defect where the row highlight ran past the column every other object resolves to — and two body-text edges, 154 and 163. Two edges, not five.

And those two are two different structures doing their conventional job: an elevated plane whose edge sits on the rail and whose interior is its own coordinate space (24px symmetric card padding), and a flat list row with a leading status column on the rail and its label inset by icon+gap (20+13). That is exactly what Linear does in a list next to a panel and what Stripe does in docs. Calling it a broken rail is taste stated as a defect; the counter-argument — that the same note's text moves 9px when it lifts — dies on the fact that it also changes measure from 875px to 496px and moves several hundred pixels vertically.

THE FIX IS WORSE THAN THE PROBLEM. Branch (a), 43 → 34, is only reachable by collapsing `column-gap` from 13px to 4px (10 padding + 20 glyph are both load-bearing: the 20px column holds a 15px svg, the 10px padding is welded to the -10px margin bleed). `.idxMark i` — the unread dot — is `position:absolute; right:-3px; width:6px` with a `0 0 0 2px var(--white)` halo. Measured: the dot's box runs to x=153 and its halo to 155, on all eight rows in the notebook state, against text at 163 — 8px clear. At a 34px inset the text starts at 154 and the halo lands on top of the first letter of every unread note title. The seat proposed a number that collides.

Branch (b), +9px on the desk card's left inset, makes an elevated card's padding asymmetric (33 left / 24 elsewhere) to chase a list below it — visibly wrong on the card itself — and breaks the frozen Notes fidelity master at four widths for a change not on the round's named list.

Severity: even granting the observation, this is refinement, not defect. Nothing is visibly wrong; two conventionally-inset text columns are 9px apart across a plane boundary.

refuted.problem: The widening gave the row width without giving it structure. The longest note text now renders 875px at 1280, 1028px at 1440 and 1146px at 1920 — about 160 characters on a single line at 15px. At the same time the chip column is pinned near the sheet's right edge, so the distance from the end of a note's text to its status chip runs 13–100px at 1280, 20–260px at 1440 and 20–378px at 1920. The rows that gained the most white are the short notes, which are the ones whose status matters most.
refuted.why:
Measurements verified and essentially exact — I drove notes.notebook at 1280/1440/1920 and read the geometry. Text column: 875 / 1035 / 1153px; longest rendered ink 875 / 1029 / 1146px; longest row 136 / 154 / 170 characters; end-of-text-to-chip gap 13–100 / 19–260 / 20–378px. Every number in the Problem is right. The conclusion drawn from them is not.

1. "The widening gave the row width without giving it structure" is factually wrong about the code. `.idxRow` is `grid-template-columns: 20px minmax(0,1fr) 76px 92px` — the metadata columns are fixed, and the CSS at :2955 states why in writing: the right-hand verticals hold the index down instead of stepping in and out with each timestamp. I measured what that vertical is worth: `.idxWhen`'s right edge lands at 1392 (1440) and 1691 (1920) — the *same* pixel as every `.idxDayTail` ("1 still to decide", "3 still to decide") on the day headings. The index has exactly one right-hand vertical and the row's chip pair is what ties the rows to the group heads. That is the structure; the variable gap is its cost, and it is the cost Linear, GitHub and Gmail all pay for the same return.

2. The row is not prose and the source argues so explicitly at :2390: `--stack` was raised 1060 → 1440 on the stated ground that it governs the index, "whose rows are scan lines rather than prose", while `--measure: 31em` still caps every surface carrying the person's own writing. The finding neither cites nor rebuts that argument — it reports a deliberate, written decision as an oversight, which the round notes specifically ask panellists not to do. And the "160 characters" is a 48-char ink lede followed by a grey `.idxText span` preview at `--ink-2` with a word-safe ellipsis: a snippet, scanned, not a line anybody reads to the end.

3. The load-bearing claim is unsupported: "the rows that gained the most white are the short notes, which are the ones whose status matters most." Nothing links note length to status importance, and the fixture contradicts it — the two widest gaps at 1920 are "Course reading for Thursday" (To decide) and "Quote from today that I want to keep" (Kept), one live and one filed.

4. The fix is self-contradictory and would regress the sheet. Its own numbers disagree: it asks for "≈840px at 15px, about 90 characters", but the measured artifact renders 130–136 characters in 875px, so 840px is ~130 characters and 90 characters is ~575px — a builder implementing the pixel and a builder implementing the count ship two different designs. It also says "keeping the `.idxRow` hover band full-bleed" and then "the sheet's surplus width then becomes margin rather than a gap inside the row"; both cannot hold. Full-bleed band + capped content = a 1440-wide hover highlight with ~370px of empty tail at 1920, which is worse than what is there. Worst of all, moving `.idxTag`/`.idxWhen` to sit immediately after a capped text column drags every timestamp ~325px left of the day-group tails it currently aligns with, destroying the index's only right-hand vertical and leaving "1 still to decide" floating over the middle of the rows beneath it.

At worst this is a refinement, not a defect: the product does what it says, asserts nothing untrue, and the growth is bounded — `--stack: min(100%, 1440px)` already stops the index at 1440, so 1153px / 170 characters is a fixed ceiling reached at 1920, not a runaway.

refuted.problem: The round asked whether three ratified tracking curves standing side by side are a system or three. Measured at 1440 on the same role — the small uppercase section label, the most repeated typographic object in the suite — the answer is three. Tasks: Geist Mono, 11px, 400, letter-spacing 1.1px (+0.10em). Timeline: Geist Mono, 11px, 400, 1.76px (+0.16em). Notes: Geist, 11px, 600, 0.825px (+0.075em). Two of those are identical in family, size and weight and differ only in tracking, with no defence available. The 15px body curves (Notes −0.012em, Timeline −0.015em) are 0.045px apart at that size and are not the problem; this is.
refuted.why:
The PROBLEM is real and every number checks out against the source and a driven measurement at 1440: Tasks .trayName/.tag = Geist Mono 11/400/1.1px (hardcoded 0.1em, off Tasks' own by-size ladder where --tr-11 is 0em); Timeline .b-measureHead/.b-behindLabel/.b-todayLabel = Geist Mono 11/400/1.76px (--track-label 0.16em); Notes .indexHead/.deskFact b = Geist 11/600/0.825px (--tr-cap 0.075em). Three treatments of one role, and the Tasks/Timeline pair differing only in tracking has no identity story. The round explicitly asked this question, so it is in scope, and the direction (converge) is right.

The FIX is wrong, and wrong in the way that makes the work worse rather than better, so this is REFUTED per the rubric. I enumerated every visible element carrying 1.76px in timeline.owner-flight at 1440: b-todayLabel x1, b-measureHead x1, b-behindLabel x1, b-layoutBtn x2, b-grab x7, b-foot x1, plus 3 unnamed - sixteen elements. The fix names three. .b-layoutBtn sits in the measure's own head bar immediately beside .b-measureHead, and the seven .b-grab controls sit on the measure that .b-measureHead labels. Retracking only the three named leaves a 0.10em head adjacent to a 0.16em orientation control and above seven 0.16em grabs - an intra-product split more visible than the cross-product one, on the `across` surface the round named as its largest risk. Notes is worse: --tr-cap feeds seven sites including .peelLabel and .specName, and I measured .deskFact b at y=108/159/225 and .peelLabel at y=295/376 in notes.seam at 1440 - same sheet, same viewport, ~70px apart. Converting .deskFact b and .indexHead to Geist Mono 400 while .peelLabel ("TURN THIS INTO A TASK", "THE TASK WORDING") stays Geist 600 fractures the micro-label register inside the seam, a protected object.

Two smaller errors. (1) .b-todayLabel is a sentence ("TODAY IS 16 JULY 2026", 878px wide), not a section eyebrow; it does not belong in the group being unified. (2) "Update the corresponding entry in each product's own tracking ladder" has no referent in Notes: --tr-cap is a single caps token feeding seven sites in a file whose stated rule is one curve by size with no seventh step, so it is all-seven-or-none, never two - and the fix as written also silently changes family and weight on those two Notes sites, which is a Notes register change, not a suite retracking.

SEVERITY: defect, not blocking or misleading. Nothing fails to work and nothing asserts an untruth; the three registers are never on screen together because only one product is visible at a time. It is a system inconsistency felt across a product switch on the most repeated micro-object. If the seat filed it higher than defect, that is overstated.

refuted.problem: The one object always on screen on a phone has unequal optical margins, and they differ per product. Tasks: bar spans 9→381, tiles run 28→373 — 19px of margin on the left, 8px on the right; and `.railAdd` (295→339) sits 2px from `.railAvatar` (341) while every other adjacent pair is 24px apart. Timeline: tiles run 35→373 — 26px left, 8px right, an 18px asymmetry on a 372px bar. Notes' dock is 8/8 but mixes three object sizes in one row (36px glyphs, 44px tiles, a 30px avatar) with gaps of 14, 3 and 16px. The account disc is 32px in the rail and 30px in the dock — one object, two sizes.
refuted.why:
The Tasks/Timeline half of the problem is real and I reproduced it exactly; the Notes half is factually wrong about the artefact, and the proposed fix does not fit the viewport it names. Measured live at 390 (Playwright, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper`):

CONFIRMED. Tasks: `.rail` 9→381, tiles 28→373 — 19px left, 8px right. `.railAdd` 295→339 with `.railAvatar` at 341 — a 2px gap. Timeline: tiles 34.75→373 — 25.75 left, 8 right. Both as claimed. The disc is 32px in `.rail` and 30px in Notes' dock — one object, two sizes, and COMPOSITION.md §6/§5 reconciled that disc's *type* (11px/0.075em/1.28) and left its *diameter* unreconciled, so this is a genuine residue the gates cannot see (audit.mjs's target floor is 28px, so 32 and 30 both pass).

The seat also under-describes it. The cause is `justify-content: space-around` on both `.rail` and `.railGroup`, so the bar has no rhythm at all — it is width-derived. Tasks' inter-tile gap measures 16.5px at 360, 24 at 390, 34 at 430, 120.5 at 600, 150.5 at 720, and the left margin grows 15→19→24→45→60 while the right stays pinned at 8. At 720 the Tasks bar has 60px of air on the left and 8px on the right. Timeline's gap is 37.5px where Tasks' is 24px at the same width — same object, two rhythms.

REFUTED on the Notes claims. The dock at 390 is not "one row": it is three stacked children — `.phoneField` 356×51, then two `.dockRow`s. The tiles in it are **36px, not 44px** (`.railGroup` children measure 229/265/301/337, 36px each, `border-radius: 10px`), and the gaps are 2px between glyphs, 6px rule→group, **0px** between the three suite tiles, 6px group→avatar. "44px tiles" and "gaps of 14, 3 and 16px" match nothing at 390 in any Notes state (notebook, seam, voice all identical). "Every other adjacent pair is 24px apart" in Tasks is also wrong — timeline→add is 19px.

REFUTED on the fix, which is the disqualifying part. A 44px box for every object plus a fixed 24px gap does not fit the phone it is written for. Tasks at ≤720 carries six objects: 6×44 = 264 plus 5×24 = 120 → 384px, inside a rail whose content box at 390 is 356px (372 − 2×8). It overflows by 28px at 390 and 58px at 360. Worse, the fix's two halves are mutually exclusive: with a fixed gap and a variable object count (Tasks 6, Timeline 5), you cannot also have 8px inset on both sides in both products — only `space-between` gives that. And "use the same 44px box in the Notes dock" is built on the false 44px measurement: the dock's neighbours are 36px glyphs and 36px tiles, so a 44px box would introduce the odd object rather than remove it, and would add height to a dock already 101px tall over the sheet.

refuted.seat: UX and information design — Orla, venue manager at The Orchard
refuted.problem: The carry model is announced correctly until the last step. Space says "Picked up Confirm marquee sides with the hire company."; each ArrowRight says "In progress, position 1 of 4." then "Review, position 1 of 3." Enter drops the card in the right lane and position — and the live region says "Showing the whole note." Nothing opened: no note panel is on screen after the drop (measured: no visible panel element). The drop's own confirmation is the Enter-opens-the-note handler's sentence firing over it.
refuted.why:
REFUTED — the finding is factually wrong about the code and about what it measured. Driven at 1440x960 on `?v=paper&state=tasks.board`, focusing `.card[data-id="demo-t-01"]` ("Confirm marquee sides with the hire company"):

1. **Enter does not drop the card.** After Space → ArrowRight → ArrowRight → Enter, the card still reads `aria-grabbed="true"`, still carries `data-force="moving"`, and the foot strip is still on screen reading "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company · ↑↓←→ move · Space drop · Esc cancel". Pressing Space afterwards is what drops it, announcing "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company dropped in the review column." Esc after Enter still cancels correctly: "Move cancelled. … is back in the to do column." Source: `_gate-suite.html` ~L9880-9912 — the drop is the `key === " "` branch (`if (carriedId === id) { … say(title + " dropped " + inLane(lane) + ".") }`); the `key === "Enter"` branch only toggles `openNoteId`. The seat mistook the carry model's *live* move for a drop: each ArrowRight relocates the card in the DOM immediately (measured: after Right1 demo-t-01 is in `doing`, after Right2 it is first in `review`), so it was already "in the right lane and position" before Enter was ever pressed.

2. **Something did open.** "Showing the whole note." is a true sentence. On Enter the card goes `aria-expanded` false→true, gains `data-open`, and `.cardNote` goes `max-height: 37.7px → none`, height 38px → 58px, colour `rgba(17,17,17,.72)` → `rgb(17,17,17)` (CSS L1079). The reveal is in-card by design, not a floating panel — the seat measured for "a visible panel element", found none, and concluded nothing happened.

3. **The artifact never advertises "Enter drops".** The card declares `aria-keyshortcuts="Space ArrowUp ArrowDown ArrowLeft ArrowRight"` and the carry strip prints `Space drop`. "Enter drops" appears only in the orchestrator's loose prose in the round brief, not in the product's own contract. Nothing here asserts anything untrue, so no class above refinement survives.

The proposed fix would make the work worse: it invents a second, unadvertised drop key, contradicts the strip and `aria-keyshortcuts` the operator is reading at that moment, and removes the only way to read a task's full note while deciding which lane it belongs in — which is exactly when an operator wants it. It would also strand `openNoteId` semantics (Enter would become a no-op on a carried card that the user had just opened).

refuted.seat: UX and information design — Orla, venue manager at The Orchard
refuted.problem: Five facts share one row and read as one kind of thing: "5 of 13 done" (inert text), "1 today" (hairline pill, toggles a board filter), "1 overdue" (solid ink pill, white text — also toggles a board filter), "5 with no day" (underlined text — opens the Planning drawer, not a filter), "Wedding season, day 11 of 97" (inert text). Three interactive, three unrelated treatments, two different kinds of action. Worse, state is not readable from any of them: measured at rest both filters are aria-pressed="false", yet "1 overdue" is painted rgb(17,17,17) on white — this system's on/primary fill, the same treatment as Get the link, Send to Tasks, Add task and the ACROSS toggle's on state — while "1 today" is transparent. Pressing "1 today" ON changes its background, colour, border and weight not at all (measured identical before and after); the only change is a small × appearing inside it. "5 with no day" carries neither aria-pressed nor aria-expanded.
refuted.why:
REFUTED on the central measurement and on the fix.

(1) The load-bearing claim is false. "State is not readable from any of them" and "Pressing '1 today' ON changes its background, colour, border and weight not at all... the only change is a small x" — the seat measured four properties that were never the state channel and missed the one that is. Driven at 1920 against `_gate-suite.html`, the today chip goes from `box-shadow: rgb(17,17,17) 0 0 0 1px inset` at rest to `rgba(17,17,17,0.72) 0 0 0 3px` pressed; the overdue chip goes from `none` to the same `0 0 0 3px`. Source: L1801 `[data-soft][aria-pressed="true"] { box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--ink-1), 0 0 0 3px var(--ink-4) }` and L1802 `[aria-pressed="true"] { box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--ink-4) }`. Both filters therefore already share ONE state channel — an outer halo — drawn identically on both regardless of their rest fill, which is exactly the property the finding says is absent. It is also a three-rank ladder, not a binary: hover 3px at wash-2 (0.08), pressed 3px at ink-4 (0.28), pressed+hover 3px at ink-2 (0.72). Plus the x glyph, plus `title` flipping to "Show all 13 tasks", plus aria-pressed, plus a live announcement ("Showing 1 task due today. 12 others are hidden."). Five channels, not one.

(2) "Three unrelated treatments" misreads two of the three. The filled/hairline split is not arbitrary and is not urgency-vs-nothing invented for the head: L1152-1160 states it explicitly, and the head chips are the card's own due-chips — `.when[data-t="overdue"]` is filled ink, `.when[data-t="today"]` is a transparent hairline, on every card on the board. The head fact and the card badge for the same task are the same object. And `.undated` is not "underlined text": it is `underline dotted` at rest going `underline solid` on hover (L1442-1451, confirmed live) — deliberately given text grammar rather than pill grammar precisely because it is a door, not a filter. So the row reads: two pills = filters (differentiated by the board's severity language), one dotted-underline word = a door. That is a legible three-way, not an accidental one.

(3) The fix would make the work worse and is the reason to refute even if (1) had held. Drawing the overdue chip as a hairline at rest severs it from `.when[data-t="overdue"]` on the cards below it — a filled ink badge on a card and a hairline badge in the head, same fact, two silhouettes. It also collapses rest-state overdue and rest-state today into the same pill, deleting the only severity rank in the band (the file's own note at L1311 calls the filled overdue chip "the board's whole emotional output"). And "move urgency into ink density on its text" cannot work: the chip's text is already ink-1 at 600, so there is no density left above it, and the leading-dot alternative adds a mark the specimen sheet does not carry. Net: lose a working cross-object correspondence to fix a state channel that already exists.

(4) The one true residue in the finding is the smallest sentence in it: `.undated` (L8551) carries no `aria-expanded` while the Planning ghost (L8564) does, and both are `data-act="planning"` toggling the same drawer (L9972). That is real, verified, and refinement-grade — the disclosure is still announced via `say("Planning open.")` and focus moving to `.drawer`; what is lost is only the button's own state when a screen-reader user tabs back to it with the drawer already open, at which point it is the close control and says nothing. It does not carry the rest of the finding.

Severity correction: the seat's framing implies a defect ("state is not readable"). Measured, nothing in this row is visibly wrong; the surviving item is a one-attribute a11y refinement.

refuted.seat: UX and information design — Orla, venue manager at The Orchard
refuted.problem: Press "1 overdue" and four of the five tray bodies render as literally nothing — measured innerText "(nothing)" for To do, Review, Waiting and Done. No line of copy, no restatement of what is hidden, and the "Add here" row is gone too. The only signals are an 11px mono "0/3" at the far right of each lane head and the black strip at the foot of the sheet. The product already owns the right answer: unfiltered, the empty Waiting lane says "Nothing held up." and offers "Add here". That designed empty state is not used in the state a person reaches far more often.
refuted.why: Driven at 1920 with the "1 overdue" chip pressed. The premise is a DOM artefact read as a visual one. `.trayBody` innerText is empty for To do / Review / Waiting / Done because those bodies are `display: none` — `src/tasks.css:1577-1587` collapses a filtered empty lane to a 52px head with the pip at rgba(17,17,17,0.14), the name at --ink-2 and the count at --ink-3. Measured: todo/review/waiting/done all h=52, top=131; doing h=231 with its body and its "Add here" row alive (addDisp "flex"). Nothing renders as a void with copy missing from it; the lane physically flattens, and that flattening IS the state — one tall lane, four flat rules, readable in a glance from ten feet. The finding calls the head "the only signal" and never registers that the lane's height changed. Second, it is already answered on three channels: the head carries "0/3", the aria-label carries "To do, 0 of 3 shown" (and takes the same branch for a lane that was empty anyway — "Waiting, nothing here yet", no ratio of nothing to nothing), and the foot strip reads "Showing 1 overdue task. 12 others are hidden." with "Show all work", which is also what the live region announced. When the filter matches nothing at all there is a designed centred block: "Nothing matches." + the same sentence + "Show all work" (`src/tasks.js:670-678`). Third, the exact fix proposed has been built and removed twice, with both removals recorded in the source: "Under a filter, five columns saying the same sentence read as a rendering fault" and, on the lane note specifically, "the column already carries its name, its count of total, and the foot strip's whole sentence. A note here is the same fact a fourth time" (`src/tasks.js:600-635`). "3 here, none overdue" is a prose transcription of "0/3" printed five times. Fourth, the fix's own premise is wrong against source: "a new task would not match" is false — adding a task while the overdue filter is on turns the filter off and says so ("The overdue filter is off so you can see it.", `src/tasks.js:1765`), which is why the surviving lane keeps its Add row rather than hiding it. Restoring the lane description line would also reprint "Agreed and ready to start." over a lane showing nothing, which is the false-in-context copy that removal fixed. There is a real observation adjacent to this one — a filtered board leaves roughly 800px of white below a single 231px lane — but that is a composition question about the sheet, not a missing empty state, and this finding does not make it.

refuted.seat: UX and information design — Orla, venue manager at The Orchard
refuted.problem: The across measure is the largest new surface in this round and it does not fit at two of the five declared viewports. Measured at 1280×900 and at 1024×900: the three below-the-line moments sit at y 832–927 in a 900px viewport, so "Send the invitations", "Choose the evening music" and "Venue walk-through" have their dates cut and all three of their Edit controls (b-grab, y 877–927) entirely below the fold. The sheet scrolls, so nothing is lost permanently — but the orientation's whole promise, which the gate itself states as "the whole approach is in one frame", is delivered as the top row only. The gate proves that promise by checking horizontal scroll and never looks down.
refuted.why:
The PROBLEM reproduces almost exactly; the FIX is wrong on all three of its named levers, and two of its factual claims are overstated. Refuted on the fix, per the rubric.

What I measured (chromium, `?v=paper&state=timeline.owner-flight&layout=across`). The real fold is `main.app.sheet`'s bottom, not the window: at 1280x900 the sheet is y18-882 (clientHeight 864, scrollHeight 1236). The measure runs y506-942, so it overruns the sheet by 60px. Below-the-line copy sits at 832-927 and the three `.b-grab` "Edit" controls at 877-905, 899-927, 877-905 — all three outside the sheet's client box (only ~5px of two of them peek). Identical at 1024x900, 1152x900, 1300x900, 1340x900. So the seat's y-numbers are right, and against the true fold (882) rather than the window (900) the "entirely below the fold" claim on the Edit controls is actually stronger than stated.

Where the finding is factually loose: (1) "two of the five declared viewports" — the five declared are 390x844, 768x1024, 1280x900, 1440x960, 1920x1000. 1024x900 is not one of them; at 768 the layout is `down` and the measure never goes across. It is ONE of five, not two. (2) "have their dates cut" — only one of the three dates is cut (`Sat 29 Aug`, 880-895 vs fold 882). `Sat 8 Aug` (858-873) and `Sat 19 Sep` (858-873) are fully visible. What is uniformly lost is the Edit row, not the dates.

What the seat got right and is worth keeping: `tools/orientation.mjs` really does prove "the whole approach is in one frame" with `!m.scrolls`, where `scrolls` is `span > usable` — horizontal only, at every width, and it opens every desk width at height 960. At 1280x960 the measure bottom is 942 and the sheet fold is 942 — flush to the pixel. The gate passes because it runs 60px taller than the height the artifact's own shots declare.

The cause is not a missing height derivation, which is what the fix assumes. `placeAcross` already derives the band from measured label heights. The 60px comes from a HORIZONTAL rule spending VERTICAL budget: at 1280 the above-lane pair at 37d(x455) and 51d(x625) are 170px apart, `ACROSS_LABEL` is 168 and the collision test demands `left < lane[rank] + 14`, so 51d is pushed to rank 1; `--rule-y` is the above band, so one rank above costs 128px and shoves the entire below lane off the sheet (`--rule-y` 154 -> 282, band 308 -> 436). At 1366x768 there is no rank at all and it still overruns by 64px, so short height is a second, independent cause the fix does not separate.

Why the fix is refused. (a) "tightening the label leading" spends the ratified type ladder to pay for a layout — leading, leading-role and leading-ladder are all gated at zero drift across three products, and this would take them red; it is also the exact class the lessons library already paid for. (b) "tightening the stagger offset" has 14px of air per step to give; zeroing it saves ~42px of the 60 needed at 1280x900 and ~142 short at 1280x800, and buys it by making labels touch — which `no two labels collide` then catches. (c) "fall back to down at that height" is the worst of the three: the layout is decided once at load from WIDTH (`orientation.mjs` asserts 1920/1440/1024 -> across, 900/390 -> down) and `?layout=across` plus the `[data-layout-to]` control are explicit contracts. Implemented as written, the flagship new surface would default to `down` at 1280x900 and 1024x900 — it would not appear at all at the commonest laptop height — and pressing "Across" at a short viewport would hand back "Down". That trades a defect for a control that does not do what it is pressed to do.

Severity: the seat did not overstate — it says plainly the sheet scrolls and nothing is lost, which I confirmed (sheet scrollMax 372 at 1280x900; focusing a below-line Edit scrolls it into view and it lands inside the box). Nothing false is asserted in words: the toggle's accessible name is "Draw the whole approach across the page", which is true, and "one frame" lives only in a code comment and a gate label. The centre label's cut glyph declares the fold. So: defect, not misleading and not blocking — but a strong defect on the round's largest new surface at a declared viewport, and the fold lands precisely on the control row so three of six moments read as having no editor. Worth fixing this round; it just does not gate the stopping rule.

refuted.seat: UX and information design — Orla, venue manager at The Orchard
refuted.problem: At 390 the seam state renders neither the note nor the peel. Measured: the desk's read body and the whole .peel subtree resolve to zero boxes with offsetParent null; the tab order is head, chip, two head actions, one index row, the compose field, dock — no desk, no peel. What is on screen is the ledger, "ALREADY IN TASKS · 3 so far, and every note stayed here", three finished tasks, and roughly 600px of empty ground above the dock. The gesture itself is fine on a phone by the real route: tapping an index row lifts the note, a real selection in the read body enables peel, and Send to Tasks renders at 138×44 well inside the fold. So this is the narrow layout dropping the two panes that carry the argument and keeping the one that does not.
refuted.why:
The OBSERVATION is confirmed; the FIX is wrong, and two of the measurements are wrong, so it is refuted as filed.

Confirmed by driving `?v=paper&state=notes.seam` at 390x844 (chromium, file://): `[data-app="notes"] .desk` computes `display:none` (source: the `@media (max-width: 720px)` block, `[data-app="notes"] .desk { display: none; }`), `.readBody` and `.peel` both resolve to 0x0 with `offsetParent` null, and the page is the head, the "ALREADY IN TASKS - 3 so far, and every note stayed here" ledger, three Done rows, then dead ground. At 768 the same state renders desk 668x455, readBody 527x55, peel 496x258, so the break is ≤720 only. The strongest form of it is one the seat did not file: open the seam at 1440 (peel 496x258, send 138x36), then narrow to 390, and the picked words and the open peel draft go to zero boxes with no notice and no phone affordance to reach them - a real phone landscape-to-portrait rotation, not just a deep link. Neither `verify.mjs`'s seam section nor `interaction-check.mjs` asserts anything about the seam below 720, and no notes.seam frame at 390 was supplied, so this is genuine gate blindness.

Two evidence errors: the tab order at 390 has THREE `.idxRow`s (Clear Sunday / Chase linen / Send registrar), not one; and the empty ground is ~367px (last row bottom 367, dock top 734), not "roughly 600px" - the seat appears to have read device pixels off a 2x shot.

The fix is refuted on a false premise. The seat says "the narrow layout drop[s] the two panes" and proposes building a stacked seam at ≤720. But the phone already has that stacked layout and it already works: driven with `hasTouch`, tapping an index row in notes.notebook at 390 tears the desk out of the DOM and renders a phone reader (`.readBody` 358x110 at top 112), `[data-act="peel"]` is live at 305x44, pressing it opens `.peel` at 358x363 spanning top 300 to bottom 663 with `[data-act="send"]` at 138x44 at top 601, and send lands the card. The dock sits at top 734 - it does not overlap the peel, and `--peel-h` / `--walk-reserve: 137px` show the reservation machinery is already built. So "reserve the peel's band so the dock never sits over it" fixes a problem that does not exist, and "stack the seam at ≤720" builds a plane that already exists. What is actually broken is narrower: the seam ENTRY STATE never enters the phone's own reader - it sets only the desk-side seam, which ≤720 hides, and it filters the index to the 3-row ledger so there is no route back to any of the 14 notes (only the head chip escapes, and it swaps to "STILL TO DECIDE / 7 behind this one").

Severity is defect, not blocking: the product does do what it says on a phone by the real route, end to end, so this is a state that fails to compose itself for the narrow layout plus a silent drop on a cross-720 resize - visibly wrong, passable.

refuted.seat: UX and information design — Orla, venue manager at The Orchard
refuted.problem: At the shipping density (tasks.dense, 1920×1000) three of five trays overflow — by 418px, 255px and 118px — and each cuts its last card mid-line with a hard edge. Measured on the overflowing trayBody: mask-image none, no ::before/::after gradient, no rule. The only gradients anywhere in the Tasks sheet are the two horizontal lane fades on .sheet, so the vertical edge is the one that was missed. The same edge cuts a card at the TOP of the tray once scrolled, seen at 390 in dense. "Price the extra hour on the bar for Nora & Cian" ends with its ENQUIRY label sliced through the middle of the letterforms, and the "Add here" row sits below the cut, so the cut looks like a fault rather than an edge.
refuted.why:
REFUTED — the finding measured the wrong element and both halves of its fix already ship.

"no ::before/::after gradient, no rule" is false. The indicator is on `.tray`, not `.trayBody` (source comment says why: "an inset shadow on the scroller is painted under its own content and a card at the foot covers the very line that says there is more of it"). At _gate-suite.html:952-962 there is `.tray::before` / `.tray::after`, 1px, `var(--line)` = rgba(17,17,17,0.08), z-index 2, positioned at `--body-top` / `--body-bottom`. Driven at tasks.dense/1920x1000 I measured, per tray: todo afterOpacity 1 at top 727px, doing 1, done 1, review 0, waiting 0 — on exactly the three that overflow and off on the two that do not. Computed after layout at _gate-suite.html:10379-10402 from the content's own offset extent (deliberately not scrollHeight, "which includes the FLIP settle"), toggled on every scroll, both edges independently. Scrolling todo to 232 flips `::before` to opacity 1. That is precisely "computed after layout so it appears only when something is genuinely hidden, and on both edges independently" — the finding proposes the feature that is in front of it.

Second half, "snap the scroll to a whole card," also already ships: `.trayBody` carries `scroll-snap-type: y mandatory; scroll-padding: 20px 0` (line 940). Live: asked scrollTop 100 → rests 126; asked 260 → rests 232. At every snapped rest the card above the fold shows exactly 12px — its own bottom padding, no glyph — matching the source's stated 32px-of-clearance arithmetic.

The proposed gradient would make the work worse, and the source records it being tried: "a 26px ramp over a 19px line box then renders a bold title at about 40% ink — the one thing on this sheet that read as a rendering fault rather than a decision." Reinstating it re-opens a fixed defect. Note also the fix is not implementable as stated: `scroll-snap-align: start` aligns card tops, and card heights here are variable (79/98/136px measured), so no snap position can make the tray's *bottom* land on a card boundary — the column height would have to be quantized to a card height that does not exist.

The observation underneath is partly accurate and I confirmed it: at rest the fold does cross glyph boxes — "Enquiry" cut 7.5px into a 14px box in todo, "Aisling & Tom" 8.9 into 16 in doing, a two-line cardTitle 32.2 into 38.1 in done. The overflow numbers 418/255/118 are right as max-scroll (the code's own extent measure reads 410/247/110; the 8px delta is trayBody's padding-bottom). But a clipped word sitting behind an explicit 1px fold rule is the Linear/Stripe idiom, not a fault — and lessons.md ("Overflow is designed or it is a guillotine. Any edge that can clip gets a measured fade **or snap** — measured after layout") is satisfied twice over here, so the class is not creeping back. Severity is refinement at most, not a defect: nothing is wrong.

refuted.seat: UX and information design — Orla, venue manager at The Orchard
refuted.problem: The sentences themselves are right and well written — "Every project in one list. Not here yet.", "What came in while you were working. Not here yet.", "Guides and support. Not here yet.", "Your account, in Signal Studio. Not here yet." — and each is announced on a live region when the door is pressed. But each lives only in title, while the same button carries aria-label="Home" / "Inbox" / "Help and settings" / "Orla, venue manager", which wins. A screen-reader user landing on the door hears "Home, button, dimmed" and nothing else; the sentence exists for the mouse and for the press, not for the name.

The architecture lock says three products are mounted at once so "nothing a person was doing is lost when they glance at another", and the router's own comment says the leaving product "keeps its DOM, its scroll, its focus and every fact it was holding". Two of those three are false. Hiding with `display: none` discards every descendant scroll position, and nothing captures or restores them. Measured at 1280×800, tasks.board: `.board` scrollLeft 160 and the Done `.trayBody` scrollTop 126, focus on `.card`; press Timeline, press Tasks — both scroll offsets are 0 and focus is on `MAIN.sheet` (tabindex −1). The load-bearing measurement is wrong. I drove `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board` in Chromium 149 at 1280x800 and reproduced the exact scenario the seat describes: `.board` scrollLeft = 160, Done `.trayBody` scrollTop = 126, focus on `.card[data-id]`; click `[data-rail="timeline"]`, click `[data-rail="tasks"]`, wait 800ms. Result: boardLeft 160, doneTop 126 — unchanged. Same by the keyboard route (focus the tile, Enter, Enter). Notes is the same: `.index` scrollTop 180 -> 180, not 0. At 390x844 via the dock tiles, board scrollLeft 599 -> 599, where mandatory snap makes the reset most likely. Timeline `across` at 1440 has no descendant scroller at all (the only elements reporting overflow are `.b-vh` visually-hidden text nodes), so there is nothing to lose there.

The premise behind the numbers is also false as stated: "Hiding with `display: none` discards every descendant scroll position." I ran a control in the same page — a fresh `overflow:auto` div scrolled to 200, its parent set `display:none`, forced layout, unhidden, one rAF: scrollTop is still 200. Blink preserves scroll offsets across a `display:none` round trip on current engines (the CSSOM-View scroll-state preservation behaviour), and I confirmed the same by toggling `[hidden]` on `#tasks`'s `.app` host directly, bypassing `go()` entirely: 160/126 in, 160/126 out. So the router's comment at :7757 ("keeps its DOM, its scroll…") is true, and the architecture lock's claim holds for scroll.

That leaves only the focus half, and there the finding describes a documented deliberate decision as an oversight. `go()` at :7778 says so in as many words: "Focus moves to the sheet the spine just opened… A switch that leaves focus on the tile leaves a keyboard in the chrome." It cannot be otherwise: `apply()` at :7824 sets `inert` on the leaving host, so the card that had focus is inside an inert subtree the moment the switch commits — focus on it is not restorable by staying, only by re-granting. Landing on the arriving `MAIN.sheet` with `tabindex="-1"` and announcing `LABEL + summary()` on the live region is the standard region-arrival pattern, and `openTask()` already opts out (`{focus:false}`) precisely so `api.reveal(id)` can take focus to the card when the seam is the reason for the switch. I confirmed the announcement fires and the sheet takes focus. "First Tab lands on `.late "1 today"`, nine stops from the card" is accurate but is the consequence of that pattern, not evidence against it — and it is an argument about a decision, offered here as a defect.

The fix is worse than the problem twice over. Its scroll half is dead code against a platform that already preserves the offsets. Its scroll half is also actively dangerous: Tasks' own `restorePlace()` at :10556 suspends `scroll-snap-type` for exactly one frame while it writes `board.scrollLeft`, with a comment naming the bug it fixes ("every tick on a phone threw the operator back to To Do"). A second, router-level `scrollLeft` write inside `requestAnimationFrame` lands in the frame where snap has just been restored, which is the precise condition that produced that bug. The fix would re-open a paid-for defect to solve a non-existent one. And "only then announce" pushes the live-region write behind a rAF and behind a focus move, which is the ordering most likely to make a screen reader drop or truncate the arrival — a real regression in the one thing that currently works.

refuted.problem: The orientation control renders visible, enabled and pressable at 768 and at 390 — it is not gated by the same breakpoint that chooses the default.
