Measured: at 768 the measure is scrolls="true", scrollWidth 640 / clientWidth 474, maxScroll 166; at 390, maxScroll 308–310. Setting scrollLeft to max puts the "Wedding day" label at 487–655 inside a measure box of 185–659 (768) and 189–357 inside 29–361 (390) — `inside: true` at every width tested. So "clipped away with no route to it" is wrong; #tl not scrolling is precisely the design, because the overflow is contained in the object that owns it rather than dragged across the whole sheet.
- The keyboard route works too. Focusing the far-right `.b-grab` ("Edit") in owner-flight scrolls the measure to 164 (768) and 308 (390) automatically. There is a reachable route by pointer, by touch and by keyboard.
- The source states this as a decision in as many words: "below it the track scrolls rather than lying about the proportion" (ACROSS_FLOOR block, ~line 15229), and ACROSS_FLOOR was moved 14 → 8 specifically so 1280 and 1024 fit. This is a documented answer, not an oversight.

The fix is wrong on its own numbers. There is no 900px across/down breakpoint. The default is `window.innerWidth >= 1024` in JS (line ~17643) and the across horizon grid is `@media (min-width: 1024px)` (line 6477); the 900px media queries at 440/2160/3726 are suite chrome and unrelated. Worse, 900 is not even the fit threshold: measured with ?layout=across, the track still scrolls at 900 (max 34) and at 950 (max 2), and first fits at ~960 (1000 → scrolls="false", px 8.61). So the proposed cut line leaves the alleged defect live from 900–959 and removes a composition that fits from 960–1023. Cutting at the correct number would still be cutting a working scroller.

The fix would also break a stated contract — "The reader may say otherwise at any time, and ?layout= says it for them" — turning a deep link into one that silently disagrees with itself, and it would need re-running the 44 orientation assertions plus the four-width fidelity check.

Finally, "at 390 it is pressable" is a fixture artefact, not a product fact: `acrossAllowed` keys on `data-medium`, which each state declares. The actual phone state, `timeline.phone`, renders no control at all (ctrlExists: false, medium: phone). "A phone opens on down" is already literally true. What the finding drove was an A4/desk fixture forced into a 390 window.

Severity is overstated by three classes. Nothing is unreachable and nothing untrue is asserted, so this is at most a refinement about affordance, not blocking.

refuted.problem: Every other region of the board re-derives under a filter and does it beautifully: the tray heads switch to `1/3`, `2/3`, `3/5`, and the empty state reads "No overdue task is on the board for Mara & Finn. All 13 are hidden." with a `Show all work` escape. The sheet head does not. Measured: press `.who` ("Mara & Finn") — 7 of 13 cards remain, the overdue card (`Order tonic and the good olives`, tagged BAR) is removed, and the head still reads `5 of 13 done · 1 today · 1 overdue · 5 with no day`. Press `1 overdue` on top of that and the board renders "Nothing matches. All 13 are hidden." while the head, 400px above it, still says `1 overdue`.
refuted.why:
The measurement is right and I reproduced it exactly at 1440 (Playwright, tasks.board): pressing `.who` leaves 7 of 13 cards, tray counts switch to 1/3, 2/3, 1/2, 0, 3/5, and `.headFacts` still reads "Thu 16 Jul · 5 of 13 done · 1 today · 1 overdue · 5 with no day · Wedding season, day 11 of 97"; adding `1 overdue` renders "Nothing matches. No overdue task is on the board for Mara & Finn. All 13 are hidden." with the head unchanged. But the premise that this is an oversight is wrong, and the fix is wrong in both branches it offers.

(1) It is a stated rule, not a miss. `_gate-suite.html:8128` — "The header counts the whole project. The board shows what is being looked at. Filtering must never change what '5 of 13 done' means." — sits directly above `tasksFor()`, the accessor the finding wants the head to adopt. The head's row is a season ledger, not a view summary: `5 of 13 done` sits between the date and `Wedding season, day 11 of 97`, a figure that cannot be filtered either. The board already answers "what am I looking at" in three voices — tray `n/total`, the live sentence ("Showing 7 tasks for Mara & Finn. 6 others are hidden."), and the empty state with its `Show all work` escape. This file elsewhere refuses to print "the same fact a fourth time" (the `trayNote` comment at 8642). Reporting it as an argument would have been fair; reporting it as a region nobody derived is not.

(2) Fix option A ("show the filtered figure in `n/total`") makes three things worse, only one of which the finding checked. Its own example `3/5 done` is correct, but `0/1 overdue` is not the general case. The `today` and `late` filters are mutually exclusive (`9946-9958`: turning one on clears the other) and `timeOf().kind` is exclusive, so under `lateOnly` the today chip would *always* render `0/1 today` while pressing it yields 1 task — a new false statement, worse than the one being fixed. Under `lateOnly` alone the ledger would read `0/1 done` beside "day 11 of 97". And `5 with no day` opens Planning, which I drove: under `who=Mara & Finn` it still lists all five undated tasks. A derived `3/5 with no day` would be contradicted by the room it opens one click later.

(3) Fix option B ("append 'of all 13'") appends a total to a line that already says "of 13" — redundancy, and it does not touch the chips, which are the only part that is actually false.

(4) One factual overstatement: the head is 111px above the empty block at 1440 (`.headFacts` y=37, `.emptyBoard` y=148), not 400px.

The residue that is genuinely true is much smaller than the finding claims, and it is not a number — it is one `title` string. Under an active couple filter the overdue chip's tooltip still reads "Show only the 1 overdue task" while pressing it shows none. That is a control promising an outcome it will not deliver, and the file already reasons about this class one screen away (`9186`: the overdue filter releases itself when the last overdue task is completed). At the declared bar that is a refinement bordering on a small defect, not a systemic accessor mismatch.

refuted.problem: One string, one slot, three sheets of one application, three different objects. Tasks: 20px / 600 / `#111` / −0.026em, at x 207 y 35. Notes: 15px / 400 / ink at 72% / −0.012em, at x 389 y 38. Timeline: 11px / 400 / ink at 72% / +0.04em mono caps, at x 196 y 110. Press a spine tile and the name of the venue nearly halves in size, drops a weight, loses a third of its ink, flips from tight to loose tracking, and moves 180px sideways and 75px down. This is the visible version of the letterfit question the gate could not answer: at 13px the three tracking curves differ by 0.065px per character and nobody will ever see it, but this nobody can miss.
refuted.why:
The raw numbers are mostly right but the argument built on them fails, and the fix would re-open a documented defect.

1. THE TRACKING LEG IS BACKWARDS. The finding reads "flips from tight to loose tracking" as drift and calls it "the visible version of the letterfit question the gate could not answer." It is a shell-declared SIZE ramp working correctly: `_gate-suite.html:553-554` declares `--tr-19: -0.026em; --tr-14: -0.014em; --tr-11: 0em`, and Notes re-ratifies `--tr-14: -0.012em` in its own scope at :2362. Tasks' venue is 20px on --tr-19, Notes' is 15px on --tr-14, Timeline's is 11px mono near --tr-11. Tracking loosening as size falls is the ramp doing its job. The gate's open letterfit question is about three curves at the SAME size; this string is set at three DIFFERENT sizes, so it demonstrates nothing about that question.

2. THE TIMELINE LEG IS DOUBLY MIS-DESCRIBED. `.b-where` is not caps: the rule at :6020 overrides :5065's `text-transform: uppercase` with `text-transform: none`, and computed style measures `text-transform: none`. And it is not a third sheet head — I drove all three Timeline states at both orientations: `.b-where` renders ONLY in `timeline.owner-flight`, inside the owner's `.b-bar` above the measure. In `timeline.desk` and `timeline.phone` the venue name is not painted anywhere. So "one slot, three sheets" is actually two sheet heads plus one owner-bar label present in one of three Timeline states.

3. THE CITED PRECEDENT ARGUES THE OPPOSITE. `#deck .word` at :399 hoists exactly ONE property — the tracking curve — and the comment above it states the doctrine: "The full stop after the word stays product-scoped — it is ink in Tasks and indigo in Notes, and both locks defend their own." :399 is precedent for hoisting the shared curve while leaving role expression product-scoped. The finding invokes it to justify hoisting size, weight, ink AND position — the exact case that comment was written to deny, and which the round notes list as a deliberate decision.

4. THE FIX RE-OPENS A FIXED DEFECT. The comment at :714-718 records why headName is 20/600: "Four sizes inside a 2px band, all at 600, gave the top of the scale no rank at all — and with Planning open the drawer's h2 was setting the same venue name larger than the board's own h1." The drawer h2 is 16px/600 (:1568). Unifying the venue down to Notes' 15px/400/72% puts the drawer's h2 back above the board's own h1.

5. THE FIX'S PREMISE IS FALSE FOR TASKS. It says each product keeps "its own subject line beneath it (the board's project...)". In Tasks the project IS the venue: `B.workspace` = "The Orchard, events" and `projects: [{label: "The Orchard, events"}]` (:6586, :7094). `.headFacts` is date/counts/chips, not a subject. Hoisting the venue out of Tasks' h1 leaves the board with no title, or prints the same string twice.

6. "ONE POSITION" IS UNREACHABLE. x207/y35, x389/y38 and x196/y110 differ because the wordmarks differ in width, the rail geometry differs, and Timeline's is a bar above the measure. Tasks' head also restructures to a `data-head="stack"` grid below 1200px of sheet where headName takes its own row (:784).

What survives is smaller than claimed and is refinement, not defect: a title set as a title on one sheet and a context caption on another is correct hierarchy, not an error.

refuted.problem: The round widened Notes' content column 1060 → 1440 to stop painting the sheet white for no reason. Measured after the change: the desk plane spans x 100–1902 and its last ink is at x 989 ("Other ways in"). 913px — 50.7% of the top plane — carries nothing at 1920. In notes.seam it is worse: the desk's facts stop at ~1040 and the peel sheet is 517px wide at x 348, so a block roughly 700×490 in the top half of the most important state in the product is empty white. The index below it does use the new width. The two planes now disagree about where the composition's right edge is.
refuted.why:
Measured in Chromium at 1920x1000 against `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=notes.notebook|notes.seam`, three of the finding's four load-bearing facts are wrong, including the headline.

1. **"The desk plane spans x 100–1902."** No. `.desk` is a transparent, unpainted centring wrapper (`display:flex; justify-content:center`, master.html:2542). The painted top plane is `.pile > .top`, measured **x311–1691, w1380** at 1920. The finding measured the *sheet*, not the plane, and then attributed the sheet's margin to the plane.

2. **"The two planes now disagree about where the composition's right edge is."** This is the finding's whole argument and it is false at every width. Measured right edges: desk `.top` 1691 / index content 1691 (`.index` 281–1721 with 30px `--gutter`) at 1920; 1392 / 1392 at 1440; 1232 / 1232 at 1280. They agree to the pixel — which is what `--stack: min(100%,1440px)` exists to do, and the source comment at master.html:2386 states it: "One column for both planes… `--stack` is what the two planes agree on."

3. **The numbers.** Rightmost ink in `.top` is "Read a photo" at **x1089** (not 989) in notebook and "Written, 4 days ago" at **x1006** (not ~1040) in seam. Against the real plane edge 1691 that is **602px, 43.6% of the 1380px paper** — not 913px / 50.7%. The peel is **496px wide at x335**, not 517 at 348; the finding's peel numbers are the PNG's device coordinates (1.0417×) read off the frame and never converted, which is what inflated the rest.

4. **"The peel sheet overlaps beneath the note."** `.readBody` bottom y191, `.peel` top y267 — a 76px gap, no overlap with the note at all. The only overlap is the peel's top edge tucking **10px** under `.paperStack`'s bottom (277 vs 267): that is the direction's peel-off depth signature, not an accident.

What survives is much smaller than stated: `.deskAside` is an 802px grid track (`grid-template-columns: 496px 802px`) whose three short facts are left-aligned, so the ink stops well short of the paper's right edge. That is real but it is **not new to this round and not a disagreement** — the same run of blank measures 324px at 1280 and 484px at 1440, and it reads as the margin of a sheet of paper, which is precisely what a plane called "the desk carrying the newest paper" is meant to read as. Refinement at most.

The proposed fix fails on both branches. Branch A — "hold the desk at a stated width and centre it against the index's measure" — **is already the shipped implementation**, verbatim; there is nothing to do. Branch B — move the peel sheet beside the note into the desk's right half — redesigns a protected object. The locked architecture says "the seam peels a second smaller sheet off the note" and the brief says polish the gesture, do not redesign it; a right-hand side-by-side panel is an inspector, not a peeled sheet, and the depth reading (a second, smaller, lower sheet lifted off the first) is the entire visual argument. It would also have to displace `.deskAside`'s three facts, which have no other home on that plane.

refuted.problem: 1024 is a default `across` width per the gate. Measured there, the seven labels occupy four distinct vertical bands (y 543, 649, 671, 832) instead of the two they occupy at 1920, `Final guest numbers` is lifted a whole tier and joined to its tick by a bare 160px leader, and the below-line row (`Send the invitations`, `Choose the evening music`, `Venue walk-through`) is cut by the sheet's bottom edge at 884 with no fade. At 960 it is six bands spread over 417px and the measure line itself is below the fold — you cannot see the horizon and its labels at the same time. The label box is a fixed 168px at every width from 768 to 1920, so widening the stage bought more space between ticks and not one extra character of room for the words.
refuted.why:
REFUTED on the fix, not on the problem. The problem is real and I reproduced almost every number by driving it (chromium, `?v=paper&state=timeline.owner-flight`, no forced layout).

CONFIRMED: `across` is the default at >=1024 (`_gate-suite.html` ~line 17646: `window.innerWidth >= 1024 ? "across" : "down"`). At 1024x900 the seven `.b-copy` tops are exactly 543 / 649 / 671 / 832 — four bands, as claimed — against 521 / 543 / 704 at 1920, which is two lanes (521 vs 543 is only a two-line title in one bottom-aligned band at 616). `Final guest numbers` is `data-rank="1"`, lifted one whole `--step` (128px) and joined to its tick by a bare hairline `::after` — 148px, not the 160px claimed, a minor slip. `--rule-y` goes 154px at 1920/1440 to 282px at 1280/1024 and the measure grows 308 -> 436px. `main.app.sheet` is the scroll container (clientHeight 864 at 1024x900, rect bottom 882); the below-line row bottoms at 905/927, so at first paint `Send the invitations`, `Choose the evening music` and `Venue walk-through` are sliced mid-word at the sheet edge with no fade. At 1024x768 it is worse than the finding says: the rule itself is below the fold and the day-counts 16/37/79 are cut through the middle of the glyphs. `ACROSS_LABEL = 168` is a hard constant used at every width — confirmed, `copyW` is 168 at 960, 1024, 1280, 1440 and 1920.

Two corrections: at 960 `across` is NOT a default (it falls to `down`; the reader must press the control), and forced there it is five distinct bands, not six — the 417px spread is exactly right.

REFUTED because the fix is wrong in two of its three clauses, and the central one makes the artifact worse.

(a) `min(168px, gap-to-next-tick)` is backwards. `blockH` — the tallest rendered `.b-copy` — is what sets `--step`, and `--step` x rank is the band height that is doing the clipping. Narrowing the box wraps titles onto more lines, raises `blockH`, raises `step`, and makes the band TALLER. And it does not even remove the collision it targets: the only above-lane collision at 1024 is 37 -> 51 (14 days, 125px). Two 125px boxes centred 125px apart still overlap by the 14px pad, so `Final guest numbers` goes to rank 1 anyway. Read the other way (nearest tick on the rail, 63px at 1024), `Choose the evening music` becomes about five lines. Both readings lose.

(b) "cap the stack at two bands each side" is a no-op at both widths cited. Deepest rank is already 1 above / 0 below at 1024 and 1 / 1 at 960 — i.e. at most two bands per side already. Nothing would ever be folded, so the "and 2 more between 22 Aug and 5 Sep" summary never fires in this fixture. Where it did fire it would take moments off a measure whose locked direction is that position IS the quantity, and would strip those moments of their `.b-grab` editor and their entries in `role="list" aria-label="What is still ahead, nearest first"` — a behaviour and a11y regression.

(c) is the only right clause, and it misdiagnoses. The band already IS measured in real layout — `placeAcross` reads `awayH`/`blockH` off rendered boxes and writes `measureEl.style.height`. What is never consulted is the sheet's visible height.

The deeper thing the finding missed: at 8.94px/day a lane needs ~21 days between labels (84 + 84 + 14 = 182px). Greedy over 16/23/37/44/51/65/79 dies at 51 on both lanes, so NO two-lane packing exists at 1024. A third band is forced by geometry; the lever is what a band costs, not how to avoid one.

Severity: defect, not blocking or misleading. The labels are reachable by scrolling the sheet, ticks stay on their true pixels, `data-scrolls` is honestly "false", and `down` is one press away. No on-screen string promises otherwise — the button says "Draw the whole approach across the page", which it does. The only untrue "nothing to scroll past it, because the whole approach is in frame" is a source comment (~line 6445), not a surface claim. But it is the default rendering at one of the two commonest laptop widths and it cuts words in half at first paint, which is well below the bar.

The locked constraint says these are "present, reachable, in the tab order, and say plainly that they are not here yet", and "on a phone the capsule and the dock are the same object". Separately the account tile is 32×32 in the phone rail and 30×30 in the Notes phone dock, where every neighbouring tile is 44×44 and the shell declares `--tap: 44px`.

REFUTED on the fix, not on the observation — and with two measurement errors that matter for a seat named "Measured evidence".

What I confirmed by driving at 390 with hasTouch (chromium, `?v=paper&state=…`):
- `.railMark` is `display:none` at ≤720 (_gate-suite.html:454). `inbox` and `help` are NOT `display:none` as claimed — they compute to `display:grid` and are zeroed because their parent `.railUtil` is `display:none` (line 456). Same visible outcome, wrong statement of the code.

So the Notes phone dock is Notes/Tasks/Timeline + avatar. That half is accurate.
- The shell `.railAvatar` is 32×32 at 390 with a coarse pointer and there is no shell-level `pointer: coarse` block anywhere — its neighbours measure 44×44 and the shell declares `--tap: 44px` (line 207). Real, and gate-blind: audit.mjs:389 floors targets at 28, not 44, so it passes green. This half is a genuine defect.
- But the Notes dock avatar is not 30×30 as a target. `[data-app="notes"] .dockAvatar::before` gives it a measured 30w × 44h union under coarse (lines 3966–3980), which is the union convention this file's own audit measures from. The finding measured the drawn box and reported it as the target.

Why the fix is refuted rather than sharpened-and-confirmed:
1. "the same overflow the dock already uses for Notes' verbs" — no such overflow exists. The dock shows search/voice/photo/keep inline and solves 372px by dropping `more` from the suite list and, at ≤380, deleting the decorative `.dockRule` (line 3878). There is nothing to hang closed doors behind.
2. "state them once in the account sheet's place" — there is no account sheet; the account tile is itself a not-yet door, and building one is out of scope.
3. "Bring both avatars to 44×44 under pointer: coarse" would regress a paid-for fix. Lines 3962–3965 record explicitly that a 44px min-height on the round 36px and 30px dock controls "drew them as ellipses in a row of squares", and that the target grows underneath instead. A drawn 44px circle also adds 14px to a foot that already had to delete its divider to fit at 380 — the same nine-pixel overlap that once silently swallowed a save.

Severity: defect, not misleading. Dropping secondary tiles on a phone is ordinary compaction and nothing untrue is stated to the operator — the lock's "present, reachable, in the tab order" is a desk-width description that the phone quietly narrows. The 32px account target is the part that is visibly wrong and passable.

The thing the finding pointed at but did not find: because the doors are removed by CSS and not by the renderer, they poison the spine's roving tabindex on a phone. The arrow handler (line 7951) enumerates every `.rail [data-rail]`, hidden ones included. Driven at 390 on tasks.board, ArrowRight from `tasks` reaches `timeline` and then stops dead — the next press sets `railCurrent = "inbox"`, moves `tabIndex = 0` onto the hidden inbox button, and `next.focus()` silently fails. `add` and `me` are unreachable by arrow, and the next Tab skips the capsule entirely (it landed on a `late` chip in the head). The round notes advertise "left/right at ≤720"; at ≤720 it walks two steps and evicts itself from the tab order. That is a separate finding and it is closer to blocking.

refuted.problem: With the content column at 1440, each index row sets the note's own words as a single line ending wherever it ends, then right-aligns the status pill at a fixed x 1510. Measured across the first eight rows the white between the last word and the pill is 123, 227, 103, 304, 259, 20, 24 and 303px — a 284px swing inside one list. refuted.why:
The gap numbers reproduce exactly (I measured 123, 227, 103, 304, 259, 20, 24, 303 at 1920 for the first eight rows), but the reading of them is wrong on three counts, and the fix is worse than the condition.

(1) Nothing "right-aligns the pill at a fixed x". `.idxRow` is `grid-template-columns: 20px minmax(0,1fr) 76px 92px` with `.idxTag { justify-self: start }` — the pill is LEFT-aligned at the head of its own fixed column, and `.idxWhen` is right-aligned to a second fixed vertical (measured: tagL constant 1510, whenR constant 1691 at every row). A left-aligned, ragged-right scan line sitting beside a fixed metadata column produces exactly this variance. That white is the rag of the sentence, not a layout defect; it is already "the text's own", which is what the finding asks for. Every list in the named benchmarks (Linear's issue rows, Stripe's ledger, Vercel's deployments) works this way.

(2) The character figures are simply wrong against the source. I measured `.idxText` at 1920: 155, 143, 155, 128, 138, 170, 166, 136 characters, not 106; at 1280: 130, 129, 124, 128, 132, 130, 120, 136, not 84. The measure is longer than the finding claims, so the one defensible half of this — that a ~1146px, ~165-character single line at 1920 is past any measure — is stated with numbers that do not survive checking.

(3) The proposed fix reintroduces a documented, paid-for defect. The row's own comment records why the metadata columns are fixed: "the right-hand verticals hold down the whole index instead of stepping in and out with the length of each timestamp." Putting the pill "at a fixed distance from the end of the text" makes its x float per row, which (a) destroys the vertical the eye uses to compare In Tasks / Kept / To decide down a ten-row list, and (b) strands a moving pill between a fixed left edge and a still-fixed `.idxWhen`, which is the worst of the three options. One soft rag in a person's own prose is replaced by a hard rag in repeated furniture.

The 80-character number is also wrong against the ratified surfaces. The index already runs 120–136 characters at 1280 on a sheet that is pixel-frozen against its own lab master; an 80-character cap bites at 1280 and 1440 and breaks that fidelity assertion, not just the 1920 frame. And `--stack` carries an explicit argument for the opposite: "What --stack actually governs is the INDEX, whose rows are scan lines rather than prose, and every pixel of width there is another few words of a person's own note visible before the ellipsis." Disagreeing with that is legitimate; disagreeing with it without engaging it, on wrong numbers, is not.

Severity is overstated by implication. Only one of ten rows even reaches its ellipsis at 1920, which means the index is showing nearly the whole note — a real composition question about whether a preview that is no longer a preview weakens the reason to open a note. But nothing is misread, nothing is misasserted, and nothing is unusable. This is refinement at most, and the version of it worth carrying is a different finding than the one filed.

refuted.problem: The foundation `:root` ships four off-palette hues — `--status-done: #10b981`, `--status-flight: #f59e0b`, `--status-blocked: #ef4444`, `--x-status-done: #1b873f` (plus `--x-status-done-tint: #eaf5ee`) — and a third weight, `--weight-medium: 500`, into a file whose lock is four colours and two weights. Grepped: `var(--x-status-done)` 0 references, `var(--accent-tint)` 0, `var(--accent-glow)` 0, `var(--accent-soft)` 0, `var(--accent-hover)` 0, `var(--weight-medium)` 0, `--indigo-50…500/800/900` 0, `--paper-soft`/`--paper-deep` 0, `--radius-md`/`--radius-lg` 0. `--status-next` resolves to the file's only surviving `--ink-faint` reference and is itself unused. The palette gate passes because it measures painted colour; the source still declares the thing the lock forbids, with a comment ("the Tasks board's own Done green… kept as an --x- extension exactly as the product does") describing a use that no longer exists.
refuted.why:
The greps are accurate — I re-ran them. `var(--x-status-done)`, `var(--x-status-done-tint)`, `var(--accent-tint)`, `var(--accent-glow)`, `var(--accent-soft)`, `var(--accent-hover)`, `var(--weight-medium)`, `var(--paper-soft)`, `var(--paper-deep)`, `var(--radius-md)`, `var(--radius-lg)`, `var(--status-done|flight|blocked|next)` are all 0 in _gate-suite.html. So the observation is right. Three things sink the finding as written.

(1) The proposed fix's second branch is factually false about the file. "Move the whole vendored `:root` behind a comment saying it is inert" would install a lying comment: that block is the opposite of inert. `var(--ink…)` resolves 44 times, `var(--paper…)` 17, `var(--accent)` 8, `var(--font-mono)` 8, `var(--font-sans)` 3, plus `--weight-regular`, `--ease-out`, `--ease-in-out`, `--motion-fast`. The whole document is painted out of that block.

(2) The first branch is far larger than the finding's own inventory admits and self-defeating. It is not four hues and a weight — `--space-1` through `--space-12`, `--radius-sm/md/lg/pill`, `--shadow-float`, `--shadow-modal`, `--hairline`, `--hairline-soft`, `--ink-soft`, `--ink-ghost`, `--indigo-100/200/300/400/500/800/900`, `--motion-instant/base/slow` and `--weight-semibold` are all 0 too. "Delete every declaration with zero references" guts roughly 85% of the ladder and leaves a dozen-token stub. The block's own header declares it "the vendored Signal Design System 2.0 values from src/ds/tokens.css, unedited" — a token file carrying its system's full ladder is what a token file is for, and gutting it makes that header comment false, which is the exact defect class the finding is invoking.

(3) The severity framing overstates. "The source still declares the thing the lock forbids" is not what the lock says: the palette lock governs painted colour and hierarchy, which is why the audit measures composited paint. An unpainted declaration in a vendored DS file is not a palette breach; nothing reaches Orla, no gate is fooled, and the only downstream consequence is at port time, which `references/handover.md` governs and this engagement excludes. Refinement, not defect.

What survives, and it is small: the `--x-status-done` / `--x-status-done-tint` pair at src/foundation.css:97–98 is NOT vendored — it sits below the vendored ladder as a declared extension, and its comment ("kept as an --x- extension exactly as the product does") asserts a live use this file has zero references to. That is lessons.md:342 verbatim — a dead value with a credible comment. Two lines and a comment, not a block rewrite.

Also: the element pointer is at generated output. build.mjs's header says master.html is generated from src/ and "is never hand-edited"; _gate-suite.html is a wrap of that. The editable source is src/foundation.css:24–99.

rounds.notes: selfInflicted 0.48 — thirteen of the twenty-seven confirmed findings sit on work built since the last panel, which there had never been: the horizontal Timeline, the space changes and the suite composition itself are all new surface. The three that matter most (the spine's keys, the seam's leak, the two wedding days) are all composition defects rather than product defects — none of them exists in any of the three frozen labs.

seatsSat: UX and information design — Orla, venue manager at The Orchard
rounds.headline: Two of three seats independently found the same blocking defect: Tasks' Planning drawer covered a fifth of the board and reserved no layout, so DONE was 100% covered at every desk width and the arrow keys walked the focus ring in behind an opaque panel. The cause was the composition, not the drawer — the lab had already fixed this and said so in a comment that is still there; scoping the product under its app compound turned the lab's root element into a demanded descendant, and five rules matched nothing from the day the document was composed. A selector that matches nothing fails nothing, which is why no gate saw it. Three more findings were one hole: focus moved and the board did not follow it. And the URL contract had never written once, because a const at the top level of one product's script shadowed window.history for the whole document.

confirmed.seat: UX and information design — Orla, venue manager at The Orchard
confirmed.element: Tasks · the Planning drawer over .board, at 1440 and 1920
confirmed.problem: Planning opens as a 388px overlay, not as reserved layout. Measured at 1440: board.scrollWidth === board.clientWidth === 1322, so the scroller has no travel; the drawer occupies x 1034–1422; the DONE tray sits at x 1148–1406 and is therefore 258 of 258px covered, with 114px of WAITING under it too — including WAITING's count '0' (x 1129–1137) and the tail of its description, cut mid-word at 'a deliver'. At 1920 it is the same shape: DONE 354 of 354px covered, maxScroll 0. Scrolling cannot recover any of it. Nothing says so: the live region announces only 'Planning open.' The covered trays are neither inert nor aria-hidden — ArrowRight from the first card walks the rover onto a Done card at x=1161, entirely behind the opaque panel, and Enter there announces 'Showing the whole note.' while nothing on screen changes. Share, Planning, More and Filter remain tab stops underneath the panel. The drawer survives a spine round trip to Notes and back, and the return announcement is 'Tasks. 5 of 13 done.' with no mention that a lane is buried. Both entry points are in the head: the 'Planning' button and '5 with no day' (title: 'Open Planning to see the 5 tasks with no day').
confirmed.consequence: Orla opens Planning from the head to give five undated tasks a day, and a fifth of her board — everything finished — silently ceases to exist, along with the count on Waiting and half its sentence. There is no scrollbar, no fade, no sentence, and no way back except closing the panel she is trying to work in. If she is scheduling by keyboard, the arrow keys carry her focus ring in behind an opaque white panel and the product starts narrating content she cannot see.
confirmed.fix: When Planning is open, reserve its width in layout rather than painting over the board: narrow the board's scroller by the drawer width (388 at ≥1024) so board.scrollWidth > board.clientWidth and every tray including DONE stays reachable by the board's own horizontal scroll, and move the head's right-hand controls (Share, Planning, More, Filter) inside the narrowed head. At ≤768 the drawer already takes the whole sheet, which is correct; leave that branch alone.
confirmed.assertion: With Planning open at 1440 and 1920: for every tray in .board there exists a scrollLeft reachable from the board's own scroller at which the tray's rect lies entirely left of the drawer's left edge; and no focusable element outside the drawer has a bounding rect intersecting the drawer's rect. Watch it fail against the current build first.
confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED, and the cause is worse than the seat knew: the fix for this is already written in the source and is dead code.

Driven in Chromium at `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board`, clicking `[data-act="planning"]`:

- 1440: `.sheet` computed `margin-right: 0px`; sheet 100–1422, drawer 1034–1422, board `scrollWidth === clientWidth === 1322`, maxScroll 0. Trays: todo 116–374, doing 374–632, review 632–890, waiting 890–1148, done 1148–1406. DONE is 258 of 258px covered, WAITING loses 114px. The screenshot confirms it visually: WAITING's description is guillotined mid-word at "a deliver", its count is gone, and DONE is not on screen at all.
- 1920: same shape — board 1802/1802, maxScroll 0, done 1532–1886 inside a drawer at 1514–1902.
- Live region: only "Planning open." `.tray[data-lane="done"]` has `inert === false`, no `aria-hidden`, 20 tabbables. ArrowRight from the first card: doing → review → **done card at x=1161, behind the opaque panel**, and it stops there; Enter announces "Showing the whole note." with nothing visible changing.
- Share (x 1180), Planning (1260) and More (1357) are all under the panel with `tabIndex 0`.
- Spine round trip Tasks→Notes→Tasks: drawer still open, announcement "Tasks. 5 of 13 done.", board still 1322/1322.

ROOT CAUSE, which raises this above the seat's own framing. `src/tasks.css:1071/1079/1086` (and the breakpoint overrides at 1683/1718) already do exactly what the seat asks:

    [data-app="tasks"] .floor:has(.drawer) .sheet { margin-right: calc(388px + var(--inset)); }
    [data-app="tasks"] .floor:has(.drawer) .board { grid-auto-flow: column; grid-auto-columns: minmax(258px,1fr); scroll-snap-type: x proximity; }

with a comment that names this exact failure as already fixed: "Before this the drawer was white on white with no edge: it sliced the Waiting column mid-word and erased Done entirely, which read as the board breaking rather than a panel opening."

The selector matches nothing. The DOM is `.floor#deck > div[data-app="tasks"] > (.sheet, .drawer)` — `.floor` is the **ancestor** of `[data-app="tasks"]`, not a descendant. Measured: `document.querySelectorAll('[data-app="tasks"] .floor').length === 0`, while `.floor:has(.drawer).length === 1`. All five rules are inert. This is precisely the class of defect this engagement exists to find: a fix that held when Tasks was a standalone sheet and died when the three products were mounted under one floor.

Not a gate restatement — `interaction-check.mjs` has zero assertions containing "planning" or "drawer". Not on the closed list. Not taste.

Blocking, not defect: a whole lane is 100% occluded with maxScroll 0 so no scroll can recover it, and the keyboard rover walks focus onto an element behind an opaque surface and announces a state change the operator cannot see. Escape does close the drawer, so the operator is not trapped — but "the product will not do what it says" is met twice over.

The proposed fix is refuted only on its numbers, not its direction, so I am confirming and correcting in sharpenedFix: the breakpoints are 1200 and 900 in this source, not the 1024 and 768 the seat cites, and narrowing `.board` rather than `.sheet` forces a second edit for the head controls that the shipping intent gets for free.
confirmed.sharpenedFix:
Do not write new layout — repair the selector that already carries it.

1. In `src/tasks.css` change all five occurrences of `[data-app="tasks"] .floor:has(.drawer)` (lines 1071, 1079, 1086, 1683, 1718) to `[data-app="tasks"]:has(.drawer)`, and mirror into `_gate-suite.html` (1551, 1559, 1566, 2163, 2198) and `_gate-tasks.html`. One token per rule, no new numbers. Because it narrows the *sheet*, the head narrows with it and Share / Planning / More / Filter land inside the narrowed head automatically — the seat's separate "move the head's right-hand controls" edit is unnecessary and would fight the stacked-head rule.

2. Keep the breakpoints the source actually has, not the ones the finding names: 388px base, 364px at ≤1200 (`margin-right: calc(364px + var(--inset))`), and `margin-right: 0` with a full-bleed drawer (`left: var(--inset); width: auto`) at **≤900**, not ≤768. The ≤720 phone branch is already correct; leave it.

3. Then close the two halves the finding measured but did not fix. With the board a real scroller, the rover must bring an off-screen tray into view: ArrowRight onto a Done card currently lands at x=1161 without scrolling, which after this change means landing off-screen instead of behind glass. Add the scroll-into-view the carry already does. And say it: "Planning open." should carry the consequence ("Planning open. The board scrolls.") and the spine return should not announce "Tasks. 5 of 13 done." as if the drawer were not there.

The comment at line 1567 anticipates this ("Opening the drawer takes the sheet under 1200, so the header stacks") but it has never actually executed, so the stacked head in the planning state has never been seen. confirmed.element: src/timeline.js:841 (`place()` dispatch), :718 `placeAcross()`, :943–961 (the sentence writer), `.b-gapNote` in `header.b-horizon`
confirmed.problem: The horizon's gap sentence never recomputes in the `across` orientation — which is the default, the one every shipped frame shows, and the one the ACROSS pill is pressed on. `place()` computes `atRest = gapSentence(items[0].getAttribute("data-date"))` at line 955, but line 841 reads `if (measureEl.getAttribute("data-across") === "true") return placeAcross(measureEl);` and returns before ever reaching it; `placeAcross()` never writes `.b-gapNote`. Driven at 1440 on `?v=paper&state=timeline.owner-flight`, three ways: (a) open the nearest moment (Menu tasting, Sat 1 Aug) and press +7 three times → sentence still "Nothing is planned until 1 August." while the moment now reads Sat 22 Aug; (b) press +1 once → still "1 August" while the moment reads Sun 2 Aug; (c) delete the moment outright → the moment is gone from the measure and the sentence still says "Nothing is planned until 1 August." It survives a scroll of the sheet and a viewport resize. The identical sequence at `&layout=down` returns the correct "Nothing is planned until 8 August." every time. The code's own comment at lines 945–948 states this exact failure — "it went on naming a date that now holds nothing, which is a plain falsehood rather than a stale phrasing" — as something already guarded against; the guard it describes only covers `items.length === 0`.
confirmed.consequence: Orla moves or cancels the next thing in the season and the first sentence on the horizon goes on telling her nothing is planned until a date that now holds nothing — sitting two inches above an undo bar reading "Menu tasting at The Orchard moved 7 days later" and a measure whose first node is a different day. The one product whose stated job is making the distance legible states a false fact about it, in its default orientation, and keeps stating it through every repaint.
confirmed.fix: Lift the sentence writer out of `place()`'s down-branch into a `writeGap(measureEl)` helper and call it from both branches: in `place()` before the `placeAcross` dispatch at line 841, and at the tail of `placeAcross()` after its own rows settle. It must read the nearest UPCOMING row rather than DOM position — sort the live rows by `data-away` and take the smallest positive — so a moment pushed past its neighbours does not leave itself as `items[0]`.
confirmed.assertion: For `&layout=across` and `&layout=down` alike on `?state=timeline.owner-flight`: after opening the nearest moment's editor and pressing `[data-delta="7"]` three times then Done, `.b-gapNote` reads "Nothing is planned until 8 August."; after instead deleting that moment, `.b-gapNote` reads "Nothing is planned until 8 August."; after deleting every upcoming moment, it reads "Nothing is planned yet." Both orientations return identical strings for identical edits.
confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED — every code citation is exact and all three driven sequences reproduce verbatim.

CODE, verified line by line in `src/timeline.js`: `place()` opens at 836; line 841 is exactly `if (measureEl.getAttribute("data-across") === "true") return placeAcross(measureEl);`. The sentence writer sits at 943–961, after the down-branch's own placement loop, and computes `gapSentence(items[0].getAttribute("data-date"))` at 956. `placeAcross()` (718–840) never touches `.b-gapNote` and never sets `field.__gapAtRest`. The only other writer, `speak()` at 2016–2062, short-circuits when `.b-stick` is not `position: sticky` and repaints `root.__gapAtRest` — which in a session that has never been placed down is `undefined`, so it returns and leaves whatever the initial `horizon()` render put there. So the node has no live writer in `across` at all.

DRIVEN, chromium, 1440×960, `?v=paper&state=timeline.owner-flight` (no `layout` param — `data-layout` reads `across`, `[data-layout-to="across"]` is `aria-pressed="true"`, `.b-gapNote` is `display:block`, 457px wide, `.b-stick` computes `static`):
- baseline: note "Nothing is planned until 1 August.", rows 08-01@16 … 10-03@79.
- open Menu tasting, +7 ×3 → row is `2026-08-22@37`; note still "Nothing is planned until 1 August."
- +1 ×1 → row `2026-08-02@17`; note still "1 August."
- Delete this moment → row gone, nearest is 08-08; note still "1 August."
- It survives `.b-plan` scrollTop 400 + window scroll, and a resize to 1280×900.
The identical sequences at `&layout=down` return "8 August.", "2 August.", "8 August." — correct every time. Guest `timeline.desk` is also `across` by default and carries the same node.

This is the sentence whose whole job is to state the empty run, on the default orientation, on the head of the sheet, naming a date that after the delete holds nothing and misreports three weeks of runway as one. The code's own comment at 945–948 calls that "a plain falsehood"; the guard it describes only covers `items.length === 0` and only in the branch `across` never reaches. Not a gate restatement (no `gapNote` assertion exists in `gate.mjs`, `verify.mjs` or `interaction-check.mjs`), not on the open or refuted lists, no constraint touched. Misleading, not defect: the product asserts a fact about its own plan that is false.

The fix is right in substance — in particular the insistence on reading nearest-by-`data-away` rather than `items[0]` is load-bearing, not decoration: `placeAcross()` deliberately never reparents, so after +7 ×3 the DOM order I read back was `08-22, 08-08, 08-22, …` and a DOM-position reader would have written "22 August", a second falsehood. I sharpen the mechanics only (see sharpenedFix), so this is a CONFIRM.
confirmed.sharpenedFix:
One writer, one call site, and a rail guard.

1. Lift 943–961 into `function writeGap(measureEl)` and call it ONCE at the top of `place()`, immediately after the `if (!measureEl) return;` and BEFORE the `placeAcross` dispatch at 841. Then delete the block from the down branch entirely — do not also call it from the tail of `placeAcross()`, as the finding proposes. Two call sites re-open the "ONE WRITER" invariant the 950–954 comment was written to protect, and buy nothing: the sentence depends on `data-away`/`data-date`, not on where placement puts the pixels, so it is correct before either instrument runs.

2. Inside `writeGap`, take the live rows, `Number(el.getAttribute("data-away"))`, keep `> 0`, take the minimum, and read that row's `data-date`; fall back to `"Nothing is planned yet."` when the filtered set is empty. Keep `field.__gapAtRest = atRest` and the `__gapSpeak()` / `textContent` tail exactly as they are — the scrolled reading in `across` (static `.b-stick`) then paints the fresh at-rest string through the same door.

3. Guard the back rail: `if (measureEl.getAttribute("data-back") === "true") return;` as the first line of `writeGap`. `backMeasure()` (1103–1127) builds `.b-measure.b-back` with negative `data-away`, and `behindBlock({owner:true})` renders it inside the SAME `.b-field` as the horizon (2248). `settle` places every measure in the document (2955). Without the guard, a plan with a past would place the back rail second, find no positive `away`, and clobber a true sentence with "Nothing is planned yet." The current fixture has no past moments at the clock — I confirmed one `.b-measure` and zero `.b-back` in owner-flight, desk and phone — so this is latent today and lethal the day the fixture grows one.
confirmed.breaks:
Plausible breakage, and what to re-measure.

1. The scrolled reading. Moving the writer above the dispatch means it now runs on EVERY across repaint, where before it ran on none — and `__gapSpeak()` fires `speak()` plus an rAF `speak()`. At desk-down widths `.b-stick` is sticky and `speak()` names the nearest row below the pane edge, so the risk is the round-1 class "a repaint snaps the line back to the top of a plan the owner is not looking at". Re-measure: `timeline.desk` and `timeline.owner-flight` at 1440 and 1920, `&layout=down`, scroll `.b-plan` past two rows, then press +1 and resize — the note must keep the "Sat 8 Aug · in 23 days" scrolled form, not revert to "Nothing is planned until…".

2. The `items.length === 0` sentence. Changing the source from `items[0]` to min-positive changes what an all-past or all-today plan says. Re-measure: delete every moment in both orientations (the case 945–948 was written for) — must read "Nothing is planned yet.", not a stale date and not a blank.

3. Timing on first paint in across. `writeGap` now runs before `placeAcross` has set `--across-*`; it reads attributes only, so no layout dependency, but the fonts.ready re-place and the `settle` loop at 2955 both re-enter it. Re-measure: zero console errors across all eight states, and the note's text identical before and after `document.fonts.ready` in `across`.

4. Frame reproducibility. `.b-gapNote` is in `paper-timeline.owner-flight` and `paper-timeline.desk` at 1920 and in the 390/768/1280/1440 timeline shots; the at-rest string is unchanged at t=0, so the frames should be byte-identical. Re-shoot and diff — if any timeline shot moves, the writer is running at a different moment than the old one did.

5. Both gates. `node gate.mjs` and `node verify.mjs` (216 assertions) must stay green; nothing here touches palette, weight, target or motion, so a red is a signal the repaint order moved, not a threshold. Add one assertion per orientation asserting the sentence tracks the nearest upcoming row after a +7 and after a delete — the absence of exactly that assertion is why this shipped.

confirmed.element: src/tasks.js:1269–1279 (the board scroll before the flight), :2598–2622 (`restore()` — vertical `.trayBody` scroll only), `.tick`
confirmed.problem: Completing a card moves focus with it into the Done lane, and below 1280 the board does not follow. `restore()` calls `aim.focus({ preventScroll: true })` and then scrolls only the card's own `.trayBody` vertically; the horizontal branch at :1269 deliberately declines to scroll where origin and Done cannot both be on screen, which its comment at :1262–1268 argues for on animation grounds — but nothing then reconsiders where focus was put. Driven keyboard-only (Tab to the first To-do card's tick, Enter): at 1000×844 focus lands on "Mark not done" at x = 1172 in a 1000-wide viewport, `inView: false`, `board.scrollLeft` still 0 (board clientWidth 882, scrollWidth 1322). Same at 768 (x = 1160) and 390 (x = 1242, board clientWidth 372 of 1520). At 1280 the board scrolls 144px and focus stays inside the viewport, so the correct behaviour exists and simply stops below that width — the 1000–1279 band the paid-for library names as the place to look first.
confirmed.consequence: A keyboard user completing a task at any laptop window narrower than 1280 loses the caret entirely: the focus ring is a thousand pixels off the right edge of a board that did not move, the next Tab continues from a column they cannot see, and Space would untick a card that is not on screen. It is the surface's most frequent action, and it is the one place the board's otherwise exemplary restore-and-announce discipline drops the person's place.
confirmed.fix: After the flight settles, make `restore()` decide focus consistently with the scroll decision it already made. Where the board did scroll (both columns fit), keep the current behaviour. Where it deliberately did not, do not send focus across the board either: put it on the next card in the origin lane, or on that lane's `.trayAdd` when the lane is now empty, and let the existing announcement ("… done. Press Ctrl Z to undo.") carry where the card went. Alternatively clamp: if the element about to be focused lies outside the board's client box, set `board.scrollLeft` to the smallest value that brings it in.
confirmed.assertion: At 390, 768, 1000, 1280 and 1440 on `?v=paper&state=tasks.board`, after Tabbing to the first card's `.tick` and pressing Enter, `document.activeElement.getBoundingClientRect()` lies entirely within the `.board` element's own bounding box (left ≥ board.left and right ≤ board.right) at every one of the five widths.
confirmed.verdict:

CONFIRMED, and understated. It does not change the conclusion, and role="application" on .board independently suppresses any native arrow-key scrolling, so "not a keyboard scroll region either" is right.

Two things make it worse than the seat reports. (1) The fade. .sheet[data-more-right]::after is a 96px white gradient at right:0 — x=1166 to 1262 — and data-more-right is true. Of the 101px of the focused card still inside the scroller, 96 sit under a gradient that reaches opaque white at the edge. The screenshot shows the focus ring cut off and the card reading "Open da... couples..." washed out. It is not 57% hidden, it is effectively invisible. (2) Narrow widths, which the finding never tested. At 768 the SECOND ArrowRight lands at 633-866 against a board ending at 756, and the third at 1149-1382 — 393px wholly past the right edge. At 390 the second ArrowRight lands at 633-907 against a board ending at 381: entirely off-screen from the second press, and the third 850px away. scrollLeft 0 throughout both. At 390/768 the rover is the ONLY keyboard route into columns 2-5, so four of five columns can be focused and never seen.

The asymmetry is already argued inside the file. restorePlace (~10837) keeps the focused card fully inside .trayBody vertically, with a comment saying the scoping to the column is deliberate. fly() (~9502-9509) already scrolls .board horizontally so a completing card flies somewhere that exists — "at 1280 only 114px of Done was inside the scroller." The author already holds that the board must scroll to a destination; ordinary focus movement is the single path that never got it. WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) is Level AA and is failed outright; neither gate inspects it, so this is exactly the class of defect the panel exists to catch.

Severity raised from the seat's framing to blocking: below 1360px the board's own aria-label — "Task board, arrow keys to move between tasks" — moves focus onto an object the operator cannot see, and on a phone that happens on the second press. That is the advertised model not doing what it says.

The PROPOSED FIX is confirmed only in its parenthetical. The headline lever, a bare scrollIntoView, is the option the source explicitly rejects at line 10837 on measured grounds ("a general scrollIntoView nudges the horizontally snapped board on a phone and undoes the restore above") and it would also walk the sheet's vertical ancestors. confirmed.sharpenedFix:
Add a horizontal keep to restorePlace(target, kept), beside the existing vertical .trayBody keep — never a bare scrollIntoView.

1. Scope it to .board by hand, using the same arithmetic fly() already uses at ~9509 so the two paths agree: with box = board.getBoundingClientRect() and card = node.getBoundingClientRect(), if card.right > right-inset then board.scrollLeft = Math.min(board.scrollLeft + (card.right - rightInset), board.scrollWidth - board.clientWidth); if card.left < box.left + 8 then board.scrollLeft = Math.max(0, board.scrollLeft - ((box.left + 8) - card.left)).

2. rightInset is NOT box.right - 8. Whenever data-more-right is set the sheet paints a 96px white ::after over the board's last 96px, so stopping at the scroller edge leaves the card under the gradient — measured at 1280, 96 of the 101 visible px. Use box.right - 96 - 8, or equivalently scroll far enough that data-more-right clears. Symmetrically on the left against the 96px ::before.

3. Ordering: run it inside restorePlace's existing snap-suspended window — after board.scrollLeft = kept.left and before the requestAnimationFrame that restores scrollSnapType — or the `x mandatory` snap at <=720 (line 2227) pulls it straight back. This is the same trap the vertical keep already documents for .trayBody.

4. Make it a no-op while a flight is in progress. fly() writes board.scrollLeft itself; two writers on one scrollLeft in the same frame is how the phone-tick regression ("every tick on a phone threw the operator back to To Do") got in the first time.

5. Guard it on kept/refocus the way the vertical keep is, so a pointer-driven repaint does not yank the board away from where the operator scrolled it by hand.

1. The phone/tablet snap restore. restorePlace suspends scroll-snap-type for exactly one frame because `x mandatory` at <=720 re-snaps to column 1; a second scrollLeft write in or after that window is the same shape as the bug that comment was written to fix. DRIVEN, chromium, 1440x960, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=timeline.owner-flight`.

The bar's reading order is, all non-ignored: StaticText "The Orchard, events" → StaticText "Mara & Finn" → StaticText "ONE OF THREE" → button "Add a moment" → button "Preview" → button "Get the link", inside a region named "The plan for Mara & Finn". And the parity claim is itself half wrong: the rail doors carry `aria-disabled` + a `title` sentence because they are `<button>`s; the `inert()` helper the fix invokes emits a bare `span.b-inert` with NO `aria-disabled` at all (line 16064, and its two live uses at 17261 "Nothing to preview yet" and 17547 "Sending comes next"). It carried the same border colour, radius and height band as .b-act and sat beside three real buttons drawn identically, so the bar read as four controls of which one was dead... Stripped of the chrome it reads as what it is: the place, then the project, then the actions." The dead-door reading was found and removed on purpose. A class name is invisible to Orla.

4. The fix's noun is factually wrong. There are three PROJECTS, not three timelines: `SIBLINGS` (7430) holds Nora & Cian and Aisling & Tom beside Mara & Finn, and `CLIENTS` (8322) is that same set of three couples — the suite already names all three by name in Tasks, where cards are tagged "Nora & Cian" and "Aisling & Tom". The product's word for the object is "plan": `field()` renders aria-label "The plan for Mara & Finn", and the empty-owner copy reads "Everything on this plan is measured from it" — a string a prior round deliberately changed off "page" as the last one calling the object something else. "Timelines" would be a fourth name for it and, inside the Timeline product whose sheet head reads `timeline.` at 17/600, would read as three copies of the app.

5. "Switching is not here yet" disclaims a feature the surface never offers. No project switcher exists anywhere in the suite (no `data-act` for it in the file). Announcing an absence where nothing was promised re-installs, in words, the dead-control reading that #3 removed in pixels.

6. The fix's markup destroys the project name. `bar(projectName, actions)` puts `projectName` inside `.b-switch` as its first child; `inert(label)` returns a single span with one text string. Rendered as written, "Mara & Finn" leaves the bar entirely — or, if kept, moves from 15px Geist 600 `--fore` into `.b-inert`'s 11px Geist Mono uppercase `--fore-62`, collapsing the bar's place → project → actions hierarchy into one flat mono line.

Scope: also note the element exists in exactly one of the eight ratified states. `.b-switch` count is 1 in timeline.owner-flight and 0 in timeline.desk and timeline.phone — there is no `.b-bar` on the guest surfaces at all.

Severity correction: the residue — a bare positional index without its noun — is at most a `refinement`, not a defect, and certainly not the "no door" framing filed here.

refuted.problem: REGRESSION of the closed r1 finding `spine-arrows-hijacked-on-notes`, at ≤720 only. At desk width Notes uses the suite's `.rail`; at ≤720 the rail is `display:none` and Notes paints its own three suite tiles into the dock with `data-act="suite-notes|tasks|timeline"` and no `data-rail`. app.js's spine handler selects `.rail [data-rail]`, so it never sees them; notes.js:3415 declines the keys only for `e.target.closest(".rail")`, so it never declines them. Driven in chromium at 390, 700 and 720 on `?v=paper&state=notes.notebook`, standing on the "Tasks" spine tile: ArrowRight → focus unchanged; ArrowLeft → focus unchanged; ArrowDown → `BUTTON.idxRow` (second note in the index); Home → first index row; End → last index row. The same walk at 768 and 1440 on Notes, and at 390/700/720/768/1440 on Tasks and Timeline, is correct. The spine is also three tab stops at ≤720 in Notes (no tabindex management on the dock tiles) against one in Tasks and Timeline. And shell.css:216, whose comment says it exists "so the same tile would [not] answer the keyboard differently depending on which sheet was open", cannot reach the dock tiles: measured computed outline at 390 is `rgb(255,255,255) 2px off=3px, radius 10px` in Notes against `rgb(79,70,229) 2px off=2px, radius 12px` in Tasks and Timeline. verify.mjs asserts only "notes @390 · the capsule stands down 0 tiles" and never tests the object that replaced it, which is why 48 spine assertions pass over this.
refuted.why:
REFUTED ON THE FIX ONLY. The problem is real, I reproduced every measurement, and it is blocking-class — do not discard it; re-file it with the sharpened fix below.

WHAT CHECKS OUT. Driven in chromium at `?v=paper&state=notes.notebook`, standing on the dock's "Tasks" tile, at 390, 700 and 720, identically at all three: ArrowRight → focus unchanged; ArrowLeft → focus unchanged; ArrowDown → `BUTTON.idxRow` "Mara & Finn's menu tasting…"; Home → `BUTTON.idxRow` "Saturday wedding, Mara & Finn…"; End → `BUTTON.idxRow` "Photographer recommendation from the Hen…". The same walk at 768 and 1440 on Notes, and at 390 and 720 on Tasks and at 390 on Timeline, walks the rail correctly. Tab stops: `dockTiles=3, dockTabindex0=3` at ≤720 in Notes against `rail tabindex0=1` everywhere else. Rings, keyboard-driven with `:focus-visible` confirmed true on the element: notes@390 `solid 2px rgb(255,255,255) off=3px r=10px`; tasks@390 `solid 2px rgb(79,70,229) off=2px r=12px` — the seat's numbers exactly. The code reads as described: notes.js:1617 calls `railTiles({tight:true})`, which emits `data-act="suite-*"` with no `data-rail` and outside any `.rail`; shell.css:307 sets `#deck[data-product="notes"] .rail{display:none}`; app.js:416/420 select `.rail [data-rail]`; notes.js:3415 declines only `closest(".rail")`. The gate gap is real, though mis-cited — "the capsule stands down" lives in tools/spine.mjs:51, not verify.mjs, and verify.mjs *does* test the dock tiles exist and are real doors (`suiteInDock >= 3`, click → `data-product` becomes tasks). What nothing tests is their keyboard, which is the seat's actual point.

WHY THE FIX IS REFUTED — all three parts are inert or destructive as written.

(1) Part 3 is empirically a no-op. I injected `.rail button:focus-visible, .rail [tabindex]:focus-visible, [data-rail]:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--indigo); outline-offset: 2px; }` verbatim, put `data-rail="tasks"` on the dock tile, and keyboard-focused it: the ring stayed `solid 2px rgb(255,255,255) off=3px r=10px`, unchanged. `[data-rail]:focus-visible` is (0,2,0); it loses to notes.css:194-199 `[data-app="notes"] button:focus-visible` (0,2,1) and to notes.css:1623 `[data-app="notes"] .dock :focus-visible` (0,3,0). "One ring serves the object at every width" is false. And winning would be worse: I measured the dock's ground as `rgb(17,17,17)`, and indigo #4f46e5 on ink is about 2.3:1 — which is precisely why notes.css:1623 puts a white ring there. The ring difference is a correct answer to a different ground, not the defect the seat reads it as.

(2) Part 1 as literally written breaks the dock. "inside a container app.js's selector reaches" means a `.rail` ancestor, because app.js:416/420 select `.rail [data-rail]` — and shell.css:307 hides `#deck[data-product="notes"] .rail` outright at ≤720, so nesting the dock's group in a `.rail` deletes the suite tiles at the only width they exist. The selector must be widened, not the markup nested.

(3) Part 1's "cleaner" alternative re-opens a closed finding. `railHtml()` emits railMark, home/inbox/help and `railAvatar`; the dock already carries `dockAvatar` with its own honest-door sentence (notes.js:1617-ish). Rendering the suite's nav into the dock slot puts two account tiles in one 372px dock — closed r1 `two-account-tiles-one-honest`, verbatim.

(4) "let railHtml()'s stop() set the roving tabindex on them" cannot reach. railHtml() builds the nav; the dock is rebuilt by notes.js's own paint() on every keystroke in `.phoneField`, and `window.__SUITE` exposes no read of `railCurrent`. Any tabindex app.js writes is thrown away on the next character typed — the same mechanism as closed r1 `spine-tabstop-lost-to-railadd`.

(5) Part 2 is correct in spirit but inert alone: `closest(".rail, [data-rail]")` matches nothing on today's source, because no dock tile carries `data-rail`. It only works after (1) lands, and (1) as written does not land.

SEVERITY. Blocking, and I am raising it, not correcting it down. The brief advertises "Arrows walk it (down/up at desk, left/right at ≤720)" and "The suite tiles live in the dock at ≤720"; the architecture locks "on a phone the capsule and the dock are the same object". At ≤720 in Notes the arrows do not walk it, and ArrowDown/Home/End throw focus out of the capsule into the note index — the exact failure mode of closed r1 `spine-arrows-hijacked-on-notes`, at the one width that fix's `.rail` guard could never cover.

refuted.problem: The crossing is one act with one undo, owned by Notes — but `open-task` deliberately carries the person to Tasks, and Tasks then denies that undo exists. Driven at 1440: `?state=notes.seam` → `[data-act="send"]` (card count 13 → 14, receipt appears) → `[data-act="open-task"]` (product switches, focus lands on the new card, `#say` reads "Opened in Tasks. Your note stayed in Notes.") → `Ctrl+Z` → `#say` reads "Nothing left to undo." and the card count stays 14. Pressing the notes rail tile and `Ctrl+Z` there reads "Taken back. Nothing went to Tasks." and the count returns to 13. So the crossing is reversible by the very chord Tasks just said had nothing to reverse, one tile away, with the Notes undo bar still live and still printing `Ctrl Z`.
refuted.why:
REFUTED ON THE FIX ONLY — the problem is real, reproduces verbatim, and must not be discarded. Every observed fact checks out. Driven in chromium at 1440x960 against `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=notes.seam`: `.card` count 13 → 14 on `[data-act="send"]`; `#say` "Sent to Tasks. Your note stayed here. In The house."; the Notes strip reads "Sent to Tasks. Undo Ctrl Z for 30 seconds"; `[data-act="open-task"]` switches `__SUITE.current()` to `tasks`, focus lands on `ARTICLE.card`, `#say` "Opened in Tasks. Your note stayed in Notes."; Ctrl+Z → "Nothing left to undo.", count stays 14; the notes rail tile then Ctrl+Z → "Taken back. Nothing went to Tasks.", count 13. The mechanism is confirmed in source: `TASKS_API.add` (src/tasks.js:405) never calls `arm()`, so a seam card is never on `history`, and `undoLast` (src/tasks.js:1586) refuses. The file's own doctrine agrees with the seat — src/app.js:311 says "A crossing is one act with two halves, so it has one undo." Tasks denying that undo exists, inside a suite that insists it is one application, is an untrue claim: misleading, not defect.

BUT BOTH HALVES OF THE FIX MAKE THE WORK WORSE, so the finding as filed is refuted.

(1) "call the seam's `uncross` for it" produces a HALF-UNDONE seam. `uncross` (src/app.js:343) only does `api.remove(id)` and `delete crossings[noteId]`. The Notes half — `Object.assign(note, before)`, `CROSSED.shift()`, `sentTask = null`, `decided.pop()` — lives in the closure passed to `offerUndo` (src/notes.js:1092 and :1135) and is unreachable from Tasks. I drove exactly what the fix instructs: `window.__SUITE.uncross({id:"n14"})` returned true, cards went 14 → 13, and back in Notes the note STILL carried its "Open in Tasks" receipt; pressing it announced "That task is not on this board." The fix trades one false sentence for a broken door and a ledger that records a crossing to nowhere. That is strictly worse than today.

(2) The trigger is unbounded in time and destructive. `crossings` is a plain map that is only ever emptied by `uncross` — nothing expires it, unlike Notes' 30-second `undoTimer` (src/notes.js:306, `UNDO_SECONDS = 30`). "if `window.__SUITE` holds a live crossing for a card currently on the board" stays true for the whole session. So: cross, move a card, Ctrl+Z (undoes the move), Ctrl+Z again — and under this fix the second press silently deletes a card that crossed twenty minutes ago, announcing a seam sentence about an act nobody just performed. An undo that reaches past its own stack boundary and eats an old object is the worst class of failure in this file, and the fix has no ordering rule for multiple crossings either.

(3) The fallback string is a fresh lie. `?state=tasks.board`, no crossing anywhere, Ctrl+Z → "Nothing left to undo." That is the same code path. Replacing it with "Undo for that crossing is in Notes" tells a person on a cold board about a crossing that does not exist.

refuted.problem: Pick a card up (Space on .card → "Picked up Confirm marquee sides with the hire company."), walk it one lane (ArrowRight → "In progress, position 1 of 4."), then click the Notes tile on the spine and come back to Tasks. The carry is never resolved. The card is still aria-grabbed="true" with data-force="moving", still painted in the held treatment (indigo 1.5px ring, transform: scale(1.02)), and still armed — but focus is on main.sheet, and the only thing announced on return is "Tasks. 5 of 13 done." Focus that card again and ArrowRight moves it to Review ("Review, position 1 of 3.") instead of walking the rover to the next card; Escape then reverts it all the way back to To do with "Move cancelled… is back in the to do column", undoing a move the person watched land before they left.
refuted.why:
REFUTED ON THE FIX, NOT THE PROBLEM. The observation reproduces verbatim — do not discard it — but the proposed fix would ship a false instruction, and its stated alternative is unimplementable as written and more destructive than the finding claims.

DRIVEN (chromium, 1440x960, ?v=paper&state=tasks.board), in order: focus demo-t-01 -> Space -> "Picked up Confirm marquee sides with the hire company." -> ArrowRight -> "In progress, position 1 of 4." -> click .rail [data-rail="notes"] -> "Notes. 14 notes.", activeElement MAIN.sheet, card still aria-grabbed="true" data-force="moving" -> click [data-rail="tasks"] -> say = "Tasks. 5 of 13 done.", activeElement MAIN.sheet, held card force=moving, transform matrix(1.02,...), box-shadow rgb(79,70,229) 0 0 0 1.5px. Re-focus, ArrowRight -> "Review, position 1 of 3." Escape -> "Move cancelled. Confirm marquee sides with the hire company is back in the to do column." Every number and every sentence in the finding is exact. The cause is structural: the pointerdown handler that already ends a carry lives on window.__SUITE.host("tasks") (src/tasks.js:2711), and the spine sits outside it, so the one law tasks.js states in its own comment at endCarry — "The hand ends where the operator's attention goes" — is enforced for four vectors (pointer off the card, the composer, the Planning drawer, the tick) and not for the fifth.

WHY THE FIX IS REFUTED.

1. It names the wrong key. The proposed sentence says "Enter to drop it here". Enter does not drop. Driven: Space, then Enter -> "Showing the whole note.", carry still live (aria-grabbed still true). Space drops (tasks.js:1881-1899); the foot pill footPill() already prints the true vocabulary, "arrows move / Space drop / Esc cancel". Shipping this sentence puts an instruction into the spoken channel that does nothing — the exact failure endCarry's own comment names ("a foot pill printing instructions that no longer worked").

2. It throws away the arrival line. The replacement announcement never says "Tasks", so a person who just pressed a spine tile is no longer told which product they landed on. go() composes LABEL + summary for a reason.

3. The alternative half cannot be built as specified. "Dropping the carry at the point the spine is used ... must announce the drop" — but say() writes textContent on one shared #say region (app.js:181-196), and go() calls say(LABEL + ". " + summary) synchronously in the same tick. A drop sentence emitted before that is overwritten and never read. As stated, the alternative announces nothing.

4. The two options are not "equally acceptable" — the drop is the worse one. A completed keyboard carry records no undo entry: driven, Space -> ArrowRight -> Space gives "Confirm marquee sides ... dropped in the in progress column.", then Ctrl+Z gives "Nothing left to undo." So force-dropping at the spine converts a live, Escape-reversible carry into an irreversible move. The finding's own harm ("undoing a move the person watched land") is real, but its preferred remedy strands the opposite harm.

5. One material omission in the framing. "Returning armed, unfocused and silent" is true only of the spoken channel. Measured on return: the foot pill is still rendered at top=826 reading "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company | arrows move | Space drop | Esc cancel", and the held card is in view at 195..334 with its ring. The board's declared "only statement of what it is currently doing" is present and correct, so a sighted keyboard user is not left guessing. The real, unguarded case is narrower than stated: the arrival announcement omits the modal state, and focus lands on the sheet instead of the thing in hand.

SEVERITY. Defect, not blocking or misleading. No advertised affordance fails — the arrows move the card because a carry genuinely is live, and aria-grabbed="true" is exposed on the card for anyone who navigates to it. Nothing untrue is asserted. What is wrong is that the suite's most stateful moment survives a product switch without a word.

refuted.problem: .readBody is labelled "The note. Pick the words that should become the task, with the arrow keys." and the handler above it deliberately claims ArrowRight/ArrowLeft/ArrowUp/ArrowDown, Home/End, Enter, Space and PageUp/PageDown while it holds focus — its comment says "while it holds focus the arrows belong to it and not to the pile behind it". The two vim aliases for those same arrows are not in that guard. Driven: focus .readBody, pick five words with Shift+ArrowRight ("5 words picked. Use these words to make them a task."), then press k. Focus is torn off the note onto .idxRow in the index below and the live region announces "1 of 14. Saturday wedding, Mara & Finn." — while the desk above still shows the pick bar reading "5 words picked. Send to Tasks will use exactly these." j does the same downward, announcing note 2 of 14. The index's own handler treats j and k as ArrowDown/ArrowUp, and k additionally means "keep" in the review hand, so one unmodified letter carries three meanings across the product.
refuted.why:
REFUTED ON THE FIX, NOT ON THE PROBLEM — the fix as written kills a keycap that is drawn on screen.

WHAT I REPRODUCED (chromium, 1440x960, _gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=notes.notebook, click .idxRow to lift a note, focus .readBody):
- 5x Shift+ArrowRight → live region "27 words picked. Use these words to make them a task.", .pickCount reads "27 words picked.", 3 .pick marks.
- press k → document.activeElement becomes .idxRow ("Saturday wedding, Mara & Finn…"), live region "1 of 14. Saturday wedding, Mara & Finn.", while the desk above still shows the pick bar ("27 words picked." + "Send to Tasks will use exactly these.") and the 3 marks survive.
- press j → .idxRow, "2 of 14. Mara & Finn's menu tasting…".
So the mechanism is exactly as described: src/notes.js:3628 scopes the body guard to arrows, Home/End, Enter, Space, PageUp/PageDown; j/k fall past `if (typing) return;` (3674) to 3725/3728 → moveCursor(±1), which sets refocus = {kind:"row", id:cursorId} (3363) and say()s the index count. Two of the finding's details are loose: Shift+ArrowRight extends by SENTENCE not by word, so five presses is 27 words, not "5 words"; and k has two meanings today, not three (the third is the leak itself).

WHY THE FIX IS WRONG. It says explicitly: "while document.activeElement matches .readBody, .handBody, route j to moveSentence(1) and k to moveSentence(-1)". The onBody branch at 3628 runs BEFORE the review-decide branch at 3682 and returns. In the review hand, .handBody is the focused element by construction (refocus = {kind:"act", sel:".handBody"} at 3290, and the guard at 3711 refocuses it). I drove it: entering review via [data-act="review"] leaves focus on .handBody, and k there currently fires decide("keep") — "Kept in Notes. 7 left. Next, …", card advances to 2 of 8. Line 2278 draws that key on screen: `Just keep it<kbd>K</kbd>`. Under the proposed fix, K on the card becomes moveSentence(-1) and returns, so the printed keycap for the hand's Keep decision goes dead. That converts a defect-class leak into a misleading-class lie about a visible keycap — the fix makes the work worse. Nothing in interaction-check.mjs asserts j, k, or keep (I grepped), so the regression would ship with all 216 assertions green.

SEVERITY. The seat's implied class is right at defect, not higher: the body advertises "with the arrow keys" and the arrows all work; the pick and its bar survive the tear intact, so nothing is lost and nothing untrue is asserted. It is a real hole — the file already names and fixed this exact class one plane over (3705-3711: "the hand owns these keys while it is up; if focus has drifted, they bring it back to the card rather than moving anything") and the notebook body is the unpatched instance — but it is passable, not blocking.

rounds.notes: Three rotating seats, not seven — the closing round is the full panel. refuteRate 0.50, down from 0.61, on a third the seats. selfInflicted 0.14 against round 1's 0.48: round 1's remediation did not manufacture round 2's findings, with one exception, and that exception was a stale comment rather than behaviour. The two blocking drawer findings are one defect found twice, which is the blind panel working as designed. Every confirmed finding closed with an assertion written first and watched failing; two of those assertions were themselves wrong on the first run (a node held across a repaint measures 0x0, and an ASCII space does not match the non-breaking space the horizon binds a date with) and were corrected before being trusted.
